  refunds each paid joiner from what is left of their payment after earlier
  refunds, and refunds can never add up to more than the organiser paid. A
  refund Stripe accepts as pending and later fails is noticed by the payments
  cron and owed again, retried once Stripe has forgotten the failed attempt. Groups the organiser settled by Internet Banking are
  unchanged.
  Treasurers can list joiner payments whose refunded figure is not backed by a
  Stripe refund with `pnpm run payments:audit-organiser-child-refunds`; it is
  read-only.

  A refund to the organiser that only succeeds on a retry now leaves a
  `booking.payment.refund_recovered` record in the audit log (category
  `booking`, so the audit-category distribution moves by one booking writer;
  no member-facing change).
- **A booker can now use their guests' promo codes, and several codes at
  once (#3492, epic #3813).** On the booking review step, the booking edit
  panel and Admin → Book on Behalf, each guest member's assigned promo codes
  appear as chips grouped under that guest's name and marked "applies to
  *name* only", beside the booker's own. Nothing is applied until the booker
  presses a chip or types a code. With the **Several promo codes on one
  booking** module on, the booker can apply more than one code and use
  **Move earlier** / **Move later** to set their order - where two codes could
  cover the same night, the earlier one does - and the summary shows one line
  per code. With the module on, a working-bee discount also combines with
  codes on the review step, covering its own nights first. With the module
  off, a booking still takes one code and a working bee still stands alone.

  Only a family guest's codes, or those of a guest from outside the family whom
  the booking treats as confirmed (they or a delegate accepted, the club only
  notifies, an officer added them, or the booking predates guest consent), are
  ever offered; a pending or declined guest never shows a chip. A code only its
  own member may book with (a "booker picks guests" or group fixed-nightly
  assignment) is never offered as a guest's chip. The booker sees only each
  code and what it gives.
  Every lookup is recorded in the audit log as `promo_code.guest_lookup`
  (category privacy) and is limited to 30 a quarter-hour per member.
- **Several codes on one booking now work with this release's other money changes.** A cancellation after a bank-transfer edit refund gives back the right amount of account credit. A guest's acceptance that lowers an organiser-paid group booking refunds the organiser's card. If that card can't take the full amount, the acceptance still goes through and nothing changes. (#3829)
- **Net Collected no longer counts an unpaid bank-transfer booking as money received** (#3372, the owner's review on #3811). When a booking paid by bank transfer was edited down before it was paid, Xero's credit note could mark its payment as partly refunded, and every Net Collected figure (the dashboard card, the Payments tile, Reports and the Finance dashboard) then counted most of the booking's price as collected. A partly or fully refunded payment now counts only when there is a record of the money actually arriving, or it was a card payment, so these unpaid bookings add nothing. Card payments, and bank transfers that were paid and later partly refunded, count exactly as before.
- **The booking ledger now records a group organiser's payment on each joiner's
  booking (#3854).** When an organiser settles a whole group in one card payment
  or one combined internet-banking invoice, each joiner's booking is now
  confirmed on the ledger and records its own share of that payment, anchored
  on the group's settlement. A group cancellation records the refund it plans
  for each joiner and what the club keeps - less any edit refund the club
  has promised to send back by bank transfer, so that money is not counted
  twice - and a refund to the organiser's card
  for one joiner (an edit's reduction or a cancellation) is recorded against
  that joiner, and taken back off if Stripe later fails it. Nothing anyone sees
  changes yet: every screen, email and report still reads the existing figures.
  This is the groundwork for moving those readers onto the ledger (#3584)
  without showing a group joiner's booking as unpaid. The booking-ledger
  back-post (#3583) now records the same for groups settled before this
  release - each joiner's share, and for a cancelled group its planned refund
  and what the club kept - so a joiner it covers is no longer only listed; a
  joiner it cannot explain is listed with the reason, and the cut-over census
  now keeps the gate shut on such a joiner rather than listing it as covered
  (a refund the card retries have given up on, or shares that do not add up).
  The census also counts a card refund that failed but will be retried as
  still in flight, and accepts a joiner's share when the organiser's whole
  payment was refunded. A database change adds
  one value to the ledger's list of anchors; it is safe to run while the
  previous version is still serving.

  **Deploy note:** finish the switch to the new version before processing any
  group organiser's cancellation. If the previous version cancels a joiner the
  new version has already settled, that joiner's ledger is left wrong (the
  census reports it, and an officer corrects it by hand).
- **A card refund Stripe gave up on can now be closed as "Paid another way" (#3372).** When the club refunds a card and every retry fails, the refund stays in Refunds owed and keeps coming off Net Collected until it is settled. If the treasurer pays the member back another way, for example by bank transfer, they close it under **Card refunds Stripe gave up on** on the Stuck States page. Seeing the list needs Finance view access, and closing a refund needs Finance edit.

  The dialog asks the treasurer to choose **Paid back in full** or **Paid back part of it - the rest will no longer be owed**; it never guesses from the amount. In full, the amount is what is still owed. In part, the treasurer types an amount below that, and the dialog says in dollars how much will stop being owed. A part payment is final: the rest is no longer owed anywhere, and a later refund on the booking pays only its own share. A note saying how the member was paid back is always required. A refund that replaces a superseded payment can only be closed in full.

  Closing it records the amount as refunded on the payment and in the booking's ledger, takes the refund out of Refunds owed, and writes an audit entry saying whether it was paid in full or in part. Stripe is not asked again. Every kind of card refund now gets a Xero refund credit note for exactly the amount paid back, worded as a bank transfer and dated the day it was closed, as long as there is a Xero invoice to credit. A late card charge - one taken after its booking was cancelled, which the treasurer chose to refund - is credited against its own record in Xero, never the booking's invoice. If Xero has no record of the charge yet, closing the refund first records it, as an invoice for the whole charge paid into the Stripe account on the day Stripe took it, and the bank-transfer refund credit note follows once that record is in Xero, naming it. If the charge's record is already on its way to Xero as a booking change's invoice, the note follows that invoice instead, and no second record is made; if that invoice has failed, the dialog and the message say to retry it from the Xero operations list rather than "on its way", and retrying it sends the note too. If a record fails before reaching Xero, the close puts it back to run, and the Xero repair tool retries it; one that failed after it may have reached Xero - the charge's own record or a booking change's invoice - is left for an officer to check in Xero first, so Xero never gets two: retry it if it is not there. If it is there but the app has not linked it, mark it resolved and record the refund by hand. If the app already linked it, mark it resolved first, before recording anything by hand, and do not record by hand what was paid back another way, because the app raises that note through the nightly credit check or the repair tool. Record by hand any part Stripe refunded to the card, because the app raises no card note once the record is resolved: the retry's message names both amounts, counting only card notes already in Xero, and with nothing (or $0.00) paid back another way it still says to record any card refund by hand. A card note that may be in Xero - the app tried to send it and cannot tell whether Xero took it - is named separately, by the message and by the repair tool: check Xero for it, and record that part by hand only if Xero does not have it. A card note Xero refused is counted as never sent, and one an officer retried from Xero Operations counts once it is in Xero, even while the original still shows as failed. If the charge still has another invoice in Xero, or one on its way there, the app notes its card refunds against that one, and the message says not to record them by hand: any not yet noted are noted the next time the app notes the charge. The dialog, the message and the audit entry say exactly that instead of reporting it queued, and a booking change's invoice already linked in Xero cannot be retried at all. Only a late charge's change invoice is retried by sending it again in the background; an ordinary card change's invoice is retried as before. If only the note fails, the record stays in Xero and the note is retried with **Retry in background** in Xero Operations; the nightly credit check queues a note that was never queued, and the repair tool queues a note that never followed its record. If an officer records the charge in Xero by hand before the app sends it, the repair tool names what was refunded to the card, less any note already in Xero for it, plus what was paid back another way, to record by hand. Whenever else the charge's record was marked resolved - the app's own invoice in Xero, a booking change's invoice resolved before it was sent, or once a note for the close exists - the repair tool names the card refunds to record by hand on their own. It names each charge once at most, and a kept charge's invoice resolved while still linked in Xero, whose refunds the app notes itself, is not named at all. Both are report-only and keep appearing after the refund is recorded by hand, which is expected: the app cannot see a refund recorded by hand in Xero. The repair tool no longer asks for a refund to be recorded by hand when the app raises its note. Each close's note is for exactly what it paid back, however much other notes on the payment already cover, and a note retried after a crash is never raised twice in Xero. When the last refund on a list is closed or resolved, the list stays on the page saying it is empty, so keyboard focus is not lost. Xero then shows the money into the Stripe account and the money out of the bank, and the charge nets to nil. The dialog says before you close what will be recorded in Xero, and the message afterwards says what was queued. The nightly credit check no longer raises a card note, settled from the Stripe account, for money that went back by bank, even while that money's own bank-transfer note has failed - and a genuine card refund on the same payment is still asked for in full.

  A refund whose last retry failed with a timeout, a network or Stripe server error, or Stripe saying the money was already refunded is flagged "Stripe may have refunded: check the Stripe dashboard first". If Stripe did refund it after all and the refund reaches the app after the close, the payment now shows under a new **Card refunds paid back twice** list on the Stuck States page, so the treasurer can recover the extra money. Once it is sorted out with the member, the treasurer marks the row **Resolved** with a note saying how (Finance edit). The note goes in the audit log and the row leaves the list; nothing is refunded, charged or sent to Xero. If Stripe refunds the card again while the dialog is open, the dialog says so, and a Resolved against an amount the treasurer did not see is refused. If the list changes while the dialog is open, the dialog follows it: it closes if the refund is no longer waiting, and resets the amount and says so if what is owed changed. If what is owed changes just as the treasurer closes it, the close is refused and the list refreshes, so a full or part answer is never applied to a figure nobody saw. A refund with nothing left owed is no longer offered for a $0.00 close.
- **Refunds owed and Net Collected now agree to the cent for every payment (#3372).** A card refund that has sent part of the money now owes only the part still to send. A later, unrelated refund on the same card charge no longer makes an older stuck refund look smaller. If an approved refund request's card refund fails partway, only the unsent part is retried. Refunds owed now reads, payment by payment, exactly what Net Collected took off. Before, a payment owing both a refund by hand and a card refund could show more in Refunds owed than the payment ever held.
- **Refunds owed now includes old group cancellation card refunds as one club-wide amount (#3372).** Before #3653, a group cancellation was refunded as one card refund that belongs to no single booking. If that refund is still unpaid, what it still has to send now counts in Refunds owed as one amount for the whole club. It is not counted against any booking or in Net Collected. A refund owed by hand on a payment that never showed money taken also counts in Refunds owed now.
- **A card refund that fails partway is retried only for what it has not sent (#3372).** If Stripe refunded a slice but the app could not record it, the retry now replays that slice and records Stripe's original refund. Before, it could ask again for slices already recorded. A closed card refund no longer takes a later refund as its own, so a still-open refund is no longer shown as owing more than it does.
- **Net Collected now takes off a refund still owed on a live booking straight away (#3372).** When a paid booking is edited down and the refund is to be paid back by hand, or an approved refund request is to be paid back by hand, Net Collected used to keep counting that money until the treasurer marked it paid back. It now comes off as soon as it is owed, as a cancelled booking's already did: $200.00 paid and edited down by $50.00 shows $150.00. The dashboard card's breakdown line now says "owed back by hand" rather than "owed back on cancellation".
- **Card refunds Stripe has not yet paid, and late card charges waiting for the treasurer, now come off Net Collected too (#3372).** A card refund the club has started that is still pending, processing, or failed and waiting for a retry now comes off straight away, and so does a late card charge on a cancelled booking until the treasurer decides to keep it. On a cancelled booking, a bank transfer that arrived after the cancel and was credited to the member's account no longer counts as kept either. The dashboard card's breakdown line names each of these when it is not zero.
- **"Refunds owed" and "Credits owed" now sit beside every Net Collected figure (#3372).** They show on the dashboard card, the Payments page, Reports (and its CSV) and the Finance dashboard. **Refunds owed** is every refund owed and not yet paid: refunds promised back by hand, card refunds Stripe has not yet paid, and late card charges waiting for the treasurer's refund-or-keep decision. **Credits owed** is all the account credit members hold and have not yet used. Both are as at today and across the whole club, so the page's dates, lodge and filters do not change them, and each amount comes off Net Collected only for its own booking. A refund leaves the figure when it is paid, dismissed or kept, and credit leaves it when it is spent on a booking. On a phone, the two figures stack under the dashboard card's title.
- **A cancelled booking's "Non-refundable amount retained" no longer counts a refund the club still owes (#3372).** On the booking page's Cancellation Outcome, a cancelled booking paid by hand whose refund is still an open task for an officer used to show the whole unrefunded payment as retained. The refund owed now comes off straight away, as it already does in Net Collected, and the line says so: for example "$30.00 (after $60.00 still being paid back by hand)". The line now always matches what Net Collected counts in cash for that booking. The "retained amount" in the booking page's messages follows the same figure. A card refund Stripe has not yet paid, a late card charge waiting for the treasurer, and a late bank transfer credited to the member come off the line the same way. Bookings with nothing still owed back show exactly what they did before.
- **Stripe setup's Webhook step can now be verified on a live-only club.** It
  used to tick only from a Stripe *test-mode* event. Stripe's dashboard no longer
  sends those to a live endpoint, so the step stayed amber ("Skipped for now")
  even while live webhooks were arriving and passing their signature check. Any
  signature-verified event, live or test, now verifies it. The hint now
  describes Stripe's current flow: in Workbench → Webhooks (Developers →
  Webhooks), select the endpoint and a recent delivery and click **Resend** -
  or, if it has none yet, make a payment (a test payment in test mode) - then
  click **Re-check verification**. Changing the signing secret still clears the tick until an
  event verified under the new secret arrives.
- **Stripe library upgraded to stripe-node 23 (#4029).** Payments now use Stripe
  API version `2026-09-30.endive` (was `2026-08-26.dahlia`). No change to what
  members or officers see: none of the SDK's breaking changes touch fields this
  app uses. Webhook events keep arriving at the version set on the club's
  Stripe webhook endpoint; leave that setting alone in the same deploy. The
  webhook signature age limit (300 seconds) is now passed explicitly and tested
  against the real library, so a future upgrade cannot quietly loosen it. After
  deploying, a test-mode payment, saved-card charge and refund on staging is a
  sensible smoke check.
- **The booking page and the payment step now agree on what is owed
  (#3991).** While the club is checking the money for a change a member made,
  the summary at the top of the booking page shows the amount still to pay.
  It used to show the booking's price on its own, leaving out any change fee an
  officer had recorded and any account credit already applied. It now shows
  what is actually owed: the price plus any recorded change fee, less applied
  credit. That is the same figure the card payment and the emailed payment link
  charge. When credit covers everything, it says there is nothing left to pay
  and names no amount.

  A guest on someone else's booking is no longer told about the owner's
  account credit. The summary names no credit, including on a cancelled
  booking, where "$X was added to your account credit" is dropped and only what
  was retained is said. The booking's history leaves out the "Saved account
  credit was not applied" entry and any "Credit Choice Updated" change, and
  shows a cancellation only as "This booking was cancelled.". That cancellation
  entry's stored wording is free text that can name the credit, so a guest no
  longer sees any of it, including a cancellation reason. A cancelled
  booking's outcome leaves out its "Held as account credit" and "Previously
  applied credit restored" lines and shows "Settled on Cancellation" instead
  of "Credit Issued". That matches the credit-choice notice and pay-card
  credit row they already did not see. The owner, admins, and officers who
  can view bookings (read-only ones included) see everything as before. An
  officer without bookings access can open someone else's booking only as a
  guest on it, and sees what any guest sees. The price, what was paid, what went back to the card and what was
  retained stay visible to the guest, so they can still work the credit out
  by subtraction.

  The page's pay card, and the `{amountDue}` wording in the club's booking
  messages, now take the applied credit from the same record as the payment
  step, so all three agree. Nothing about what is charged changes.
- **An organiser's cancel of a group paid by Internet Banking now asks an
  officer to repay the organiser (#4042).** The cancel already recorded each
  joiner's refund in the app's ledger, and each joiner's email says the club
  will repay the organiser directly, but nothing asked anyone to send the
  money. The cancel now raises one task in **Money to settle** on the payments
  board, on the organiser's booking, holding every joiner refund the ledger
  shows for the group and listing the shares. Admins get the **Manual refund
  needed** email after the cancel has worked through the joiners, worded for a
  group (the cash-booking wording is unchanged); one that could not go out is
  sent on a later run. Re-running the cancel
  adds nothing twice. Marking the task paid back records only that the money
  went, sends nothing to Xero, and is refused if the total has grown since the
  page loaded; the task cannot be dismissed, and an officer who would not
  repay is sent to the treasurer. The task counts in **Refunds owed** but in
  no booking's Net Collected. When the group's paid Xero invoice cannot be
  voided, that alert now points to the task and says how to credit the
  invoice, instead of naming the invoice's paid total. The "Manual refund
  needed" message gains five tokens - `{{handBackNote}}`, `{{handBackLabel}}`
  (both now required), `{{handBackHeading}}`, `{{handBackRecipientLabel}}` and
  `{{handBackAmountLabel}}`; a club that customised it keeps its own wording
  until it adds them.
- **Approving a refund appeal on a group joiner's booking that the organiser
  paid for by card now actually refunds it (#3956).** When a group organiser
  paid for everyone in one card payment and a joiner then appealed, approving
  the appeal refunded nothing, yet still queued a Xero refund credit note for
  the full amount and told the joiner their refund was on its way.

  The approved amount is now refunded out of the organiser's card payment,
  back to the card the organiser paid with. It is retried automatically if the
  card provider does not answer straight away. The Xero refund credit note is
  queued only once the refund has gone through. The joiner is told the refund
  went (or is on its way) to the organiser's card. The organiser gets a new
  email, **Group Organiser Joiner Refund**, saying the amount for that joiner's
  share is being refunded to their card. The admin's choice not to email covers
  both.

  The most you can approve is what the organiser's payment can still return
  for that booking. Approving more is refused with a message naming how much
  can still be refunded, or saying to decline the appeal when nothing is left.
  The review screen and the joiner's appeal form now show that same figure,
  with a line saying it is refunded to the organiser's card. While an older
  group cancellation's own refund to that card is still being retried,
  approval is refused until it has been made.
- **A price increase whose card request was lost on the way back from Stripe is
  now still asked of the member (#4036).** When a paid booking's price goes up,
  the club asks the member's card for the extra. If Stripe accepted that request
  but its reply never arrived, the automatic retry used to send a slightly
  different request under the same reference, which Stripe refuses, so every
  retry failed and the member was never asked. The retry now sends exactly the
  request the edit sent, and Stripe hands back the card request it already made.
  If Stripe still refuses, the retry finds that request itself: one unpaid
  request for this booking and amount that the club has not recorded. If it
  finds none, more than one, or one that another change to the booking could
  own, it records nothing, keeps retrying, and alerts an administrator as
  before. A school's booking with no saved card customer
  now gets its request when the change is saved, instead of only on the retry.
  Nothing needs doing.
- **A bank-transfer booking now records the money its Xero invoice actually
  collected** (#3979). When Xero shows a booking's invoice paid, the app records
  what the invoice took, so a booking whose price (or a change fee) changed
  before its invoice was raised is no longer settled at its old price, and its
  refunds and account credit are worked out from what was really paid. A credit
  note that lowers an invoice nobody has paid yet (*Invoice correction -
  nothing refunded*) is now a price correction, not a refund: a $300 invoice cut
  by $100 and paid $200 shows $200 paid and nothing refunded. When the app
  cannot be sure the payment belongs to the booking alone, or the member paid
  more or less than the booking owes, admins with finance edit access get a
  **Bank transfer amount needs checking** email, which cannot be switched off,
  and a note appears on the booking's history. Bookings settled before this
  change are not rewritten: after upgrading, whoever runs the club's booking
  system should run the settled-cash audit described in the Internet Banking
  guide, which lists any that need correcting.
- **Bank-transfer settlement follow-ups (#4095).** A bank transfer whose invoice
  carried an *Invoice correction* note is no longer reported as a "mixed
  invoice" when its booking is cancelled for capacity. When the settle keeps a
  payment's stored figure, an invoice correction already synced is now counted
  as refunded in the same step that records the payment, so the payment's net
  matches the cash, even for a cancellation waiting on that step, instead of
  waiting for another note. A credit-note sync that loses its refunded-total
  recount twice to a concurrent writer now fails its stored event, which is
  retried, instead of leaving the total uncounted. The inbound invoice sync
  clears its overpayment and prepayment count once Xero lists none, and the
  settled-cash audit says when an invoice was last synced before that count was
  recorded. The triage of all thirteen items is in
  [`docs/reviews/2026-10-26-4095-triage.md`](docs/reviews/2026-10-26-4095-triage.md).
- **A card refund the card provider refuses on a booking change or a
  cancellation is no longer lost (#4083, #4096).** When a booking change
  lowered the price of a booking paid by card, or a cancellation refunded the
  card, and the card provider answered the refund straight away as failed or
  cancelled (rather than with an error), nothing was retried and the
  treasurer's **Refunds owed** did not show it - a cancellation's refund was
  even marked as paid - so the member might never get the money. Now the
  refused amount stays owed: it counts in **Refunds owed**, the officers are
  emailed once for the refusal (and again if the retries run out), and it is
  retried automatically, each retry a fresh request so
  the provider does not just repeat its refusal. If the retries run out it is
  listed for the treasurer to close as paid another way, as any other card
  refund that could not be made is. This covers changing dates, removing a
  guest, a combined edit, a re-price after a guest accepts, and a
  cancellation. Other refunds that can be refused this way (a late card
  charge's, a reviewed change's, a refund request's and a few automatic ones)
  are tracked in #4103 and #4102.
- **Account credit is now used in the same order every time (#4013).** When a
  member's account credit is applied to a booking, the system uses their
  oldest credit first. Two pieces of credit recorded at exactly the same moment
  could previously be used in either order, so the same booking could
  sometimes use an existing Xero credit note and sometimes create a new one.
  Credit recorded at the same moment is now always used in the same fixed
  order. No amounts change.

  One case now stops instead of guessing: when a retry of an interrupted
  allocation would no longer keep what its earlier attempt recorded (for
  example one interrupted across this upgrade, or one whose credit was partly
  handed back in between), the Xero operation fails with a message naming the
  booking, and nothing is allocated twice. If credit was handed back, retry it
  once that hand-back has gone through; if the booking's credit notes in Xero
  genuinely disagree with its allocations, resolve the operation in Xero.
- **A card refund that follows a guest's acceptance lowering a booking's price
  now recovers if the first attempt is interrupted (#4101).** When a guest
  accepting their place re-prices a paid booking down, the club refunds the
  difference to the card. If that refund was interrupted after the card
  provider had already made it (a timeout, for example), the background retry
  sent a slightly different request under the same reference, the provider
  refused it, and the retry never finished, leaving an officer to reconcile by
  hand a refund that had in fact been made. The retry now sends exactly the
  original request, so it picks up the refund already made and records it. This
  never refunds a member twice. The other refund retries were checked and
  already matched their original requests.

  For operators: a retry that had already given up before this release stays
  stuck. Stripe did make that refund, so check the Stripe dashboard and do not
  pay the member again. The **Card refunds Stripe gave up on** list now marks
  such a row **Stripe may have refunded**.
- **A refund request's card refund that the card provider refuses is no longer
  lost (#4102).** When an officer approved a refund request and the card
  provider answered the refund straight away as failed or cancelled (rather
  than with an error), nothing was retried and the treasurer's **Refunds owed**
  did not show it. If a refund was split across two card payments, a refused
  part was also dropped when a later part then failed. Now the refused amount
  stays owed: it counts in **Refunds owed**, the officers are emailed once for
  each refused part (and again if the retries run out), and it is retried
  automatically, each retry a fresh request so the provider does not just
  repeat its refusal. A part the provider did refund is never asked for again,
  and is never counted as owed by this or any other refund. If the retry could
  not be queued after the card provider was asked, the approval now stands,
  rather than the request going back for a second approval that could refund
  the same money twice: the officers are emailed, and the refund appeals screen
  says, which part the provider refused (refund it another way) and which got
  no answer (it may have gone back, so check the payment with the card
  provider first). A refund the card provider records later clears it there. The refund appeals screen says what an approved refund still owes -
  queued for retry, out of retries, not queued, or by bank transfer (a
  dismissed transfer counts as not refunded) - and its
  **Refunded** figure is what was actually refunded.
- **A card cancellation whose card refund cannot cover the whole refund now
  records the rest, and tells the member honestly (#4097).** A cancellation
  refunds to the card only what the card refund carries: what the payment's
  card charges can still give back. When that was less than the refund the
  cancellation policy gives, usually because the payment's records disagree,
  the difference was only written to the server log: nothing recorded it, and
  the member's email and the cancel confirmation said the whole refund had
  been made. Now the cancellation records the rest on the payments board,
  counted in "Refunds owed", and admins are emailed once. The part the
  payment's other (non-card) charges hold is to be refunded by bank transfer,
  and the member is told so. Anything beyond that - the payment's records show
  it already refunded, or nothing holds it - is a task to check before paying,
  and the member is told only that the club will be in touch about it. The
  booking page says where each part stands. The card refund's booking history
  and its Xero refund credit note are for what the card refund carries.
  Marking a part paid back raises one Xero refund credit note for exactly that
  amount, worded as a bank transfer.

  For treasurers: pay the bank-transfer part by bank transfer and mark it paid
  back once the card part of the refund has gone through (until then the app
  refuses it). For the part to check, look at Stripe and the bank first, and
  dismiss it with a note if the member was refunded.
- **A card refund the card provider accepted and later reported as failed is
  now owed again (#4104).** The card provider can accept a refund and fail it
  days later, for example when the member's card has been closed. The app
  counted such a refund as paid, so for a cancellation, a booking change or an
  approved refund request the member was never paid back and **Refunds owed**
  did not show it. Now the failed refund is taken back out of what was
  refunded, shows under **Refunds owed** once, the officers are emailed, and it
  is asked for again automatically. If that retry also fails later, it is
  listed under **Card refunds Stripe gave up on** on the Stuck states page for
  the treasurer to close as paid another way. Closing one notes in Xero only
  what the card refund note already there does not cover, and the dialog says
  how much that note covers. A refund made by hand in the card provider's
  dashboard, or an older group refund, is not re-sent; the officers are emailed
  with its refund id (and told not to raise a second Xero note for it), and the audit log records it under **Payment** (one more
  `payment` audit writer: 503 in all). A cancellation's card refund shortfall
  can no longer be marked paid back while such a refund is still owed.
  **Operators:** once the new release alone is serving, add the `refund.failed`
  event to the club's card-provider webhook endpoint (the Stripe setup wizard's
  Webhook step lists every event; see `DEPLOYMENT.md`). It is required: the
  payments cron only catches refunds still pending. **On upgrade:** a refund
  the card provider created before this release that is found failed is not
  re-sent - the member may already have been paid back by hand - but listed
  with its retries spent, for the treasurer to check and close; and check the
  card provider's failed refunds once by hand, as `DEPLOYMENT.md` says.
- **A card refund the card provider refuses is no longer reported as made,
  wherever it starts (#4103).** Some card refunds - a reviewed change's, an
  approved late card charge's, a duplicate charge's, a refund after the dates
  filled up while the member was paying, and a few automatic ones - could
  still be marked as done when the card provider answered straight away that
  the refund failed or was cancelled, so the member was told they had been
  refunded when they had not. Now the refused amount stays owed: it counts in
  **Refunds owed**, the officers are emailed once, and it is retried
  automatically as a fresh request. An automatic refund of a late card charge
  on a cancelled booking that is refused is held on the payments board for a
  treasurer to approve instead, whatever the club's setting. A late-charge
  refund from the booking repair tool reports the refusal as a failure, and
  running the repair again asks afresh. An old group organiser's refund and
  the refund of a stale group payment report it as a failure too, and are
  retried automatically as a fresh request; the officers are told once.
- **The cancel dialog no longer promises the card more than the cancellation
  will refund to it (#4119).** Since #4097 a card cancellation refunds to the
  card only what the payment's card charges can still give back, and records
  the rest to be refunded by bank transfer, or checked first. The dialog's
  summary still quoted the whole refund as "Refund to card", so a member could
  be told one figure before confirming and a smaller one after. Where the card
  cannot carry the whole refund, the summary now shows the card's part, the
  part the club will refund by bank transfer and the part the club will be in
  touch about, worked out exactly as the cancellation works them out, in the
  cancellation email's wording put in the future tense. The refund option
  names where each part goes. Nothing changes where the card carries the
  whole refund, or for account credit.
- **An approved late-card-charge refund no longer marks its retry record as
  done from under another process (#4126).** After a treasurer approves the
  refund of a late card charge, the app marked its retry record as done
  without checking whether the record had already moved on, for example
  because it was re-planned after a refusal, or picked up by the retry worker.
  It now marks it done only when the record is exactly as the approval left
  it. If the retry worker has picked it up, the worker finishes it and writes
  the refund record once, now naming the refund. If the record was left
  untouched and still could not be marked done, officers are alerted once,
  with the refund's id, to check it.
- **A price increase whose card request already belongs to another change of
  the same booking now reaches an administrator at once (#4081).** In a rare
  order, two changes to one booking can end up with the same card request
  recorded for the first. The automatic retry for the second used to be refused
  the same way on each of its five attempts, over about five hours and twenty
  minutes, before anyone was told. It now stops on the first refusal, keeps the money owed on
  record, and sends one alert that names the cause; the "Exhausted recovery
  operations" item on the stuck-state page lists it.
- **A card payment already taken can no longer read as unpaid again (#4081).**
  When Stripe confirmed a payment before the booking change or card step that
  asked for it had finished recording its request, that recording could set
  the payment back to "pending" and the booking would look as if it still owed
  the money. A recorded payment, or a refund made against it, now keeps its
  status. Nothing needs doing.
- **A refund appeal can no longer be approved against money a card refund
  still owes (#4124).** A card refund not yet completed - still being sent,
  refused and being retried, or failed after being accepted - stays owed, but
  it had dropped out of the payment's refunded total, so the most an appeal
  could refund rose by the same amount, and approving one could return that
  money twice. The appeal limit now subtracts card refunds still owed, as
  **Refunds owed** counts them: on the approval itself, on the member's
  request, on reopening a dismissed appeal, and on the figures the booking page
  and the refund-requests screen offer. Both screens say when a card refund is
  what lowered the limit, and the approval reads it under the payment's row
  lock, so a refund recorded at that moment cannot slip between its reads.
- **The payments job's check on group organiser card refunds can no longer
  hang on a slow card provider (#4130).** Each check now gives up after ten
  seconds without retrying, and the pass starts no new check after a minute, as the
  card-refund check that runs after it already does. The refunds checked least
  recently go first, so the ones it skips, that keep timing out, or that
  cannot be saved, are checked on later runs without holding up the rest.
- **A late card payment on a cancelled booking is now refunded from that payment
  itself, never from a fee the cancellation kept (#4131).** Take a booking paid by
  a second card charge, where the first payment went through after the booking was
  cancelled. The automatic refund could come partly off the second charge, which
  held the cancellation fee the club kept. The late payment then kept that same
  amount. The member always got the right total back, but Xero could not follow it:
  the nightly refund-note check raised a credit note against the booking's
  original invoice, leaving the Stripe account in Xero short by that amount. The
  refund now always comes off the late payment's own charge, and only for what it
  still holds, so the cancellation fee stays where it was and no extra credit note
  is raised for any late payment refunded on this release. A refund the previous
  release had already split this way is unchanged and is still noted by the
  nightly check, as before. The refund's activity entry now also says how much
  went back now, and how much of the payment had already been refunded.

  **Before deploying:** the previous release kept no record of a refund it had
  only started. If it crashed part-way through refunding a late payment just
  before the deploy, the new release refunds the whole payment again on its own
  charge, so part of it could be refunded twice. Check the Stripe dashboard for
  failing `payment_intent.succeeded` deliveries on cancelled bookings and let
  them settle first, and do not roll back across this release while late
  payments are arriving (see `docs/UPGRADING.md`).
- **A card refund that failed later is no longer marked paid by the refund that
  first sent it (#4144).** When a cancellation, a booking edit's financial
  review, a duplicate-capture refund or a capacity-race refund was made at
  Stripe, the app closed its "refund owed" record straight away. In a narrow
  window - the automatic retry had already picked the record up, and Stripe
  then reported the refund as failed - that close could mark the money paid
  while it was still owed, so "Refunds owed" stopped counting it. The close
  now happens only while the record still holds exactly the refund it sent;
  a record that has since been re-planned stays open and is retried. The
  officers are still alerted to the failed refund. The cancellation,
  edit-review, duplicate-capture and capacity-race doors now also alert the
  officers once if their close is missed on a record nothing else has
  touched, as the approved late-capture refund already did; any other missed
  close is logged.
- **A card payment refunded short after the dates filled up is now a task to
  check (#4154).** When a member's card payment completes after the last beds
  went, the booking is cancelled and the card refunded automatically for what
  the payment's records show can go back to the card. When that was less than
  the charge, or nothing, officers were emailed but nothing in the app tracked
  the rest, and the member's page kept saying the club would be in touch.
  The rest now appears in **Money to settle** as a part to check, the same as
  a card cancellation's. Check Stripe and the bank first, since the records may
  be wrong and the money may already have gone back: dismiss it with a note if
  it has, and the member's page says the club checked it and closed it. If it
  really is owed, use **Mark paid back** first, once the card refund has gone
  through, and pay by bank transfer straight after the app accepts: it first
  checks it can record it, only on that card charge. It asks Stripe what the
  charge has refunded, and waits while Stripe shows a refund the app has not
  recorded yet, or cannot be reached. Where the charge's records read more
  refunded than the card refunds on record, it corrects them itself first and
  logs that in the audit log (under Payment, which finance officers read), but
  only for a charge made since the app kept a record of each card refund, on a
  booking with no account credit given back, no other refund task and no Xero
  refund credit note beyond its card refunds. Accepted, it records the refund
  on the booking's ledger, queues its Xero refund credit note, and the member's
  page says the whole payment was refunded; a booking with no Xero invoice to
  credit gets no note. If it refuses, it says why and what to do: dismiss the
  task with a note saying when and how much, and raise the Xero note by hand
  only where it says to. The officers' email now points at the task.
- **Card refund hand-backs are marked first, then paid (#4154).** For a card
  cancellation's parts too - the bank-transfer part and the part to check -
  the queue, the confirm dialog, the officers' email and the refusals now all
  say the same: mark it paid back first, and pay straight after the app
  accepts, so a refusal never comes after the money has gone. Where the
  records show nothing left to refund, the refusal now also says what to do if
  the member really is owed.
- **Officers are told when a card refund lands on a charge already refunded
  (#4154).** If a card refund reaches the app for a charge whose records
  already read fully refunded - for example one made in Stripe after a
  hand-back was marked paid back - officers are now emailed, once, that the
  member may have been paid twice, instead of the extra being dropped silently.
  And a capacity race's part to check can now be marked paid back after the
  nightly Xero check has already raised a card refund note for the same money:
  that note is counted, so no second one is raised.
- **A booking's confirmation shows additional money and how to pay (#4047).**
  This includes an Internet Banking correction on a finished stay. Additional card
  asks point the member to their pay card. Supplementary bank invoices show
  their remaining amounts, invoice references and when they were checked, with
  **Check more invoices** for larger groups. Unissued or unavailable amounts
  say they cannot yet be confirmed; the page no longer reassures a member that
  no payment was required while an addition is outstanding or uncertain.
  Officers see a read-only view and linked guests a neutral confirmation.
- **A cancelled booking's card refund now shows in its history on the day it
  was actually made (#4145).** When a member cancelled a card-paid booking,
  its history recorded "refunded" straight away, even when the card refund had
  failed and was still waiting to be retried. When the automatic retry later
  made the refund, nothing new was recorded, so the history never showed the
  real date.

  The refund is now recorded once, when it is actually made: at the cancel
  when the card refund goes through first time, or when the automatic retry
  makes it later, with the date and amount of that refund. Until then the
  booking page says the refund is on its way, or that the club will be in
  touch if the retries have run out. A refund an officer closes as "Paid
  another way" is shown as paid back another way, not as refunded to the card;
  if part of it had already gone back to the card, the history records that
  part, dated when the card refund was made, and the page names both - for a
  member's cancel and for a booking cancelled because its dates filled up. If
  the club paid back only some of the rest, the page says how much, and that
  the club closed the remainder. A later change to the booking's money (an
  edit review's credit or refund) is no longer shown as the cancellation's
  refund.
- **Payment records saved at the same moment now always read in the same
  order** (#4132). When a booking change saves two payment records together -
  say a new payment request and the one it replaces - the system now always
  knows which came last. The payment summary, an edit that lowers the price,
  and the finance checks therefore agree on which request is the one still
  owed, and a refund split across charges saved together refunds the most
  recent one first. Records saved before this release are given an order on
  upgrade: anything cancelled, failed or withdrawn comes before what is still
  live, so the live request stays the one that counts. **Operators:** the
  upgrade briefly locks the payment records table - about 2 to 3.5 seconds per
  100,000 records - and has read-only pre-deploy checks (stored ties, and any
  unfinished card refund on them); see the migration's row in
  `docs/BLUE_GREEN_MIGRATION_SAFETY.tsv`.
- **"Booking may have been paid twice — card and Xero" now names the same card
  payment every time (#4163).** When a booking had been settled by card and its
  Xero invoice was then also paid by bank transfer, the admin alert names the
  card payment that settled the booking. If the booking held more than one card
  capture, which one the alert named was left to chance.

  It now names the earliest capture that no duplicate-capture refund is already
  returning. On a paid booking it skips a capture that was partly refunded
  before the booking moved to Internet Banking; on a cancelled booking such a
  capture is named only if nothing else qualifies. No money moves differently;
  only which capture the alert and its record point at is now predictable. This
  applies to conflicts found from this release; an alert already recorded keeps
  the card it named.
- **The promo code box prices the nights a guest actually stays (#4199).** When
  a booking uses the night-by-night grid, a guest can stay, say, the 10th and
  12th but not the 11th. The promo code box, on the booking editor and in the
  new-booking wizard, used to work out the discount as if that guest stayed all
  three nights, so it could show a bigger discount than the price summary
  beside it. It now uses the same nights as the price summary and the save.

  What a member is charged does not change: that always came from the price
  summary. When the grid is off and a guest has their own Date In and Date Out,
  the box still prices those dates as one continuous stay, as before.

  Behind the scenes, every booking request that names guests (new bookings,
  quotes, edits, exception and change requests, and the promo code box) now
  checks a guest's nights the same way, and a night that isn't a real date is
  explained in plain words rather than as "Invalid input". One request can add,
  remove or rename at most 200 guests, and a new booking can have at most 200,
  as before; a booking edit and its price preview now refuse more than that,
  where before they had no limit, and say so in plain words. Edits, quotes and
  promo checks of a booking that already holds more than 200 guests (possible
  at a lodge that sleeps more) are not limited by this.
- **A cancelled booking no longer says its card refund was made after Stripe
  failed it (#4166).** When a cancellation's card refund was recorded as
  refunded and Stripe later reported that refund as failed, the money was owed
  again and retried, but the member's booking page and payment-link page still
  said it had been refunded on the cancellation's refund date. This applied to
  member cancellations and to bookings cancelled because the dates filled up
  while the payment went through.

  The page now says the failed amount by where its new refund stands: on its way
  to the original payment method, refunded to the card again (with that date),
  being refunded with the club in touch, or paid back another way. Any part of
  the refund that did not fail still reads as refunded on its original date.
  Nothing changes for the club's records or for how a failed refund is retried.
- **The duplicate-capture refund and the "paid twice — card and Xero" alert
  name the same settling payment (#4177).** When a second card payment lands
  on a booking that is already paid, the club refunds it automatically and
  tells the admins which payment had settled the booking, in the alert email
  and in the booking's admin history. If the booking held more than one
  payment that could have settled it, which one was named was left to chance.

  It now names the earliest qualifying payment wherever it names one, the same
  rule the "paid twice — card and Xero" alert follows (#4163). A card payment
  that is already being cancelled or refunded because a newer one replaced it
  never counts for the refund, and on a paid booking the "paid twice" alert now
  skips it too, while its cancel is under way or its refund has not yet gone
  through. On a cancelled booking the alert still counts it, because the bank
  payment has nowhere else to go. If the earliest is a cash or Internet Banking settlement, no card
  payment is named. A refund the background retry finishes, rather than the
  first attempt, still records no settling payment in the history.

  No money moves differently: the arriving duplicate is still the only payment
  refunded. This applies from this release; alerts and history already
  recorded keep the payment they named.
- **On a booking edit, the promo code box uses the prices the guests already
  paid (#4202).** When a booking is edited, every night a guest already holds
  keeps the price it was sold at, and only nights the edit adds are priced at
  today's rates. The promo code box on the booking editor used to price every
  night at today's rates instead, so once the club's rates had changed since
  the booking was made it could show a different discount from the price
  summary beside it. It now prices the booking the same way as the price
  summary and the save, so the two show the same discount. When an officer
  ticks or unticks a guest as another club's member, or links a placeholder
  guest to a member, the box now re-prices that guest as the summary does. On a
  school's booking the box now refuses a code that benefits the person who made
  the booking, with the summary's message, where it used to judge the code
  against the officer editing it.

  Behind the scenes, the server now answers an edit's promo check for the
  booking itself whatever the request says, as the price summary does: against
  the booking's owner rather than any other member named, at the booking's own
  lodge, and with the club's "group discount on later edits" setting. The
  booking editor already sent those, so they change nothing on screen; they
  matter for anything calling the check directly. The check also no longer
  counts the booking's own use of a code against the code's use limits, which
  the price summary never did; on screen that only shows when a code the
  booking already carries is checked again with a different choice of guests.

  What a member is charged does not change: that always came from the price
  summary. The box on a new booking is unchanged.
- **The "paid twice — card and Xero" alert no longer names a card payment
  whose refund is being sent again (#4221).** When a newer card payment
  replaced an older one, the club refunds the older one automatically. If
  Stripe accepted that refund and failed it later, or failed another refund
  of it, the app asks for it again, or leaves it for the treasurer to pay
  another way. Until then the alert counted the older
  payment as if it had settled the booking: if the booking was also paid by
  bank transfer, the alert named a payment already on its way back to the
  member, and an officer refunding the bank transfer on that advice would
  have left the booking with no money held.

  The alert now skips that payment while everything it holds is owed back
  to the member, as it already did while the first refund was under way
  (#4177). It names the payment that did settle the booking, or raises
  nothing when there is no other card payment. If the payment holds more
  than is owed back - say a refund made by hand in Stripe failed too - it
  is still named. Once the refund is made again, or closed as paid another
  way, the payment counts as before. Cancelled bookings are unchanged, and
  no money moves differently.
- **The app records which payment settled each booking, and refunds every
  other card payment on it (#4211).** When a second card payment lands on a
  booking that is already paid, the club refunds it automatically and alerts
  the admins. But once one such refund existed on a booking, any further
  payment was treated as the one that settled it. So when a member paid three
  times, for example from three old browser tabs, the club kept the third
  payment, with no alert and no task for anyone. Guessing which payment
  settled the booking could also go the other way: a repeat of the real
  payment's webhook could be refunded when a bank receipt or an older payment
  still held money.

  Now the payment that settles a booking is recorded when the booking turns
  Paid. It is never refunded automatically, however often Stripe repeats it.
  Every other card payment is refunded, each with its own alert and its own
  entry in the booking's admin history. The alert names the payment that
  settled the booking; the history entry names it too when the refund goes
  through straight away.

  Bookings paid before this release have no record. For those, when a card
  payment arrives while another payment on the booking still holds money,
  nothing is refunded automatically: the admins get an email that cannot be
  muted, asking them to check which payment to refund by hand. Before this
  release such a payment was refunded automatically; on a booking with no
  record it now waits for an admin. Nothing goes back through past
  bookings. Deploy note: the column is additive, and a booking the old colour
  settles during the switch is treated as paid before this release.

  Two related gaps close with it (#4227, #4283). A payment the club is already
  refunding because it was replaced by a newer one - including one whose
  refund the card provider failed later and the club is sending again - no
  longer counts as a second payment: it no longer triggers a false "paid
  twice" email, and when that same payment's confirmation arrives again it is
  no longer refunded a second time on top of the refund already under way.
- **A payment's refunded total can no longer be overwritten by a write made at
  the same moment (#4217).** When two things changed one payment at once, the
  refunded total could end up wrong. For example, a top-up's card payment could
  land just as a treasurer confirmed a bank-transfer refund cancelled, or as
  account credit was given back. The payment would then show a refunded figure
  that its own refund history did not add up to, and nothing flagged it. Every
  card capture, bank-transfer receipt, top-up request and refund now waits its
  turn on the payment, so the total is always worked out from the latest
  figures. This also fixes a rare clash between a card payment being recorded
  and a refund on the same charge, which could make one of them fail.

  What you may notice: in the rare case that a Stripe notification arrives while
  a long change to the same booking is still saving, it can now be turned away
  and Stripe sends it again a moment later, as it already does for other busy
  moments. Nothing is lost, and no action is needed. In the same rare case, a
  member or officer saving a booking change or a payment may see an error;
  trying again a moment later succeeds.
- **When an officer settles a booking-change review as money the member owes,
  a booking paid entirely with account credit is now asked by card (#3947).**
  A booking paid wholly with credit has no card payment behind it. Before this,
  settling such a review as money owed was refused when the booking had no Xero
  invoice, and the officer had to collect the money by hand. When the booking did
  have an invoice, the amount went onto a supplementary Xero invoice instead.

  The member is now asked to pay the extra by card, whether or not Xero is
  connected. This is the rule ordinary booking edits have followed since #3502,
  and the background retry that takes over when Stripe is briefly unavailable
  follows it too. Bookings that already had money taken by card are asked the
  same way as before, and a booking paid by internet banking is still billed
  through its invoice. If an earlier review of the same change was already
  billed on a Xero invoice that is still on its way to Xero (queued, being
  sent, or failed and not yet resolved), a later one goes on that invoice
  rather than to the card, so the member is not asked twice for the same money.
  One case is still open: an officer requeuing a failed invoice after a later
  review of the same change has raised a new one can bill that change twice
  (#4274).
- **A booking-change review can no longer ask a cancelled booking's member to
  pay (#4272).** When an officer settled a booking-change review as money owed
  to the club after the booking had been cancelled, and the booking still held
  money paid by card, the system created a card payment request the member
  could never pay: every place a member pays leaves cancelled bookings out.
  The task still read as completed, so the treasurer saw a charge that would
  never be collected.

  The officer now sees a clear refusal instead, and the task stays open:
  collect the amount another way, then dismiss the task with a note recording
  what was collected and how. If the organiser paid for a joiner's booking,
  the message says to agree the amount with the organiser.

  If the booking is cancelled in the moment just after a review is settled,
  nothing is asked of the member and the officer is told so straight away. The
  amount still owed is recorded once in the audit log as a review share that
  was not collected: the settled total less anything the member paid towards
  it and kept, with any refund stated, and it waits while that payment or a
  refund of it is still going through. An officer can find it there and
  collect it another way. Reviews on bookings that are not cancelled are
  unchanged.
- **A refund owed on a group booking the organiser paid for by internet
  banking can now be paid back, and goes to the organiser (#3949).** When a
  joiner's change lowered the price of their place, or an appeal on their place
  was approved, the club's refund task on the payments board could be neither
  marked paid back ("more than was ever captured on this payment") nor, once
  the organiser had cancelled the group, dismissed. It stayed open for ever.

  Marking it paid back now works, before or after the organiser cancels the
  group, and records the refund against the joiner's share of the organiser's
  group payment. The money came from the organiser, so it goes back to the
  organiser: the task says "to the group organiser by bank transfer", and the
  joiner's email says the club will refund the group organiser directly. Tasks
  already stuck can simply be marked paid back now; nothing needs migrating.

  Until #4292 the app does not raise this refund's Xero credit note (the
  joiner's booking has no invoice of its own), so marking it paid back emails
  admins to credit the group's combined invoice by hand. A price review settled as money owed back on
  such a booking goes to the organiser the same way. A joiner's own cancellation
  after such a refund no longer marks the organiser's payment as never made.

  A joiner cancelling their own place on such a group with a refund due used to
  be refused; the cancel now goes ahead and raises the same kind of task, so the
  refund goes back to the organiser by bank transfer rather than to the joiner.
  It is worked out on the club's card refund tiers, as every refund to the
  organiser is, and admins get the "Manual refund needed" email for it.

  A change that lowers the price of such a place no longer offers the joiner
  account credit: the refund, at the card refund tier, always goes back to the
  organiser by bank transfer, as it does for a group paid by card.

  A later cancellation of the group by the organiser counts a refund already
  paid this way exactly once. Dismissing a change's refund after the group is
  cancelled is still refused, as before, and the refusal now names the
  organiser. Card-paid groups are unchanged.
- **A card payment that arrives after a stay has ended is handled like one on
  a paid booking (#4285).** When Stripe sent the success of a card payment
  after the booking had moved to completed, the system refused it with an
  error, so Stripe kept retrying it for up to three days and the webhook log
  filled with failures. For the payment that paid for the stay that was only
  noise, but when a member had paid twice (for example from an old browser
  tab), the extra payment was not refunded automatically. Now it is: a repeat
  of the payment that settled the booking is acknowledged and changes nothing,
  and any other card payment is refunded automatically as a duplicate, or kept
  and flagged for an administrator to check when the system has no record of
  which payment settled the booking, just as on a paid booking.

  A card payment that reaches the app for the first time on a paid or
  completed booking that has no other payment holding money and no record of
  which payment settled it (a booking paid with account credit, at a zero
  total or by a group organiser, or one whose earlier payment was refunded) is
  now kept and flagged to the administrators, whatever its amount, rather than
  kept without a word - including a saved-card charge the app records just
  before settling it. A repeat of a payment the app had already recorded is
  still acknowledged quietly. If that alert cannot be sent (or the app stops
  before sending it), it stays owed: the payment's next arrival sends it, and a
  new payments task, "Kept card payment alert", sends it an hour later
  otherwise - about a day later at worst, when the app stopped just after
  claiming that day's alert. That later alert says if the booking was
  cancelled since (naming the cancellation's refund, which may have been
  made as account credit or by hand, and saying a card refund was sent only
  once it was and not after the card company turned it back, a refund to the
  group organiser's card as such, and a part already paid back by bank
  transfer as paid) or another payment now holds money too, and every alert names
  a payment the app no longer counts that still holds money and shows what
  the card payment still holds.
  One case stays quiet: a saved-card charge whose charging request stopped or
  failed between recording the payment and settling it.

  **After upgrading,** run the read-only query in the upgrade notes to list
  completed bookings that may hold a second card payment whose retries ran out
  before the upgrade (or a lone card payment on a booking paid with credit, at
  a zero total or by a group organiser), and check each in Stripe with the
  treasurer. An extra payment found there is refunded by hand in Stripe; the
  app records that refund and queues a Xero credit note, which must be deleted
  or voided in Xero until #4322 is fixed, whether or not its event was resent.
- **A card payment on an out-of-date payment can no longer mark a booking paid
  and then be refunded (#4300).** When a booking was edited, the payment the
  member had already started was replaced and queued to be cancelled, or
  refunded if they paid it anyway. Only Stripe's own notification checked for
  that. If the member paid the old payment from a tab still open, and the
  booking's price had come back to its old amount, the payment page, a
  reloaded payment link, or Stripe's notification arriving after the refund was
  queued could mark the booking paid with it. The refund then went through,
  and the booking showed as paid with no money held.

  The booking's settlement now refuses that payment itself, whichever way it
  arrives, including the club's own saved-card charges. The payment goes back
  as before, the booking stays unpaid, and admins are told if it got as far as
  the settlement. A member who has just paid that way on the booking page is
  told the payment will be returned to their card and asked to reload and pay
  the amount the booking shows now; a payer on a payment link sees a notice
  that their earlier payment is going back, beside a fresh payment.
  Neither page offers the out-of-date payment again once the price comes back
  to its amount.
- **Reversing a payment recorded outside the app no longer leaves a stuck card
  cancellation that refunds the member's next card payment (#4320).** When an
  officer records a booking as paid outside the app (cash or bank transfer),
  the app cancels any card payment the member still had open. If Stripe was
  unreachable at that moment, the cancellation waited to retry. Reversing the
  payment used to leave that waiting cancellation behind. If the member then
  paid by card in the page they still had open, the payment was refunded and
  the booking stayed unpaid.

  The reversal now works out again, from the booking as it stands, which open
  card payments are out of date. It keeps cancelling those, including one an
  edit had already queued, and restarts a cancellation that had given up or
  was on its last try. It withdraws the cancellation of the one the booking
  can still be paid with, even one waiting to retry or one that has given up.
  A saved-card charge is judged against the booking's full value: the amount
  the app's automatic saved-card charge takes, and the amount it accepts a
  card payment at. A card request for an extra the reversal puts back to owing is
  found even when the cash settlement had hidden it, as long as it is still
  open and not one the reversal keeps cancelling. The booking points at it
  again, so when the member pays it the extra reads as paid and is no longer
  chased, and an officer can still withdraw it. A card payment the member makes while the reversal is
  running now waits for it, then pays the booking. The reversal's audit entry
  lists every cancellation it withdrew or restarted, every card payment still
  being cancelled, and the card request the extra points at again.
  Reversals made before this release may have left a cancellation behind, or
  a hidden card request with nothing cancelling it: `docs/UPGRADING.md` has
  read-only queries to find both and what to do.
- **Credit a treasurer uses in Xero is now taken off the member's credit by itself, and put back if the use is undone (#4270).** Until now the app only found out that a member's credit note had been used in Xero (an offset against an invoice that is not a booking's, or a payment made against it) when a booking tried to use that credit and Xero refused. The credit stayed on offer to the member in the meantime. Now, within about 15 minutes of the change in Xero, once the note has been left alone for two minutes, the app writes down the part of the credit that no booking has claimed, so it is no longer offered, and shows an "Admin Adjustment" line on the member's credit history. If the use is undone in Xero, the app gives that credit back. It never takes a member's balance below zero, credit already given to a booking is left to the existing fix for that, nothing is sent to Xero and the member is not emailed. A note that is voided or deleted in Xero is not changed and is reported for an officer to look at. It can be switched off without a deploy (see the upgrade notes).
- **A booking change that adds to the price no longer leaves a card request
  open on a booking cancelled a moment later (#4316).** When a member added a
  guest or changed dates and then cancelled straight away, the extra amount
  could still be requested from their card just after the cancellation went
  through. The member could not pay it in the app, but the request stayed open
  with Stripe and the booking's payment record was left untidy.

  The extra amount is now checked against the booking just before the card is
  asked and again straight afterwards. A booking that has been cancelled is
  asked for nothing, and a request that slipped through in the moment between
  is withdrawn and cancelled with Stripe, the same way a cancellation withdraws
  one. The automatic retry of a card request that failed the first time, and a
  request re-issued after the club changes its currency, follow the same rule,
  as does a booking whose card payment had already been refunded in full. The
  change email no longer names the extra as due on a cancelled booking.
  Nothing changes for bookings that stay live.
- **Old edit reviews can no longer be put back on the finance queue, and a one-off clean-up settles any that are still open (#4343).**
  Reopening a dismissed edit review used to put it back on the queue, which blocked later changes to that booking and brought back the old settle screens. That button is gone for an edit review. Every other money task can still be put back.

  After this is the only version serving, run `pnpm run bookings:edit-review-cleanup` against a copy of the database, read the dry-run, then apply it with `--actor`. It prices any review still open through the normal refund, credit or charge. It also re-sets a booking total that an old review froze to the sum of its guests, and that re-set moves no money. Run it again only to confirm it has nothing left to do.
- **A member whose account credit was used elsewhere in the club's accounts is now
  asked to pay for it.** When account credit applied to a lodge booking is found to
  have been spent in Xero outside the app, the booking is short by that amount and
  nothing used to ask for it. The member now gets a card payment request and an
  email at the next reminder pass (a last-chance email can follow, as for any
  request), worded as "the credit applied to your booking was used elsewhere in the
  club's accounts" (not as a change to their stay). The card payment is recorded in
  Xero against the booking's own invoice, with no second invoice, and the request
  closes by itself when Xero shows the invoice paid by another route. Raising the
  requests starts switched off and is turned on by an operator after the deploy
  (see `docs/xero/ARCHITECTURE.md`); recording and closing are always on.
- **Members asked to pay for account credit used elsewhere are now reminded
  weekly, can pay by bank transfer, and the older cases are picked up.** The
  request for credit that was used elsewhere in the club's accounts is emailed
  at once, then reminded every 7 days, four reminders after the request (five
  emails at most); after that only the officers' queues chase it, and the
  reminders carry on after the stay has ended. Where the club has written its bank
  details (a new "Bank transfer details for a payment request" message under
  Admin → Booking messages), the email offers a bank
  transfer as well as card, quoting the booking's Xero invoice number as the
  payment reference, and the request closes when Xero shows the invoice paid. The
  transfer is offered only when it would pay exactly what is asked; if Xero shows the
  invoice part-paid, the automatic reminders stop and the officers are told in the
  audit log, rather than the member being asked to pay by card what may already be paid.
  Every screen and email now says why a request exists (a booking change, credit
  used elsewhere, or both, when a change was made while the request was unpaid and
  the two became one). Credit released before the requests were switched on can be
  asked for in small, audited batches behind a second switch (see
  `docs/xero/ARCHITECTURE.md`); each is re-checked against Xero first, so nothing is
  asked that is no longer owed.
  Credit released while a request for a booking change is still unpaid now waits for
  that request to be paid or withdrawn, however long it takes, and is asked for then;
  before, it gave up after a few retries and was never asked for.
- **A saved-card charge from the officer's "confirm pending guests" button or
  the charge-saved-method route now includes a change fee recorded on the
  booking (#4357).** The overnight confirm job already charged the price plus
  the fee. These two charged the price alone, so when an unpaid booking carried
  a change fee, the card was charged short and the booking could not be
  settled: the money was taken, but the booking stayed confirmed and unpaid
  until an officer stepped in. All three now charge the same amount, and the
  officer's confirm dialog and the confirmation email quote it. A booking whose
  price is $0 but which still carries a change fee is now charged the fee,
  instead of being confirmed free.
- **The retry of a lost card request for a price increase now looks for the
  earlier request more narrowly (#4079).** When a paid booking's price goes up
  and Stripe refuses the automatic retry of the card request, the retry looks
  for the request Stripe already made. It used to also accept one labelled the
  way the previous version of the retry labelled its own requests; no such retry
  is left, so it no longer does, and it only looks at requests made around the
  time the original one failed. On a very busy Stripe account the search no
  longer gives up just because of the number of later card requests. In the rare
  case where the earlier request can't be found, the retry now gives up and
  alerts an administrator instead of reusing a request it can't be sure is this
  one; the administrator checks Stripe for that booking and amount. Upgrading
  from v0.13.2 or earlier: run a release containing #4077 for a day first, or
  any leftover retry from the old version ends the same way.
- **Confirming a free booking's pending guests now records its payment in the
  same step, and the charge-saved-method route no longer tries to charge a
  booking that owes nothing (#4399).** The officer's "confirm pending guests"
  for a booking worth $0 used to write its payment record just after the
  booking was confirmed, so a change fee recorded in that moment could go
  uncollected.
  Both now happen together, as the overnight confirm job already did. The
  charge-saved-method route now refuses a booking worth $0 with a message to
  use "Confirm pending guests". Before, it claimed the booking, asked the card
  provider for a charge too small to make, and then had to undo the claim.
- **A later change now cancels an earlier declined card payment too (#4422).** When a member's card was declined for an
  extra booking charge and a later change replaced that charge, the declined
  one was marked failed in the booking system but left open at Stripe. A
  browser tab still showing it could then pay it, charging the member for both
  and, once the later charge was paid, recording one of the two in Xero
  nowhere. The declined charge is now cancelled at Stripe like any other
  replaced charge. If the old tab manages to pay it in the moment before the
  cancel lands, that payment is refunded automatically (or held for the
  treasurer where the club requires it), as for any replaced charge paid late.
  A short window remains, shared with charges that were never declined, where
  a payment made while the later change is still being set up is not caught;
  #4442 tracks it.
- **An edit's Xero note no longer records a bank refund before it is paid
  back (#4315).** The edit's refund task must be marked paid back before its
  note counts towards refunded cash, including when a later Xero sync recounts
  the payment. A dismissed task records no refund. Cancellation card notes
  now explicitly carry the card method through processing and retries.
- **A member can no longer pay the same extra charge twice from an old browser tab (#4442).**
  When a member changed a booking again while an earlier extra card charge was
  still unpaid, the new charge included the earlier one's balance and cancelled
  it. If an old tab paid the earlier charge in the moment while the new charge
  was being set up, that payment was kept and the new charge still asked for
