  the same money, so the member paid it twice and nobody was told. The new
  charge is now checked against what is still unpaid just before it is saved:
  if the earlier charge was paid in that moment, the new charge is not offered,
  and the automatic retry asks only for the latest change. A legacy retry
  whose saved amount cannot be reconstructed refuses after an earlier extra
  charge was captured, and alerts an officer when its attempts run out. This closes the
  short window #4422 left open.
- **A bank refund recorded with "Paid another way" no longer disappears from the refunded total when a late card refund fails (#4280).**
  When the treasurer closed a card refund as paid another way, and the card
  refund Stripe had lost then turned up late and later failed, the app took
  the whole failed refund off the payment's refunded total. The bank refund
  still stood, but the total could fall to nothing, so the booking showed that
  money as kept and as refundable again. The total now never falls below the
  bank money "Paid another way" closes recorded: the full amount, or for a part
  close what was actually paid.

  Only these closes count. Card and capacity refund shortfalls paid back by
  bank are outside this repair (the owner's decision of 26 October; a voided
  refund note never undoes them). Ordinary bank hand-backs are not counted,
  because a voided refund note can undo one while its task still reads
  completed.

  Known limits. On a payment with more than one charge, bank money from a
  shortfall or hand-back on another charge is not protected: for example, a
  $200 card charge closed as paid another way beside a $100 shortfall paid
  back on a second charge can still drop to $100 when the late card refund
  fails, and the audit below does not see it (#4488). Account credit the app
  over-counts on some old bookings can keep a total slightly too high, which
  errs on the safe side.

  Payments a failure already took below a close's bank money are not changed
  automatically. The read-only `pnpm run payments:audit-refunded-total` report
  now lists them, with the bank money it counted, for the treasurer to review.
  Rolling the app back to an earlier version brings the old behaviour back.
- **A card refund Stripe failed later can no longer be paid back twice (#4492).**
  Stuck States no longer offers **Paid another way** on a refund the app gave
  up on while the same money may already be going back to the card, including
  after that card refund has succeeded. The button is also withheld on a refund
  that replaces a superseded payment while the other refund has not gone back
  to the card, and on a failed refund that died because that charge was already
  sent. The row stays on the list and says why.
- **A card refund that fails after its refund was closed "Paid another way" is no longer sent again automatically (#4210).**
  When a card refund's answer from Stripe was lost, the treasurer closed it as
  paid another way and paid the member by bank transfer, and Stripe then
  reported that lost refund as failed, the app raised a new card refund for it
  and sent it again on its own, so the member could be paid twice. That refund
  is now held for an officer instead: it is listed under **Card refunds Stripe
  gave up on** on the Stuck states page, it is never sent again automatically,
  and the officers are emailed once telling them to check the bank transfer the
  close recorded and to settle anything still owed with "Paid another way",
  never with a new refund in the Stripe dashboard (owner's decision of
  25 October, #4361).

  A failed refund whose card refund was not closed this way is asked for again
  automatically, as before; so is one on a payment where a different card
  refund was closed. One case is still open (#4492): a refund whose card refund
  had stalled but not yet been closed, failing before the close, is still sent
  again automatically, and the close still goes through.

  Known limits. After a part close, the amount shown for the held refund can
  include what that close recorded as no longer owed: check the close's record
  before paying. After a close that paid the member back in full, nothing is
  left owed on the payment, so the held refund is not offered for a close; it
  stays in the exhausted recovery operations count, and the health check's
  payment recovery result stays red because of it, until the later stage of
  #4361 settles these automatically. Ask a developer to reconcile it.
- Card refund retries now check Stripe before sending money again. If a dashboard
  refund may already have paid the debt, automatic retries stop and officers are
  alerted to check it before paying anything else. Refunds first discovered by
  that check retain their existing accounting corrections. The hold writes one
  `payment` audit entry, readable by the people who already see payment records.
- **Booking edit refunds retry without sending extra money (#3984).** If Stripe
  refunds a member but saving the refund fails, recovery now replays the original
  request even when a webhook records it first. Partial refunds keep their
  completed and outstanding parts together, with existing officer alerts.
- **The database can hold Stripe balance transactions and payouts, and the app does not write them yet (#4520).**
  Two empty tables are added. One is insert-only. The payout row can change status later. Bookings, payments, refunds and Xero are unchanged, and no provisioning step is needed.
- **Old payment tabs no longer offer bank details for unavailable bookings (#4365).** An Internet Banking booking that has been cancelled or deleted now returns an unavailable-booking message instead of its old payment reference. Active bookings keep their existing reference and payment hold when the request is repeated.
- Add the inert member-money journal foundation: balanced sealed batches, exact reversals, immutable obligations/applications and a retained booking-ledger source bridge. Extend least-privilege role provisioning, narrow the new tables in their own migration so a least-privilege deploy needs no provisioning step, and add a read-only verifier; no production money writer or reader switches.
- **Delayed card refund recovery no longer repeats an evidenced refund (#4510).**
  New keyed refunds identify their exact slice in Stripe. Recovery records and
  marks a refund it finds before sending only the remaining slices, even after
  Stripe's 24-hour replay protection expires. Older refunds without this
  evidence retain their existing recovery behaviour.
- **A Stripe payment the app did not create is no longer silent (#4532).** A
  club can take money on its Stripe account outside the app - a Stripe Payment
  Link for donations, a Checkout page, or a charge made in the Stripe
  dashboard. The app used to ignore such a payment, so nothing reached Xero and
  the Stripe clearing account stopped reconciling with nobody told why.

  The app now keeps a record of each such payment and sends Finance editors one
  email per payment, "Stripe payment the app did not create - code it in Xero",
  naming the amount, when it was paid, what was bought, and the Stripe payment
  and Payment Link, with a link to it in Stripe. It cannot be muted. The
  treasurer then records the money in Xero by hand against the Stripe clearing
  account; the [Payments guide](docs/guides/payments.md#a-stripe-payment-the-app-did-not-create)
  says how. Payments the app makes itself are unchanged.
- **The member-money ledger gains its posting command and a GST setting, with
  nothing posting yet (#4626).** This is the first of three steps that will
  record booking charges in the app's own double-entry ledger. It adds the one
  command every later step posts through. That command records each business
  event as a single balanced entry, and it refuses an entry that does not
  balance before writing anything. Replaying the same event changes nothing,
  and replaying it with different amounts is refused rather than skipped.

  It also adds a record of the club's GST treatment: whether the club is
  GST-registered, the rate, and the date it applies from. Until a club records
  otherwise, the app uses the treatment its Xero invoices already show: GST
  included in every price at 15%. The ledger will split tax out of each charge
  in whole cents on that basis.

  Nothing changes for members or officers in this release. No booking, payment
  or screen uses the ledger yet, and there is no screen for the GST setting.
  Xero invoices do not read the setting yet either, so nothing may change it
  until they do: a club that is not GST-registered will need that screen
  before the ledger records its charges.
- **A booking officer can now apply a member's missed promo code to a stay that
  has already finished (#4533).** When an officer books a stay for a member and
  forgets the member's assigned free night, the member pays full price. Once the
  stay was over there was no way to put that right in the app, and the
  workarounds - a hand-made Xero credit note, or a redemption typed into the
  records - left the free night showing as unused, so it could be claimed again.

  Now the correction goes through the same approve-and-apply step officers
  already use for finished stays. In Edit Booking, choosing a code on a finished
  stay no longer leaves Save doing nothing: the panel says the stay has finished
  and offers **Send as a promo correction request**, which opens the request in
  Booking change requests. An officer can also type the code into **Promo code to
  apply** on any finished-stay request. **Check the figures** shows the
  reduction, and **Approve and apply** applies the code exactly as Edit Booking
  would on a future stay - who it is assigned to and its limits still apply, and
  a code that doesn't apply is refused with the same reason. The free night is
  then counted as used, the booking's price and ledger are corrected, and the
  reduction comes back in full, as account credit by default (with an unapplied
  account-credit note in Xero) or as a refund if the officer chooses. There is
  no change fee. For a promo-only correction the officer can choose not to email
  the member. Approving twice changes nothing a second time. The request an
  officer raises from Edit Booking is recorded in the audit log under Booking,
  readable by the same people as a member's own change request.
- **Confirmed bookings now post their charges into the member-money journal
  (Ledger M3b, #4627).** When a booking is confirmed, edited, has a review
  closed or is cancelled, the same booking-ledger lines it already writes are
  posted into the built-in double-entry journal in the same transaction, each
  linked to its line, with an organisation as the debtor for an
  organisation-owned booking. A member merge moves the merged-away member's
  open booking balances to the surviving member. Nothing reads the journal yet,
  so no screen, email, invoice or Xero document changes. Bookings confirmed
  before this release are not posted; a later step back-posts their history.
  `pnpm run booking-ledger:census` gains a `JOURNAL` check that the journal's
  charges add up to the booking-ledger lines it links, and lists any charge line
  left unlinked.
- **A booking card payment the app cannot match is no longer silent (#4624).**
  Rarely, a member's card is charged for a booking but the app cannot tie the
  payment to anything it was waiting for on that booking - for example a saved
  card charge whose answer from Stripe was lost. The app used to log it and move
  on, so the booking stayed unpaid, nothing reached Xero, and nobody was told.

  The app now keeps a record of each such payment and sends Finance editors one
  email per payment, "Booking card payment the app could not match - check it",
  naming the amount, the booking, what the app found and the Stripe payment,
  with a link to it in Stripe. It cannot be muted. The booking is not changed;
  the [Payments guide](docs/guides/payments.md#a-booking-card-payment-the-app-could-not-match)
  says what to do.
- **A card request the background retry set up just as a later booking change
  cancelled it is now withdrawn from Stripe (#4631).** When an extra card
  payment is retried in the background and a later change to the booking nets
  it off or folds it into a newer request at the same moment, the retry's own
  Stripe payment request used to stay open in the club's Stripe account,
  never offered to the member and never paid. It is now cancelled at Stripe,
  just as #4052 does for one set up by the booking change itself. No money
  moves and no operator action is needed.
- **A bank-transfer booking's charge now posts to the member-money journal when
  its invoice is issued, not when it is paid (Ledger M3c, #4628).** A booking
  made to be paid by internet banking (by a member, an officer on their behalf,
  or a group joiner who pays their own way), a switch to internet banking, a
  school request's pay-on-account approval, and a member whole-lodge request's
  pay-on-account approval (when the Xero and internet-banking modules are not
  both on) post the booking's charge into the built-in journal
  straight away, priced exactly as the booking's confirmation will later price
  it. Edits and cancellations before payment adjust that charge. When the
  payment is recorded (marked paid, or Xero reports the invoice paid), the
  booking-ledger lines it writes are linked to the charge already posted, so
  nothing is charged twice. A Xero "invoice paid" receipt now also writes the
  booking's confirmation lines on the booking ledger, as recording the payment
  by hand already did. Nothing reads the journal yet, so no screen, email,
  invoice or Xero document changes. `pnpm run booking-ledger:census` gains a
  `JOURNAL_PENDING` check comparing a bank-transfer booking's pending charge with
  its final price plus its recorded fees.
- **A booking paid entirely by credit, or at no charge, is now in the ledger when it is confirmed (#4660).**
  Creating that booking, or settling it on the pay step, marks it paid and posts its confirmation in the same step. The charge is in the journal without waiting for a later back-post. Doing it again does not post the charge a second time.
- **A change fee on a booking that is not yet paid is now charged (#4661).**
  When the dates of a booking not yet paid were moved, such as a bank-transfer
  booking whose invoice was still unpaid, the club's late-change fee was worked out but
  never added to what the member owed. The booking's history showed a fee,
  but the payment, the invoice and the booking ledger did not carry it.

  The fee is now added to the amount the member owes, once. An invoice raised
  later includes it; an invoice already sent gets a supplementary invoice for
  it; and when the booking is paid the ledger records the fee against the
  edit that charged it. Bookings already paid are unchanged: their fee was
  already collected by the edit itself.
- **Credit used elsewhere is now asked for straight away, even while a booking
  change is still unpaid.** When account credit applied to a booking turns out to
  have been used elsewhere in the club's accounts while the member still owes for a
  booking change, the two are now one payment request for the combined amount,
  emailed at once and worded as both, instead of the credit waiting until the
  change was paid. The member pays once by card, and the app records that payment
  in Xero against both invoices: the credit on the booking's own invoice, the change
  on its own invoice. Nothing is recorded twice, and nobody has to fix anything in
  Xero by hand. Where the change's Xero invoice cannot follow the merged request
  (for example it has already been sent), the credit still waits for the change to
  be paid or withdrawn, as before, and the officers are told why.
- **A card request for released credit that a stalled background retry set up
  is now withdrawn from Stripe once it can never be used (#4652).** When the
  background retry raising a card request for credit used in Xero stalled and
  another retry took over, the stalled one's Stripe payment request used to
  stay open in the club's Stripe account, never offered to the member and
  never paid. Once the retry that took over has finished without it, it is now
  cancelled at Stripe, as #4631 does for an extra card payment's retry, which
  now also covers a stalled retry that another one finished. A request that
  any record names is never cancelled. No money moves and no operator action
  is needed.
- **Groundwork for automatically matching a saved-card payment whose
  confirmation went missing (#4646).** If the app loses Stripe's answer to a
  saved-card charge and the card payment then completes a little later, the
  money is taken but the booking stays unpaid, and treasurers get a "could not
  match an app payment" alert to sort out by hand. This release teaches the app
  to recognise and match charges that tell Stripe which charge attempt they
  belong to. It does not yet send that information on new charges, because the
  previous version of the app, which can still be running during an upgrade or
  after a rollback, would not recognise those charges and could charge the card
  a second time. Until a follow-up release switches it on (#4682), such a
  payment still raises the alert, as before.
- **A saved-card charge whose answer is lost, and that completes later, is
  matched to the booking even when Stripe sends no request id (#4682).**
  The charge now tells Stripe which attempt it belongs to, so the later
  payment is recorded on that booking instead of sitting unmatched for a
  treasurer to sort out by hand. A charge an earlier release already started
  is unchanged, and still needs a person to match it.
- **A card payment request for money still owed is no longer lost when a
  stalled background retry wakes late (#4675).** A retry that had stalled long
  enough to be handed to another retry could still mark the job finished,
  so the second retry's payment request was dropped and the member was never
  asked for the money. A retry can now only finish a job it still holds.

  Nothing changes for operators. In the rare case a refund is made by a retry
  that had already been handed on, the member's "we refunded you" email and
  the admin alert for that refund are not sent; the refund itself is made and
  recorded as before.
- **The member-money journal can now record which debt a payment or refund
  pays, but nothing in the app uses that yet (#4691).** The release adds two
  empty tables for a refund reservation and its release, and checks that a
  payment is not applied for more than it is worth. No screen, charge, card
  payment, refund or Xero document changes, and no extra deploy step is
  required.
- **An unused card payment request is now cleaned up when its save fails
  partway, not only when it loses a race (#4676).** When the app asks a member
  to pay more by card, it first creates the payment at Stripe and then saves
  it. If the booking changed in between (a payment cleared, a price reduction
  was made, or the save itself failed), the save is undone and tried again
  later. Before this fix, the Stripe payment created for that attempt was never
  looked at again.

  The app now runs the same check it already runs after a lost race. If the
  request has since been closed without that payment, the payment is cancelled
  at Stripe. Members never saw it, so nothing changes for them. If the request
  is still open, the payment is left alone, because the retry may use it, and
  a `left-open` entry is logged so the club's operator can find it. Do not
  cancel such a payment by hand while its request is still open: a retry can
  ask Stripe for the same payment again and record it as the member's request.
  Retries happen as before.
- **An unused card payment request left open by a failed save is now cleaned
  up once its request ends (#4693).** When the app asks a member to pay more
  by card, it creates the payment at Stripe first and then saves it. If that
  save fails, the request is retried later, and the Stripe payment is kept in
  case the retry uses it. Before this fix, if the retry created a different
  payment instead, or a later price change cancelled or absorbed the request,
  or the request ran out of retries, the first payment stayed open at Stripe
  for good. Members never saw it and could not pay it.

  Now, when a request ends, the app looks at Stripe for the payments it made
  for that request and cancels any that nothing in the app uses. To find them
  it marks each payment it creates with the request it belongs to. Payments
  created before this release, and payments made outside a retry, carry no
  mark and are left alone. Nothing changes for members.
- **Booking-change refund retries account for refunds already made (#4713).**
  When a retry has no saved refund plan, it refreshes the recorded balance after
  checking Stripe, so a refund made through another route no longer causes an
  oversized request that wastes a retry.
- **A refund of a replaced payment no longer asks Stripe for money another
  refund already returned (#4699).** When a member pays a payment request the
  club had already replaced, the payment recovery queue refunds it. If another
  part of the system, such as a cancellation, had refunded some of that payment
  at Stripe but the app had not recorded it yet, the queue asked Stripe for the
  full amount. Stripe refused, and the attempt was retried later, using up one
  of the job's attempts. No money ever moved twice.

  The queue now records what Stripe has already refunded before it works out
  how much to refund, so it asks only for what is left. When nothing is left,
  it closes the job straight away.
- **A change fee on a card booking not yet paid is now charged (#4735).**
  When a card booking that was still waiting to be paid was edited before the
  member had opened its pay page, the club's change fee was shown in the
  booking's history but never added to what the member owed, so the member
  later paid only the price.

  The edit now records the fee against the booking straight away, and the pay
  page, the saved-card charge and the switch to bank transfer all ask for the
  price plus the fee, once. Opening the pay page again does not add the fee a
  second time.
- **A booking that costs nothing is now in the ledger when it is confirmed, whichever way it is confirmed (#4738).**
  Confirming a saved draft, accepting a waitlist offer, confirming pending guests, the overnight pending-confirm run and an admin force-confirm each mark a $0 booking paid and post its confirmation in the same step, as creating one already did. Doing it again does not post the charge a second time.
  Confirming a draft also re-checks, under the booking's locks, that it still costs nothing, so a draft priced by an edit made mid-confirm is refused rather than marked paid.
- **A second price increase no longer leaves out an earlier increase
  whose card request is still waiting to be retried (#4744).** When a
  price increase could not set up its card request (for example, during a
  card-provider outage) and the member changes the booking again before
  the retry runs, the new card request now includes that earlier increase.
  The member is asked once. The earlier retry is closed, and its Xero
  invoice, if one was waiting, is collected with the new card request. If
  that retry is in the middle of being set up, the edit is refused for a
  moment and can be saved again straight away. Otherwise no operator
  action is needed.
- **An extra card payment waiting on a retry is no longer lost when the
  booking changes again (#4015).** When a price increase's extra card request
  could not be set up at once, it waits for an automatic retry. If another
  increase was saved before that retry ran, the retry treated the first
  increase as already covered and asked for nothing, so the club was short
  that amount. The retry now asks for its own increase plus whatever the later
  request still has unpaid, and replaces that request. The member is left with
  one card request for the full amount owed. A price reduction saved in the
  meantime now sets itself against that waiting increase too. If Stripe shows
  the later request as paid or still processing, the retry waits for that
  payment to be recorded rather than cancelling it, for up to seven days
  after that payment began. If it is still not recorded by then, the retry
  stops and officers are alerted
  to check the payment in Stripe and collect the change by hand. A member
  part-way through a card security check on the later request when the retry
  runs is asked to pay the new request instead. A retry whose change already
  has its card request on record finishes with that request rather than
  asking a second time. Otherwise no operator action is needed.
- Record booking card, bank and officer receipts beside their existing writes,
  preserving full cash and explicitly applying only the selected receipt.
  Officer reversals restore the original receipt exactly; member merges retain
  charge obligations through successors. Add a dry-run-first receipt catch-up
  and census before the card-refund journal rollout. Existing payment screens,
  provider requests and legacy decision figures continue to use their current rules.
- Record card refunds in the member-money journal. Each card refund the app
  owes (a cancellation, an edit, an approved appeal, an edit review, a duplicate
  or late capture) is recorded as a debt, each card refund slice is reserved
  against it before Stripe is asked, and each refund Stripe records pays that
  debt only through its own reservation; a refund that fails later reopens it.
  A refund the journal would over-pay is not sent and lands on the stuck-states
  list for the treasurer. Closing a card refund as paid another way in part
  now asks whether the club keeps the rest or it is still owed to the member;
  a rest still owed stays in "Refunds owed" until a later close, and the
  member's booking page and payment link say both what was paid back and that
  the rest is still being refunded. A dry-run-first
  owner command lists and reconciles reservations. Stripe requests are unchanged.
- **Approving the refund of a held late card payment can no longer refund it a
  second time (#4824).** If a refund of that payment was recorded - for
  example Stripe reporting one made in its dashboard - while a treasurer was
  approving it, the approval could miss it and owe the member the same money
  again. The approval now checks what is left on the payment only once nothing
  else can change it, and refuses when it was already refunded; the item stays
  open to be dismissed with a note.
- **Marking a late card payment as paid back by hand can no longer count a
  Stripe refund of it twice (#4838).** If a refund of that payment was
  recorded - for example Stripe reporting one made in its dashboard - while an
  officer was marking it paid back by hand, the app could miss the refund and
  record the hand-back against the booking's other money as well, so the
  booking showed more returned than the member got. The check now runs only
  once nothing else can change the payment, and refuses when it was already
  refunded; the item stays open to be dismissed with a note.
- **Recording a cash payment no longer risks deadlocking with a member merge
  (#4840).** If an officer recorded a cash payment while their own duplicate
  record was being merged, and the booking named that duplicate, the two could
  wait on each other until the database cancelled one of them.

  The payment now locks its booking before it records who took the cash. If
  the merge finishes first, the payment is not recorded and the officer
  records it again from their surviving record.
- **An older late card payment item can no longer be marked paid back by hand
  after Stripe already refunded it (#4843).** Items about a card payment taken
  after its booking was deleted, raised before 19 August 2026, skipped the
  check that refuses a hand-back once the payment was refunded, so the booking
  could show more returned than the member got. They now get the same check
  as newer items; an item that was already refunded stays open to be dismissed
  with a note.
- **The booking-ledger census now names an old late card charge the same way
  as one that already has a type (#4848).** Charges raised before 19 August
  2026 have no type. `pnpm run booking-ledger:census` only recognised a
  completed late charge that already had the type, so an older one on a
  deleted booking was an unexplained difference. It is now named
  `V3_LEGACY_HAND_BACK` when its wording is one of the frozen late-charge
  sentences, the same rule the refund check uses. A cancellation refund on a
  booking deleted later is still not that class. The census reads only; no
  money moves. A booking this newly names still needs the same sign-off as
  the other old late charges before the ledger switch-over.
- **Card refunds Stripe gave up on can be tried on the card again, or closed when nothing is left owed (#4368).**
  On **Stuck States**, each card refund under **Card refunds Stripe gave up
  on** now offers **Try the card again** beside **Paid another way**. After a
  confirm dialog the app puts the refund back to its automatic retries; before
  anything is sent it reads the refunds Stripe already holds on the charge, so
  one it can match is counted rather than sent again, and one made in the
  Stripe dashboard stops it again for you to check. Where the app cannot show
  that asking again would not pay the member twice - a refund Stripe failed
  later is on the same payment, the last failure suggests Stripe may have
  refunded after all, or Stripe holds an older refund of this one's it cannot
  match - the row says why, or the request is refused with the reason, and
  **Paid another way** remains.

  A refund that Stripe refunds matched to it have paid in full now stays on the
  list, reads "nothing left owed" and offers **Nothing left owed**: its dialog
  names those Stripe refunds, and closing it moves no money, sends nothing to
  Stripe and changes nothing in Xero. Before, such a refund dropped off the list and
  needed a developer.

  The guidance on the page, in the Stuck States guide and in the officers'
  emails about refunds Stripe failed later now says to settle a refund Stripe
  gave up on here - never with a new refund in the Stripe dashboard, which on
  a booking paid by bank transfer is credited in Xero twice. The old advice to
  refund in the dashboard and wait for it to show is gone. Both new buttons
  need **Finance edit**, and are view-only without it, as **Paid another way**
  is. Both are recorded in the audit log under **Payment**, read with Support view
  and Finance view (two more audit write sites, 536 to 538).
- **An old cancellation refund owed by hand now shows as a refund owed, not as
  a late card charge, after its booking is deleted (#4848).** Refund items
  raised before 19 August 2026 carry no type. One whose booking was later
  deleted was counted in Net Collected and "Refunds owed" as a late card
  charge awaiting the treasurer, though it was a cancellation refund owed by
  hand. The amounts were right and only the line was wrong. Old items are now
  told apart by what they say they are about, the same rule the refund check
  uses since #4843.
- **A refund of a superseded card payment stops for an officer rather than
  risk paying the member twice (#4858).** When a member is refunded a card
  payment the app no longer needed, and a booking change's card refund has
  since gone through first time on part of the same card charge, the app used
  to send only the rest. If that other refund later failed, the app could owe
  it twice: once as that refund again and once more on this one. It now sends
  nothing, stops retrying and lists the refund under **Card refunds Stripe gave
  up on** in Stuck States, with the officers' email naming the other refund.
  Check the booking and the Stripe refunds, then settle anything still owed
  with **Paid another way** - unless the refund it names has since failed and
  shows as a refund of its own that Stripe failed later. Then do not close it
  that way: the two may be the same money, so ask a developer (#4492).
- **A cancellation no longer refunds a superseded card payment's money as the
  booking's own (#4866).** When a member paid a card request the app had
  already replaced, the app refunds that payment in full on its own. If the
  booking was cancelled before that refund went out, the cancellation could
  refund part of the same card charge for the booking, and the superseded
  payment's refund then sent only what was left: the member got back less than
  they were owed, and no officer was told. Where the booking's own payments did
  not reach its price, the cancellation policy was also applied to the
  superseded payment as if it had been paid for the booking. A cancellation now
  leaves that payment to its own refund: it is not counted as paid for the
  booking, and the cancellation's card refund, or its refund as account
  credit, comes from the booking's other payments. The same holds while the
  superseded payment's refund is being sent again after Stripe failed it, and
  when an earlier credit note is attributed to the payment's card charges at
  the cancellation. The cancellation preview shows the same figures.
- **Edits, approved refunds, capacity races, booking-change credits, recovery
  retries and manual hand-backs no longer spend a superseded card payment's
  money (#4872).** When a replaced card payment is captured anyway, the app
  queues its own refund for that charge. Another refund could take part of the
  same charge first, and the superseded refund then sent only what was left:
  the member was paid back less than they were owed, and no officer was told.
  Those refunds now leave the charge to its own refund. An edit's card plan is
  frozen under the payment's row before Stripe is asked. A refund an officer
  approves is capped without that money. A booking that lost its beds refunds
  the capture that just arrived, not the superseded one. A price cut paid back
  as account credit, a refund row that still has to work out its plan, and a
  hand-back an officer marks paid - including the part of a cancellation refund
  that has to be checked - do the same. A plan already frozen is left as it was.
  The refund appeal form and the officers' appeal list offer that same lower
  ceiling, so an appeal is never invited for money the approval would refuse.
- **Group organiser card refunds Stripe gave up on can now be settled on Stuck States (#4851).**
  A refund out of a group organiser's card that Stripe gave up on, for one
  joiner or an older refund of a whole group's payment, now appears under
  **Card refunds Stripe gave up on**. **Paid another way** reads Stripe first:
  if Stripe already has the refund, it is recorded and nobody is paid again;
  otherwise the bank payment is recorded and officers are emailed to credit the
  group's invoice in Xero by hand. A joiner's refund can also use **Try the card
  again**, which never sends a refund Stripe already holds. No developer or
  Stripe dashboard refund is needed.
- Cancelled bookings return their promo-code uses in the cancellation transaction, including expired bank-payment holds and capacity cancellations. Repair historical uses left on cancelled bookings.
- **The card payment screen shows the actual charge and explains saved credit (#4943).** The total and success message now use the server's card amount after credit. Members see how much saved credit was applied, why less was used when circumstances changed, and when credit covered the booking in full.
- **Switching a card booking to internet banking now asks first.** Tapping
  **Pay by internet banking instead** on an unpaid booking opens a confirm
  dialog that says an invoice will be emailed and the member cannot switch back
  to paying by card from the booking page. Choosing **Keep paying by card**
  changes nothing. The dialog's wording is club-editable under Booking Detail
  (**Confirm switch to Internet Banking**, with its own version for an approved
  whole-lodge booking) (#4958).
- **The configuration guide now explains that the money journal is active (#4912).** Booking charges and payment receipts are already recorded, and a refused journal entry stops the change. The guide clarifies that clubs currently use the default GST-inclusive 15% treatment until the tax settings screen is available. No charges or payment behaviour changed.
- **Failed cancellations no longer claim account credit was given (#4913).** The credit history now saves with the cancellation. If the cancellation fails, its credit note is rolled back too, so a retry or later manual refund shows the correct outcome.
- **Card disputes (chargebacks) are now recorded, alerted and guarded.** The Stripe webhook handles `charge.dispute.created`, `charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn`, `charge.dispute.funds_reinstated` and `charge.dispute.closed`, keeping one record per dispute. Finance editors get one email when a dispute opens and one when it closes. While a dispute is open or lost, the app issues no card refund for that payment, and cancelling the booking issues no account credit either: it records the cancel, raises a treasurer task naming the dispute, and tells the member the refund is with the treasurer. The booking page and **Finance → Payments** show "Disputed by cardholder" with its outcome. Nothing is posted to Xero for a dispute; `DEPLOYMENT.md` describes recording a lost dispute by hand. Existing deployments must add the four events to their Stripe webhook endpoint once the new release alone serves (see the upgrade note in `DEPLOYMENT.md`).
- **The emailed payment link now confirms a payment made through a bank or
  pay-later page (#4955).** Some payment methods send the payer to another site
  to approve the payment and then back to the link. On their return the page
  used to show "Amount due" and "Pay by card" again until Stripe told the club's
  server about the payment, so the payer could not tell whether it had worked.

  The page now says "Checking your payment..." and asks the server what the
  payment did, then shows the paid page or the right next step. A payment
  declined or cancelled at the provider shows "Your payment did not go
  through. You have not been charged." beside the usual pay options. Nothing
  about how money is taken or settled has changed.
- **The dashboard's Payment Owed card now shows what the booking page asks you
  to pay** (#4944). It used to add up each unpaid booking's full price, so a
  member who had applied account credit, or whose booking carried a recorded
  change fee, saw a different figure on the dashboard from the booking's Amount
  due. The total, the "N bookings need payment" count and the link now read the
  same figure as the booking page: the price plus any recorded change fee, less
  the credit already applied. A booking its credit fully covers is no longer
  counted. What is charged is unchanged.
- **A card refund from a booking edit is no longer lost if the server restarts at the wrong moment** (#4992). Shortening a stay, removing a guest, a batch edit that lowers the price, or a guest's acceptance that re-prices a booking down used to save the edit first and record the card refund as owed only if Stripe then refused or failed. A restart between the two left the lower price with no refund and nothing in **Refunds owed**. The edit now records the refund as owed in the same save, with the exact slices it will ask Stripe for, then makes the refund and marks it done. If the server stops in between, the payment recovery job finishes the same refund under the same Stripe request, so it is made once. What Stripe is sent, and what the member's email says, are unchanged.
- **The booking page, the booking wizard, additional payments and group
  settlement now confirm a payment made through a bank or pay-later page.**
  The emailed payment link already did this (#4955). On every other card
  payment, a payer sent to a provider's site and back used to see the payment
  form again, or on a draft booking the "Continue to Payment" step, with
  nothing to say whether the payment had worked.

  Each of these now says "Checking your payment..." and asks the club's server
  what the payment did. It then shows the paid state, "This payment is being
  processed" for a payment the bank is still clearing, or the right recovery
  message. A payment the payer declined or cancelled at the provider shows
  "Your payment did not go through. You have not been charged." next to the
  form. A payment still processing after an in-page confirmation is also
  described that way instead of the form being shown again. Nothing about how
  money is taken or settled has changed.
- **A card refund still owed now reads the same every time when two records
  share a timestamp (#4284).** When two card refunds were raised, or two
  refunds recorded, in the same instant, "Refunds owed", Net Collected and the
  Xero "paid twice" alert could match a refund to a different one of them from
  one page load to the next - and on one read call a refund still being sent
  as already paid. They are now always matched in one fixed order.
- **Moving the dates of a booking that has not been paid no longer adds a late-notice fee to what the member owes.**
  The stay is still repriced. A booking that has already been paid is unchanged: a later change of its dates is still charged the fee the club's policy sets.
- **A card payment under the Stripe minimum now says why it can't go through.** When a booking owes more than $0 but less than 50 hundredths of the club's currency, **Pay** on the booking page and the public payment link now say the amount is too small to pay by card, that nothing was charged, and to contact the club, instead of the generic "We couldn't start the card payment" error. The refusal happens before Stripe is called, so no customer lookup or payment is created. Amounts of 50 and above are unchanged.
- **Charging a saved card or settling a group by card now says when the amount is too small.** An amount above $0 but under 50 hundredths of the club's currency used to fail with a generic error. Before it failed, a saved-card charge had already claimed the booking and sent admins a payment-failure alert. Charging a booking's saved card now answers that no card was charged because the amount is below the smallest card charge, and to settle it another way. It does this before claiming the booking, recording a charge attempt or calling Stripe, and sends no failure alert. Settling an organiser-pays group by card gives the organiser the same "too small to pay by card" message as **Pay**, before any joiner's booking is confirmed or Stripe is called. Amounts of 50 and above are unchanged.
- **Stripe setup no longer gets stuck after the app's auth secret changes.** When only the stored webhook signing secret could no longer be read, **Admin → Stripe → Setup** kept warning on **Enter keys** and kept **Continue** disabled even after both keys were re-entered, so the **Webhook** step, the only place to replace that secret, could not be reached. Each step now warns about and waits on only the credential it asks for: **Enter keys** for the secret and publishable keys, and **Webhook** for the signing secret, which now says it needs pasting again. The connected-account check also runs when only the signing secret is unreadable.

### Membership

- **Finding the right parent again: the Link Parent search lists adults first,
  and says when it ran out of room (#2425).** Recording a parent of any age was
  the right call - a 16 or 17 year old can genuinely be a parent - but it had a
  consequence nobody meant. The search shows eight people at a time, ordered by
  surname then first name, so a family who all share a surname could put their
  **children in all eight slots** and leave the adult the admin was actually
  looking for off the list entirely, with nothing on screen to say the list had
  been cut short. On a big family, the parent was simply unreachable.

  The list now puts **the grown-ups at the top and children and youth last**.
  This changes the ORDER and nothing else: exactly the same people are offered as
  before - any active, non-archived member of any age who is not an organisation
  or school account - and the younger candidates follow immediately below. Adults
  come first, and so does a member whose membership type makes them age-exempt
  (an honorary or life member, who carries no age tier at all): they are
  grown-ups too, and sorting them in among the children would have left the
  problem unfixed for the very families it was reported on. The dialog now says
  so ("adults are listed first, children and youth last"), so the order does not
  read as a fault. Who may be recorded as a parent, and who the club emails about
  a dependent (always an adult), are both completely unchanged.

  When more people matched than the list can show, it now says **"Keep typing to
  narrow this down."** underneath - the same sentence the booking screens use
  when a member search is cut short, so the product says one thing in one voice.
  The hint appears only when the list really was truncated, never under a
  complete one, and never when nothing matched at all.
- **A member merge that is overtaken mid-merge now stops cleanly instead of
  failing with an unexplained error (#2243).** Merging two member profiles runs
  as one long transaction, and it used to work out what to copy onto the
  surviving record the moment that transaction opened, then write it much later.
  A member photo can be uploaded at any time without waiting for a merge to
  finish, so an on-behalf photo upload landing in that gap left the merge writing
  a photo reference that had already been deleted - the database refused it and
  the whole merge rolled back as an unexplained error, with nothing in the
  operator's preview to hint at why. The merge now re-checks what it is about to
  copy just before it writes, covering every field it copies rather than photos
  alone (the duplicate's family group is the other one that could fail the same
  way), and locks both member records for that final step. If anything did change
  in the meantime, the merge stops with a clear message naming what changed,
  saves nothing, and asks the operator to re-run the preview - so what was
  previewed is always exactly what gets applied. Nothing changes for an ordinary
  merge. Two smaller corrections ride along: where a booking request was already
  turned into a booking for the duplicate, that link now follows the surviving
  member (it previously kept pointing at the deleted record); and the safety net
  that stops a new member-referencing column being forgotten by a merge now also
  covers columns that hold a member id without a database foreign key - two
  calendar columns had slipped past it - with a test that fails on the next one.
- **A young member can now be recorded as a parent (#2282).** A 16 or 17 year
  old can genuinely be a parent, and until now the club simply could not write
  that down: adding a dependant refused with "Dependants can only be linked
  under active adult members", and the search never offered a non-adult, so the
  only options were to leave the child looking parentless or to attach them to a
  grandparent. Both record the wrong thing. **The family relationship can now be
  recorded at any age.**
  **Nothing about responsibility has moved.** Being someone's recorded parent
  never granted the powers people assume it does - booking on another member's
  behalf, editing or confirming their details, answering a consent request for
  them, and billing are all decided by family-group membership plus being an
  active adult with a login, and none of them looks at the parent link at all.
  Those rules are untouched. In particular the club's **contact of record** for
  a child's mail is still an adult: a dependant added under a young parent has
  their notifications routed on up to the nearest adult in the family, usually
  the young parent's own parent, and the member's page now says on screen which
  adult that is *before* you add the dependant. The two "link" dialogs say it
  too, next to the notification-recipient list - that list names *parents*, and
  the person the mail actually reaches can be someone further up, which the
  screen used not to mention. If no adult in the family has a real email
  address, adding the dependant is refused with that reason rather than quietly
  leaving the child unreachable.
  **Organisation and school accounts are not people**, so they cannot be
  recorded as anyone's parent - they were never offered before, and are not
  offered now.
  **The dead ends are gone too.** "Add Dependent" used to disappear entirely on
  a member who could not have one, teaching an admin nothing; on an inactive or
  archived member it stayed and then failed on save. It is now always shown, and
  disabled with the reason - "This member is inactive - reactivate them to add
  dependents" - on both the *create new* and *link existing* paths, with the
  reason read out to screen readers alongside the control rather than merely
  sitting beside it. Where a dependant genuinely cannot be added because no
  adult in the family can receive club email, the dialog now says so *and*
  points at the way that does work, instead of letting the save fail. And the
  copy that claimed only adults can manage dependants is gone, because that is
  no longer the rule.
  Two smaller corrections ride along: the age-up job's "your child is becoming
  an adult" notice now goes to the family's actual contact of record instead of
  whoever the parent link names, and creating a member under a parent without
  asking for inherited email no longer records them as inheriting from nobody.
- **A refused save no longer blames the email address when the email address is
  not the problem, and switching a family's login holder now explains an email
  clash (#2385).** Only one member per email address can sign in - that is why a
  family's children can share a parent's address as long as they do not log in
  themselves. Three changes, all about being told the truth when a save is
  refused:

  - On a member's **Account & Access** tab, ticking **Can Login** when that
    member's address is already someone else's login is now spotted before the
    save is attempted rather than by letting the database reject it. Admins see
    the same message as before - "A member with this email already exists" - so
    nothing looks different; the save simply stops earlier.
  - What *has* changed is what a member save says when the database refuses it
    because two records would end up sharing something that has to be unique to
    one of them. Whatever the duplicated detail actually was, that used to be
    reported as an email clash. Only a genuine email clash says so now;
    anything else is reported as a general failure and recorded in the logs for
    an administrator to look at. Nobody is sent off to fix an address that was
    never wrong.
  - On a family group's **Shared email & login** panel, handing the login to a
    different adult when someone **outside that family** already signs in with
    the address used to fail with an unexplained error. It now says "A member
    with this email already exists", and the same message is given to whichever
    of two admins loses a race to claim the address at the same moment.

  Nothing about who is allowed to sign in has changed - the database rule that
  permits only one login per address was always doing its job, and still is.
- **Clubs can safely record a trusted induction history when moving an
  established membership onto the digital register (#2361).** A new
  dry-run-first operator command classifies every active real-member
  (`USER`/`ADMIN`) record across the configured Infant, Child, Youth, and Adult
  tiers, includes non-login dependants, excludes operational and non-member
  contacts, reports an in-scope `N/A` separately, and preserves anyone who
  already has a completed induction of any kind. Apply needs a login-enabled
  Full Admin actor, one New Zealand baseline date, stable source provenance,
  and exact club, database, and reviewed SHA-256 plan-digest confirmations.
  Apply rebuilds the complete safe plan under its table lock and rejects stale
  digests before blocker, no-op, or write handling. It refuses to run
  over an open induction, locks direct induction-table writes during apply, and
  commits all completed New Member baseline rows with one audit event or none
  at all. The runbook requires a short member-population, induction, and
  configuration, group-join member-creation, and actor-access freeze from the
  final dry run through post-apply verification because the table lock does not
  freeze those inputs.
  The records are explicit Admin Overrides with no invented signers, sign-offs,
  emails, or hut-leader eligibility; a fresh post-apply dry-run digest permits
  an identical no-op rerun while the stale pre-apply digest fails closed. The new
  operator runbook documents rehearsal, review, verification, and recovery.
- **A member's membership can now be cancelled without first destroying their
  admin access, and school and organisation accounts can be cancelled at all
  (#2383).** The old rule claimed to allow "only member accounts", but what it
  actually tested was whether the account held the full admin bundle - so a
  Membership Officer, Booking Officer, Treasurer, Content Manager or holder of
  a club-defined custom role was cancellable all along, and only a Full Admin
  was refused. That refusal had no way out worth using: to cancel a Full
  Admin's membership you first had to strip their access, which throws away
  every privileged role they held and cannot be given back from the member page
  afterwards, because a cancelled member cannot be reactivated there. Worse,
  nobody can strip their own access, so a departing sole admin could not cancel
  their own membership by any route at all. The same rule also refused school
  and organisation accounts, which hold real fee-paying memberships and had no
  cancellation path whatsoever. Cancellation now asks the only question that
  matters - is there an account holder here with a membership? - so every
  member is cancellable whatever admin access they hold, as is every
  organisation account. Two kinds of record are still refused, because they are
  not people and hold no membership: the lodge kiosk device login, and the
  contact records the booking-request flows create (a public request's guest
  contact, and a school request's owner contact and teacher records). Those
  simply show no cancellation action, with nothing to explain, because nothing
  is being withheld. "The lodge kiosk" here means the shared device account
  itself - the one whose account type reads *Lodge (kiosk account)* - and not
  anyone who has merely been given the lodge role alongside their own: a
  booking officer who also runs the lodge screen is a person with a membership,
  and was quietly losing the cancellation action too. The safeguards that
  matter sit where the decision is actually made, at approval: only a full admin
  may approve a cancellation for an account with admin access, an admin can
  never approve a cancellation they raised themselves, and the club can never be
  left with no full admin - so a sole admin who wants to leave must appoint
  their successor first, and then that successor approves. The review queue now
  says what it is you are approving, marking a participant who holds admin
  access or is an organisation account - "cancel the treasurer" and "cancel an
  ordinary member" used to look identical there - and an approval is refused
  outright if the admin who raised the request has since been deleted, since
  the club can no longer tell that it is a second pair of eyes. Cancelling a
  member no longer needs their roles deleted, so the record of what they once
  did for the club stays intact; the flip side, now written down, is that the
  club cannot delete such a record outright until the roles are removed, and
  that nothing may quietly un-cancel a membership. Related hardening found
  while checking this: the lobby-display preview endpoint now re-checks that the
  admin previewing it still has an active account, which every other admin
  endpoint already did. The member-facing **Membership Cancellation** panel in a
  member's own profile follows the same rule - see the next entry.
- **A full admin, and an organisation account, can now start a cancellation
  from their own profile (#2391).** The **Membership Cancellation** panel in a
  member's profile asked a narrower question than the member page did, and it
  turned away exactly the two kinds of account the member page used to turn away
  before the entry above fixed it: a **Full Admin**, and an **organisation or
  school account**. A departing full admin was told to ring the office; an
  organisation was told the same and had no self-service route at all.
  Committee members were never affected - a Membership Officer, Booking Officer,
  Treasurer, Content Manager or holder of a club-defined custom role keeps an
  ordinary member account underneath their access, so they were always offered
  the panel and always appeared in a relative's family list. Family lists had
  the matching gap for the two classes that were refused: a relative who is a
  full admin, and an organisation sharing a family group, were simply missing
  from the list of memberships you could include, with no reason shown, so it
  looked as though they held no membership at all. The profile panel now asks
  exactly the question the member page asks: is there an account holder here
  with a membership? So a full admin can start their own cancellation, an
  organisation can start its own, and a relative who is a full admin appears in
  the family list and can be included. Two conditions remain, and both are about
  being able to use your own profile rather than about what kind of account it
  is: the account must be active, and it must have its own login. A member with
  no login of their own - most family dependants - is still cancelled either by a
  relative including them in a family request or by an admin from their member
  page, and the refusal now says that instead of implying they are not a proper
  member. The lodge kiosk login and the contact records created by booking
  requests are refused here as everywhere else, because they hold no membership,
  and if one ever appears in a family list it now says so rather than vanishing.
  Nothing about approval changed: whoever raises a cancellation, a *different*
  admin must approve it, and the club can still never be left with no full
  admin - so a sole full admin who starts their own departure from their profile
  must appoint a successor before anyone can approve it.
- **Admins can now cancel the membership of a member who has no login of
  their own (#2354).** Opening such a member's admin page used to show no
  **Request Cancellation** action at all - not greyed out, simply absent -
  so their membership looked uncancellable. Most family dependants are in
  exactly this position, as is any adult the club records without giving
  them a login. The cause was the page borrowing a permissions test to
  decide who is cancellable: a member without a login holds no permissions
  by design, so the test always failed for them, while the cancellation
  machinery behind it has always accepted them - an admin-raised request
  is confirmed on the member's behalf and goes straight to the review
  queue, exactly as it does for anyone else. The page now asks the same
  eligibility question the server enforces - is this an active,
  not-yet-cancelled, not-archived member - so the action appears for
  exactly the members it can act on. That question was later widened by
  #2383 above.
- **A member's admin page now draws the whole family as a read-only tree
  (#2253).** In the Family section - under the family-group chips, above the
  billing family and parent link cards - the page works out how everyone
  connects from the links the club has already recorded (parents, second
  parents, confirmed partners) and follows them across households, so
  grandparents, siblings, half-siblings, cousins, and a dependant's other
  parent all appear, each drawn once. It reaches three generations above and
  below the member being viewed (four counting the member's own), the same
  limit parent links themselves are capped at. Relationships that are not
  stored anywhere are marked **Derived** with a dashed outline, so a worked-out
  sibling is never mistaken for a recorded claim - and half-siblings are
  separated from full siblings by *which* parents are shared, not how many,
  with the tree saying plainly when that verdict comes from a missing record
  rather than a different parentage. Where a child's club email goes to someone
  further up the family than their own parent, the tree says so in words and
  names the person - unless the mailbox belongs to a member outside the family
  altogether, which it reports without naming anyone. Archived relatives stay
  in the tree, badged, with their contact details left off, rather than
  silently vanishing and making a grandparent look unrelated. Where a family is
  too tall or simply too large to draw in full, the tree says which, instead of
  quietly ending. Nothing in the tree can be edited: it is a picture of the
  Parent Links, Partner, and Dependents cards below it, and changing those
  changes the tree.
- **Families can now be recorded across four generations, not two (#2255).**
  A member who already had dependants could not be recorded as anyone's child,
  so a grandparent, parent and child could not all be linked in one line - the
  club had to leave a real relationship unrecorded. Parent links now run up to
  **four generations** (great-grandparent, grandparent, parent, child), still
  with at most two parents each. The limit is checked when a link is made, from
  both ends at once, so it no longer depends on the order the links happened to
  be created in - which is worth saying plainly, because the old "two
  generations" rule did depend on it: it refused to attach a member who had
  dependants, but never looked at the parent's own parents, so a longer chain
  could be built downwards one person at a time and nothing stopped it. Every
  place that creates a parent link now enforces the limit, including admin
  member-create, family-group child requests, membership-application approval,
  and **merging two duplicate member records** - four paths the old rule never
  covered at all. (Merging is the surprising one: it never creates a link, but
  joining two records joins their families, which could produce a six-generation
  chain or link a family back on itself. Such a merge is now refused, and asks
  you to unlink first.) A link that would make the chain longer, or that would
  loop a family back on itself, is refused with an explanation naming the limit.
  **Where club email goes** follows the family further too: if a dependent
  inherits their parent's email address and that parent has no real address of
  their own, the club now uses the nearest person above them who does, instead
  of leaving that generation's children unreachable. Both the member's admin
  page and the family's own profile page say whose address is being used when it
  comes from beyond the direct parent, since that is the family whose consent is
  at stake. When a young member reaches adult age and gets their own login,
  their children's notifications now follow them instead of staying with the
  grandparent. **Removing a member** - cancelling, archiving, approving an
  account deletion, or hard-deleting the record - now tells you what it
  detached: their own dependants are
  left without a parent link (they are deliberately not moved up to a
  grandparent, because who is responsible for a member is not something to
  change automatically), and both they and anyone who was receiving email at the
  removed member's address are listed on screen and in the audit log. Approving
  a deletion also stops club email being sent to the anonymised address, which
  it previously kept attempting forever. Who is **billed** is unchanged by the
  link rules themselves: parent links record responsibility and grant no fee
  coverage, which comes from family groups and membership types as before. There
  is one indirect route worth knowing about, though - approvals that add someone
  to a family GROUP still change that group's composition, and group composition
  is a fee-model input, so an approval that was previously refused can now
  compose a group the fee rules classify as a Family.
- **Recording a membership payment by hand now asks whether to tell the member -
  and can actually tell them (#2260).** When a treasurer marks a member's
  subscription paid for a cash, cheque or internet-banking payment, the club
  had no way to send that member any acknowledgement: the action wrote the
  status and emailed nobody, ever. It now offers the club's usual choice.
  "Mark paid and email member" sends a short receipt - the season, the amount
  (only where the club has a recorded fee amount for that season), and the date
  it was recorded. "Mark paid without emailing" records the identical payment
  and tells nobody. The subscription is marked paid either way, and which way
  the treasurer chose is written to the audit log, so a later "did we tell
  them?" has an answer. Because a manual payment is cash the system never saw,
  the receipt never invents a figure: it shows an amount only where the club has
  one recorded for that member alone, and leaves it out otherwise. A family
  membership fee is deliberately left out - that figure is the whole family's
  bill, and telling one member it was recorded against them (with "nothing
  further to pay") while their relatives still owe theirs would be worse than
  saying nothing. It mentions no invoice, no payment link and no Xero
  reference, because manual mark-paid only exists where there is no invoice.
  The message the treasurer gets back says what actually happened rather than
  what was asked for: a receipt "is being emailed" only if it really was handed
  over for sending, and there is a plain "the receipt could not be sent" when
  the member's address cannot receive it. The payment stays recorded either
  way - a failed email never quietly undoes it.
  Reversing a manual payment never emails the member - there is no
  "your payment was un-recorded" notice worth sending.
  The confirmation itself is now a proper dialog with a note box, replacing the
  three bare browser pop-ups this action used to rely on (including the one
  where cancelling the note prompt silently abandoned the whole action).
- **Family groups: pressing the edit (pencil) icon on a group - or New
  Group - used to look like it had done nothing (#2256).** Both forms open in
  the same place: below the search bar and the two queue cards, and *above* the
  list of groups. So if you scrolled down to a group and clicked edit, the
  editor opened off the top of the screen; and with a busy queue, New Group
  opened the form well below the button you had just pressed. Either way
  nothing you could see changed. The page now scrolls to the form and puts the
  keyboard cursor in it every time it is opened - including when you re-open
  the same group you were just editing, which previously did nothing at all.
  The group you are editing is highlighted in the list and badged "Editing"
  until you save or close, and closing puts the keyboard cursor back on the
  button you started from. Nothing about who may edit a group has changed.
- **"Add Dependant → Link Existing" now finds the members it was hiding, and
  says why when it still finds nobody (#2254).** Searching for an existing
  member to link as a dependant reported "No eligible members found" for almost
  everybody: the search silently dropped every member who had no parent recorded -
  the overwhelming majority of valid candidates - so admins could not link an
  existing member at all without first giving them an unrelated parent. The
  search now returns those members. When a search genuinely has no one to offer,
  the dialog no longer stops at a bare "not found": it lists the members whose
  names matched and the reason each cannot be linked ("already has two parents
  recorded", "is archived", "is already linked to this member"), and only says
  "No members matched your search" when nobody matched at all. The search and
  the save step are now driven by one shared rule, so the dialog can no longer
  offer a member that saving then refuses, nor hide one that saving would have
  accepted. Who may be linked was unchanged by this fix - at most two parents, no
  linking someone who already has dependants of their own, no archived members -
  and inactive members remain linkable, badged "Inactive", as before. (The
  "already has dependants" part of that was then replaced in the same release by
  the four-generation limit above, which also added a "would make the family
  chain more than 4 generations deep" reason to the same list.)
- **Clearer, kinder handling of what one adult can do for another in a family
  group (#2284).** Every adult with a login in a family group has always been
  able to act for the members who cannot speak for themselves - book them, edit
  their details, request their membership be cancelled. That model is deliberate
  for a club of small, trusting families, and it stays; this change records it as
  a decision and adds four protections for the non-login members it affects.

  - **Members are now told when a family member adds them to a booking.** If you
    have your own login the heads-up comes to you; if you do not (a child, or an
    adult on a household login) the adults in your family group are told on your
    behalf. It is a courtesy notice, not a request - nothing waits on a reply -
    and it is the missing half of being able to take yourself off a booking
    someone else put you on: you can only do that if you know you are on it. It
    is sent whether or not the club uses the member-guest feature, and every
    member can switch it off under **Notification preferences** in their profile.

  - **A membership-cancellation request now flags a member who could not
    confirm it themselves.** When someone asks to cancel the membership of a
    family member who has no login, the reviewing administrator sees an explicit
    "included without their own or a second adult's confirmation" note on that
    person's row, so an on-their-behalf confirmation is never mistaken for one
    the member personally gave. The request still only takes effect on admin
    approval.

  - **A delegated edit to a member's details is now visible to the family.**
    Where an adult completes or confirms another member's details, the family
    page shows a read-only "Details last confirmed by ⟨name⟩ on ⟨date⟩" line, so
    a change made on someone's behalf is no longer only in the audit log.

  - **Tidied up an unused "group admin" role that quietly controlled one thing.**
    A little-known one-step way to declare a partner for a non-login adult used
    to depend on an internal family-group "admin" marker that was assigned more
    or less at random depending on how the group was created. It now depends on
    who actually confirmed that member's details, which is a real relationship
    rather than an accident. Relatedly, asking to join a member's family group no
    longer quietly sets them up as the group's "admin" before they have agreed to
    anything.
- **Merging two duplicate member records no longer quietly discards a family
  link saved while the merge is running (#2437).** Family links - who a
  member's parent or second parent is, whose email address they share, and who
  confirmed their details - can be edited by one admin at the same moment
  another admin is merging that member. The merge used to finish anyway: the
  just-saved link still pointed at the duplicate record, the duplicate was
  deleted moments later, and the link vanished with it - no error, no warning,
  and nothing in the audit trail.

  The merge now notices that a family link changed while it was running and
  stops safely with a clear message naming what changed, before anything is
  saved. Nothing about either member is altered; the operator re-runs the
  merge preview, sees the up-to-date family links, and the retry goes through.

  The merge preview is also now honest about the one family link a merge
  deletes rather than moves: when the surviving member's own link points at
  the duplicate record, the preview says it will be cleared instead of listing
  it as history to be moved, and the audit records the clearance explicitly.
- **Three places now say what actually went wrong instead of blaming an email
  address or a promo code (#2455).** When the database refused a write because
  something was already taken, these paths assumed they knew which thing it was
  and said so, even when the real clash was somewhere else entirely.

  A member confirming a change of email address was told their new address was
  already in use whenever anything at all collided during the confirmation, so
  they would go off and pick a different address that they never needed to
  change. Now only a genuine clash on the address itself says that; anything
  else reports an ordinary failure they can retry or report.

  Importing members from a CSV reported "one or more login emails already
  exist" for any collision, sending an administrator hunting through a
  spreadsheet where every address was fine. A collision on something other than
  a login email now says plainly that one of the imported details is already
  used by another record. Either way the import is still all-or-nothing - no
  members are created.

  Creating a work party (working bee) event generates a private promo code and
  retries if that code happens to already exist. It used to retry on any clash
  at all, silently spending all five attempts on a problem that regenerating
  the code could never fix. It now retries only the code clash it exists for -
  a clash the database names as something else is reported straight away - and
  records the details when it genuinely runs out of attempts.

  Nothing an administrator does changes; the messages are simply accurate now.
- **Two places that read a database "already taken" failure now read it
  correctly (#2412).** Both were guessing at the shape of the error PostgreSQL
  hands back, and both guessed wrong. This time the shape was measured - the
  duplicates were forced against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 built from the real
  migration history - rather than reasoned about.

  **Group booking join codes.** When an organiser opens a group on their booking,
  the system invents a short join code, and if that code somehow already exists
  it is supposed to invent another and try again. It was not doing that. The
  retry looked for the collision in a field the current database driver never
  fills in, so it never recognised its own case and never retried. Nobody had
  noticed because a clash is roughly a one-in-850-billion event - the retry was
  broken, not load-bearing. It now recognises a real code clash and retries, and
  if it somehow exhausted all five attempts it says so, instead of telling the
  organiser their booking already has a group. A genuine "this booking already
  has a group" conflict is still reported straight away rather than being retried
  pointlessly.

  **Creating a member.** Any uniqueness failure while creating a member was
  reported as *A member with this email already exists*. That is usually true -
  the login-email rule is the only clash this path can normally produce - but it
  would have sent an admin off to fix an address that was perfectly fine if
  anything else ever collided. The email wording is now used only when the email
  rule actually fired; anything else gets a plain "one of their details is
  already used by another record" and is written to the server log, since on this
  path it would mean something unexpected. A member who cannot log in is never
  told their address is taken at all - the login-email rule cannot apply to them.
  The member **edit** path (#2385) now shares the same measured code for deciding
  whether the email rule fired, though it still answers a non-email clash with
  its existing "failed to update" error.

  For developers: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` now records exactly what the `pg` driver
  adapter populates on a uniqueness failure, including the finding that a
  hand-written partial index and a schema-level unique column are
  indistinguishable in the error - an assumption to the contrary had cost two
  separate sessions' reasoning.
- **Members and Subscriptions now say clearly whether an account can sign in,
  and opening a member no longer starts an edit (#2359).** Both lists use the
  same four Access states - **No login**, **Not invited**, **Invited**, and
  **Can log in** - with neutral, warning, information, and success tones. A
  member's admin or organisation role no longer changes that label or colour.
  Xero contact-group badges also keep the same categorical colour between the
  two lists instead of changing with each row's group order. Sorting Members by
  **Access** now follows that same four-stage status instead of the hidden
  legacy role.

  The Members row action now says **Open** and is available to view-only
  membership admins as well as editors. The member's name remains a link, but
  both routes open the detail page read-only; editing still starts only after
  choosing **Edit** inside a section. Subscriptions follows the same safe route
  for viewers who also have membership access. A finance-only viewer sees the
  member name as plain text, rather than a link to a page their role cannot
  open.

  Finance-view-only users can still read Subscriptions, but the two Xero sync
  actions are now disabled with the standard view-only explanation; the POST
  route continues to require **Finance edit** access.
- **A refused member merge now leaves an audit trail (#2498).** Until now only a
  completed member merge wrote an audit record; an attempt that was refused -
  because the two members drifted mid-merge, a guard blocked it, the confirmation
  phrase was wrong, the preview had gone stale, or a member was missing - rolled
  back and left nothing behind but a server log line. Refused attempts are now
  recorded too, so an admin repeatedly trying a merge that keeps being refused is
  visible in the audit trail. Each refusal writes a single `MEMBER_MERGE_REFUSED`
  entry naming the acting admin, both members, and why it was refused; it never
  stores member details beyond what a successful merge already records, and if the
  audit itself cannot be written the merge still refuses cleanly rather than
  erroring.
- **A member whose subscription is unpaid is now told, at booking time, that
  member rates are unavailable until they renew (#2533).** The owner has decided
  that the subscription lockout should eventually stop blocking these members
