  only pass that display setting through; integer-cent accounting fields,
  provider behavior, and booking outcomes are unchanged.
- **A warning when the club's currency and its Xero base currency differ
  (#3633).** Invoices this site sends to Xero carry no currency of their own,
  so Xero books them in the organisation's base currency, while card payments
  are charged in the club's currency. A club whose two currencies differed got
  card charges in one currency and Xero invoices in another, and nothing said
  so.

  Once Xero is connected, the site now compares the two. When they differ, a
  warning names both currencies on the Club Currency & Locale page, at the
  Connect step of the Xero setup wizard, and on the Operational Xero step of the
  setup list. It is a warning only: it blocks nothing and changes no invoice. It
  shows only to administrators with finance access, who can already read the
  Xero organisation's details, and it costs no extra call to Xero. A club on
  NZD with an NZD Xero organisation sees no change.
- **A late card payment refunded through the Xero repair tool no longer
  records a refund of money Xero never received (#3635).** When the repair
  tool refunded a card payment that went through after its booking was
  cancelled, it raised a refund credit note against the booking's original
  invoice. That invoice had already been cleared at the cancellation, so Xero
  showed money leaving the Stripe account that had never come in. The tool now
  records the refund the same way the automatic refund does, and raises a
  refund note only when the payment itself was recorded in Xero. Otherwise its
  result says to reconcile the Stripe bank lines by hand. The result names
  only what really happened: a refund it could not record, a note it did not
  queue, and a refund an officer also completed by hand (a possible double
  payment, which is alerted as the automatic refund alerts it). The refund-note link
  repair script (`scripts/xero-refund-note-link-repair.ts`) now uses the same
  figures as the rest of the app. It no longer re-links a note for a refund of
  that kind, and it counts notes an officer resolved in Xero, so it stops
  reporting gaps that are not there.
- **An Internet Banking group is kept on check-in day, the same as a single
  booking's hold (#3635).** If the group settlement runs out of time while the
  group's combined invoice cannot be read, the group now keeps its beds for up
  to seven days past the deadline, the same as a single booking's hold. Once
  check-in arrives, a group with an invoice is kept rather than released,
  whether Xero shows the invoice unpaid, no longer has it, or cannot be read, and the
  treasurer gets one email. The organiser may already have paid by bank
  transfer. Before this change the group was released at check-in and its
  joiners were cancelled.
- **Held bookings whose stay has started no longer use up the Xero read
  allowance (#3635).** The Internet Banking hold job now leaves a stay that has
  started alone before it reads Xero, so a few such holds can no longer use up
  the day's reads and hold other expired bookings' beds for up to a day. Its
  email now shows the invoice amount, not an amount owing, since the app cannot
  see a part payment without reading Xero.
- **Treasurer alerts nobody can receive are retried once a day, not every 15
  minutes (#3635).** This covers a "hold needs attention" email that reached
  nobody, for example because every admin address is suppressed or the site is
  a staging copy. It is now tried again a day later, and the same goes for one
  owed after the hold was released. Before, it was re-sent and audited on
  every run. A send that failed outright is still retried on the next run. The alert that Stripe holds a card payment this system never
  recorded now follows the same rule. It used to be lost for good if its one
  send failed or reached nobody.
- **A late card payment a treasurer keeps is now recorded in Xero (#3635).**
  Where a club has a treasurer approve the refund of a card payment that went
  through after its booking was cancelled, choosing to keep the money used to
  leave nothing in Xero naming it, so the Stripe payout held cash the accounts
  could not explain. A payment for a change to the booking was worse: its
  waiting Xero invoice was retired while the treasurer was still deciding, and
  could never come back.

  Now the change's invoice waits until the treasurer decides. Keeping the
  money records it in Xero the same way any card payment is recorded: an
  invoice for what the card paid, dated the day Stripe took it, paid from the
  Stripe bank account that day. For a change to a booking Xero had invoiced
  that is the change's own invoice; otherwise a separate "Payment kept after
  cancellation" invoice. The booking's original invoice and any note that
  cleared it are left alone, so the money is counted once, and any refund of it
  (including one made in the Stripe dashboard) is recorded as an ordinary refund
  credit note against it. A refund of a late payment Xero never recorded no
  longer raises a refund note against the booking's old, already-cleared
  invoice, which used to show money leaving the Stripe account that never came
  in. Reopening a kept one and then refunding it withdraws an invoice not yet
  sent, or credits back one already sent. The Xero repair tool records any kept
  payment Xero is missing. If an officer records a kept payment by hand in Xero
  and marks it resolved, the app treats it as done: it is never sent again, and
  the repair tool reminds the officer to record any refund of it by hand too.

  A refund of a late payment Xero never received no longer comes back a day
  later from the nightly check for missing refund notes, which used to raise it
  against the booking's cleared invoice. Refund notes for a late payment are
  worked out per payment, so one is never raised twice, and carry the day the
  refund left Stripe; the kept payment's invoice is dated the day Stripe took
  the money, read from Stripe.

  The email telling admins a late payment is held for approval is now tried
  again a day later by the payments cron if nobody could receive it, while the
  payment is still waiting for a decision.
- **A Xero operation marked "resolved in Xero" is now treated as done, and
  nothing re-runs it automatically (#3635).** On the Xero operations panel an
  officer can mark a failed operation resolved once they have fixed it by hand
  in Xero. Until now most of the system ignored that mark: the repair tool could
  retry it automatically, a retry queued earlier still ran, a stale browser tab
  could still send one, and the nightly refund check or "Queue all" on the
  missing-invoices list could raise the document again. Any of those could apply
  the same fix twice in Xero, for example a second credit note or a second
  invoice to the member.

  Now every retry path refuses a resolved operation, a queued retry is skipped
  rather than run, and nothing queues a new refund credit note or booking
  invoice beside the one the officer made. A refund credit note raised by hand
  counts for the amount it covered, so a later refund on the same payment still
  gets its own credit note for the rest. The one deliberate exception is a
  targeted force sync of a single booking's invoice, which still raises it and
  records in the audit log that it overrode the officer's mark. The repair tool
  and the booking page still show a resolved operation, as information only, so
  a wrong resolve can be caught. A resolved operation no longer holds up the
  Stripe refund-note link repair, and a newer failure is no longer hidden behind
  an older resolved one.

  Two things cannot be resolved: an operation while a retry of it is running or
  a new copy of it is queued (wait for it to finish), and an applied-credit
  allocation or deallocation,
  because a hand fix in Xero does not bring the club's own credit ledger back in
  line. Retry those instead.

  Two admin links also led nowhere and are fixed. The "Open the booking" link on
  the waitlist page and the booking link in a promo code's redemptions list both
  pointed at a page that does not exist; they now open the booking. Marking a
  booking paid, closing or reopening a money task, and correcting a booking's
  stored night prices now refresh that booking's page, and the two subscription
  payment actions refresh the member's admin page. Before, each asked to refresh
  a page address that matched nothing.
- **A booking change's Xero invoice is no longer thrown away while the member
  can still pay for the change** (#3641). When a card-paid booking is changed
  and costs more, its Xero invoice waits until the member pays. A scheduled
  clean-up used to retire that waiting invoice after 14 days, or a day after a
  declined card, even though the member could still pay the same
  request and the club reminds them before check-in. A late payment then left
  Stripe holding money that no Xero invoice named. The clean-up now retires a
  waiting invoice only once the request can no longer be paid: replaced by a
  later change, withdrawn, cancelled at Stripe, or the booking cancelled,
  bumped or deleted. A waiting invoice whose payment has already arrived is
  now sent rather than retired, unless that payment is being refunded (the
  booking was cancelled, or the request was replaced by a later change). If
  Stripe holds a payment that was never recorded here for three days, the
  club's admins are emailed. If a payment arrives for an invoice that was
  already retired, that same invoice is put back in the queue and sent once.
  Where sending an invoice could bill twice, or record more money than the
  card actually paid, the club's admins are emailed instead. The member's
  "pay this extra" form is no longer offered for a payment request Stripe has
  cancelled or already collected.
- **The emailed Xero reconciliation report now counts refund credit notes left unsettled (#3727).** The report's own summary already listed them after #3548; the email's summary table now shows the same count, so a treasurer reading the email sees there is something to settle.
- **A failed Xero retry no longer leaves the original operation stuck
  "running" with no button that works (#3462).** Requeueing a failed booking
  invoice first marks the original operation as running. If the retry then
  failed early, for example because the booking's contact matched another
  member's Xero contact, the original stayed "running" for ever. The retry row
  said "not marked replayable" and nothing on the screen could clear it.

  The original now goes back to **Failed** with the new error, so once you
  have fixed the cause you can requeue it again. The retry row's error now
  names the original operation and tells you this.

  An operation that has been running for more than 15 minutes now has a
  **Mark failed** button on its own row in **Xero → Operations**, so you can
  clear one stuck operation without resetting all of them. It asks for a
  reason and is recorded in the audit log, and it keeps any earlier error on
  the operation so you can see what to fix. Admins whose finance access is
  view-only see the button greyed out.

  **Mark failed**, **Mark non-replayable** and **Reset stale running** now
  save the change and its audit entry together: if the audit entry cannot be
  saved, the operation is left exactly as it was.
- **Two kinds of booking-change credit note no longer say "bank transfer" when none happened (#3536).**
  When a booking change lowered an invoice nobody had paid yet, the credit note
  raised in Xero read "Refund requested via internet banking", even though
  nothing was refunded. It now reads "Invoice correction — nothing refunded".
  And a booking-change refund the club pays back by hand always read as an
  internet-banking refund. When settling one, the officer is now asked whether
  the money went back in cash or by bank transfer. "In cash" gives the note
  "Refunded in cash"; no answer keeps the bank-transfer wording. The app never
  guesses cash from a payment being marked paid by hand.

  Only the words changed. The notes are still applied to the same invoice, no
  payment is recorded against any bank account, and no amount moved. The credit
  note for stored credit spent on a booking and the membership cancellation
  credit note keep the wordings they had. A note that fails and is retried, or
  that the Xero repair tool re-queues, says the same thing as the first
  attempt; notes already queued keep their old wording.
- **A booking paid entirely with account credit no longer shows as owing in
  Xero** (#3836). A card booking covered in full by the member's credit was
  invoiced in Xero at its full price, but the credit was never put against the
  invoice, so Xero showed the whole amount outstanding, aged receivables were
  overstated, and an invoice reminder could ask the member for money they had
  already paid. The member's credit is now allocated against the invoice as soon
  as it is raised, the same way a booking paid partly by card and partly by
  credit already was: a $200 booking paid with $200 of credit shows $0 due in
  Xero (was $200). A later price reduction or cancellation keeps Xero in step.
  For bookings invoiced before this release, the Xero booking repair tool
  (`pnpm run xero:booking-repair`) now reports each one as
  `UNALLOCATED_APPLIED_CREDIT` and, with `--apply`, allocates the credit once;
  cancelled ones are cleared by its existing cancelled-invoice repair. Bank
  transfer bookings are unchanged.
- **Each promo code gets its own line in Xero, on emails and on the booking
  page (#3828, epic #3813).** When a booking carries several promo codes, the
  Xero invoice now shows one "Promo adjustment - CODE" line per code, each
  posted to that code's own Xero item and account, so the treasurer can
  reconcile every code separately. A group's combined invoice does the same for
  each joiner, and a booking edit's supplementary invoice or credit note shows
  one promotion line for each code whose discount changed. Confirmation emails,
  the booking's payment summary and the member's data export name each code
  with its own amount.

  If the club's records cannot show exactly what each code took off, the
  invoice keeps one combined promotion line naming all the codes, at the
  usual promotion account, and the Xero sync record says why. The invoice
  total is the same either way.

  A booking with a single promo code is unchanged: the same invoice line,
  coding, email rows and edit lines as before.
- **A review's refund on an already-cancelled booking now reaches Xero**
  (#3880). When a financial review was completed after its booking had been
  cancelled, and money went back to the member by card refund or by
  bank-transfer hand-back, no Xero document recorded it, so the Stripe payout
  or the bank transfer had nothing in Xero to match. That refund now raises the
  same document the cancellation's own card refund raises: a credit note in the
  member's name for exactly what the review sent back (for example $25 of a
  $50 share at 50% less a $20 fee), refunded from the card clearing account or
  the bank-transfer refund account and worded "Refund against original credit
  card" or "Refund requested via internet banking". The cancelled invoice is
  left exactly as the cancellation left it. Two reviews of one booking raise a
  note each, and a repeated attempt raises none twice. Any part given back as
  account credit raises no document now, as the cancellation's own restored
  credit does not: Xero records it when the member spends it.
- **Rolling back past #3880 needs a check first.** The release before it treats
  a bank-transfer payment's refund notes as one note, so it can switch off the
  per-refund notes a review raised. Before rolling back, let every review
  refund note finish, queued or an operator's retry, and list refund-note links marked `perDelta`
  (`docs/xero/ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Deploy and rollback note (#3880)"): with none
  the rollback is safe; with any, after rolling forward set active again by hand
  each listed link the old code switched off whose note is still live in Xero. A
  completed cancellation hand-back's bank-transfer note is now queued in the
  same transaction as the hand-back itself.
- **A cash refund on a since-cancelled booking now says "Refunded in cash" in
  Xero (#3935).** When an officer settles a booking-change review and answers
  **In cash** to "How did the club pay the member back?", the Xero credit note
  already read "Refunded in cash". But if the booking had been cancelled after the
  change, the refund went to Xero as the cancellation's refund note, and that
  note ignored the answer and said the money went back by bank transfer.

  That note now carries the same "Refunded in cash" wording, and keeps it if the
  Xero sync is retried. Only the words change: the amount, the account the
  refund is recorded against, and everything the club's books reconcile on are
  exactly as before.
- **A card refund on a price cut is recorded once in Xero (#3993).**
  Lowering a card-paid booking used to raise a modification credit note against
  an invoice the card had already paid, which Xero refused, and the nightly
  check then raised a second credit for the same refund. The price cut now
  raises the same refund note a cancellation uses, settled from the Stripe
  account. A modification note is not created when the invoice cannot take it,
  and the booking repair tool no longer offers to retry one Xero has already
  refused. If this already happened: keep the refund note, void the unused
  modification note after checking it has no allocations, and Resolve the
  partial operation. Do not void the refund note.
- **A credit note voided in Xero is now recorded here.** Xero's webhook
  names a credit note `CREDITNOTE`. The app was looking for `CREDIT_NOTE`, so
  those events were stored and then ignored, including a void. They now follow
  the same credit-note sync as every other update, and the recorded status
  becomes voided. When the void switches off the note a payment points at (a
  card payment's refund note, or a per-refund note), the pointer moves to
  another live note or is cleared, so the nightly report no longer calls the
  inactive note missing. An internet-banking payment's note stays linked, now
  marked voided.

  Webhook subscriptions are chosen in the Xero developer portal, not in this
  app. Under **My Apps → your app → Webhooks**, tick **Invoices**,
  **Contacts**, and **Credit Notes**. If a void arrived before this change,
  open **Admin → Finance → Xero Sync → Inbound Events**, filter to CREDITNOTE,
  and Replay the event.
- **A refund credit note voided in Xero is no longer treated as the payment's
  refund note (#4091).** Before, when Xero voided the one refund credit note on
  a bank-transfer payment, the booking system kept that note's record active and
  the payment kept pointing at it.

  What you will see now:

  - Once a void reaches the app, the payment no longer points at the voided
    note, and the Xero repair tool no longer offers to point it back or flags it
    as a conflicting reference.
  - On a bank-transfer payment the void undoes the refund, as Xero is the
    payment rail: the refunded amount goes back down and nothing is raised again
    by itself. If the refund really happened, record it again; a fresh credit
    note is then raised.
  - On a card payment a fresh credit note is raised for the refund, as before.
    It is always a new note in Xero, never the voided one handed back.
  - A failed attempt at that fresh note stays in the failed Xero operations list
    with its Retry, instead of being shown as already repaired.
  - If Xero ever answers a refund-note request with a voided note, or with a
    note another refund already raised, the attempt fails in the failed Xero
    operations list with that reason, and nothing is recorded against the
    payment. Check the note in Xero before retrying.
- **A late card payment refunded automatically is now always recorded, even if
  the server stops mid-way (#4149).** When a card payment arrives after its
  booking was cancelled, the app refunds it and then records that refund for the
  finance team: the "Refunded automatically" entry, the audit log line, the
  admin alert and the Xero correction. If the server stopped, or the entry could
  not be saved, after the refund went out, that entry was never written - and
  the nightly Xero check then raised a credit note for the whole payment against
  the booking's original invoice, for money Xero never received. Now the alert
  and the audit line still go out at the time, and the missing entry is saved
  when Stripe next sends the payment notice, or by the nightly check before it
  raises any credit note; a payment it cannot check that night gets no credit
  note until it can. A hand-back task still open for that payment is closed
  rather than left asking someone to repay money Stripe already returned. The
  late entry is dated the day the money went back, and the alert is sent again
  with it, since the first may have failed alongside the entry.
- **Stripe's refund notice no longer credits Xero for a late payment it never
  received (#4170, closed here).** When Stripe's "charge refunded" notice
  arrived before the app had recorded a late payment's automatic refund, the app
  queued a credit note for the whole payment against the booking's original
  invoice. It now leaves that refund to the late payment's own record. A late
  payment refunded some other way (the Stripe dashboard), even before Stripe's
  "payment succeeded" notice arrived, is named in the audit log, emailed once
  to everyone who can edit Finance in its own alert that cannot be switched off
  (*Late payment refunded outside the app - check Xero*), and never noted in
  Xero as ordinary cash. The nightly check now also finds a late payment whose
  record was lost even when it shows no gap in Xero (looking back 30 days), and
  a treasurer-approved refund is no longer mistaken for a possible double
  payment; a possible double payment is escalated once, and again if that email
  failed. A late refund the repair tool made is recovered the same way, without
  a "refunded automatically" email, since the repair run already told the
  person who ran it.
- **A refund of a payment made in a stale tab after its booking was cancelled
  is no longer credited in Xero (#4173, closed here).** When a member paid for
  a change in an old tab after the booking was cancelled, the app refunded it
  as a superseded payment, and the nightly Xero check then raised a credit note
  against the booking's original invoice for money Xero never received. That
  refund is now left out of what a credit note may answer, the nightly check no
  longer asks Stripe about it every night, and no alert is sent for it.
- **The nightly Xero link cleanup now repairs refund credit notes voided in
  Xero before #4091 (#4161, #4192).** If a bank-transfer payment's refund credit
  note was voided in Xero before that fix, the booking system still held it as
  the payment's live refund note. Neither the nightly cleanup nor the
  reconciliation report noticed. Separately, the old cleanup could mark a card
  payment's voided note inactive but leave the payment pointing at it, which
  the report then showed as a missing refund-note link.

  The cleanup now finds every refund note that Xero records as voided or
  deleted and that is still held as live, or is still the note its payment
  points at. It marks each one inactive and moves the payment to its newest live
  note, or to none, through the same step an incoming Xero void uses. Its run
  summary counts what it found and what it healed, and until then the
  reconciliation report lists them as stale links. No money moves, and a second
  run changes nothing. A payment with a refund note still being created in Xero
  is left for the next night, and a heal that fails marks that night's cleanup
  as failed and is retried. Admins who run link maintenance by hand see the
  healed, failed and deferred counts, and every run is recorded in the audit
  log.

  Deploying: while the previous release is still running its cleanup, it can
  leave a payment pointing at an inactive voided note again. The next nightly
  run on this release heals it.
- **A refund note voided in Xero no longer risks losing the record of a new
  refund note raised on the same payment at the same moment (#4200).** The
  two updates could lock the payment and its Xero link in opposite orders, and
  the database would cancel one of them. They now lock the payment first and
  the link second, so both finish.
- **A refund request's own Xero credit note that is voided in Xero is no longer
  treated as live (#4195).** When a refund request is paid back by bank
  transfer, the booking system raises that request's own refund credit note in
  Xero. If the treasurer then voided or deleted that note in Xero, the booking
  system still held it as the request's live note, so a retry of the
  request's note found it and raised nothing.

  The incoming Xero sync now marks a voided or deleted request note inactive,
  even when a retry is writing the same note at that moment, and the booking
  system never treats a voided note as the request's note again. Nothing
  raises a replacement automatically: the officer decides, because the note
  was voided for a reason. Retry, Requeue and Retry all on Xero Operations
  now refuse such a request's note, saying an officer decides, and the booking
  repair tool no longer offers to retry it. Until the "Raise a fresh credit
  note" action arrives (#4214), raise the replacement by hand in Xero. When a
  request's note is raised again, it goes to Xero under a new key so that Xero
  cannot hand the voided note back.

  The refund itself is unchanged, because voiding the request's note does not
  undo the money the treasurer paid back. The booking repair tool still counts
  that refund against the request and never adds it to the cancellation's own
  refund note.

  Deploying: stop the previous release's Xero outbox and retry workers before
  this release takes over, and do not retry refund-request notes from the
  previous release during the switch, because it can take a voided note back.
  Before rolling back and after rolling forward, run the two read-only checks
  in the Xero architecture guide's #4195 deploy note, and check in Xero each
  request note they list. The first finds voided notes still held as live; the
  second lists every request note completed during the switch, because one the
  previous release took back can no longer be told apart locally.
- **A bank-transfer payment no longer forgets a refund request it already paid
  back when Xero sends an update (#4215).** When a refund request on a
  bank-transfer booking is paid back, the booking system records the refund on
  the payment and raises the request's own credit note in Xero. But whenever
  Xero then sent an update about the cancellation's refund credit note, the
  payment's account-credit note, or a booking change's credit note on its
  invoice, the booking system recounted the payment's refunded total and left
  out only the cash the refund requests had paid back. The payment then showed
  less refunded than the club had actually paid back. Since the bank-transfer
  floor (#4162) the total no longer drops below what the club recorded, but
  the same recount raised a false "refund ledger divergence" alert instead, and
  a payment it had already lowered stayed low.

  The recount now also counts every refund request the treasurer has marked
  paid back, at the amount recorded then. It does this while the request's
  note is still waiting to go to Xero, after Xero voids it, and when the
  request was paid back before the booking had a Xero invoice, so no note was
  ever raised for it. The request's refund is never added to the cancellation's
  credit note. A voided cancellation credit note is left to the nightly
  follow-up for voided bank-transfer notes (#4162), as before this change; that
  follow-up writes only once `XERO_ENABLE_BANK_REFUND_VOID_WRITES=true`.

  The booking repair tool now reads the same figure. Before, for a request paid
  back before the booking had a Xero invoice, it could offer a cancellation
  credit note that included the request's refund as well. It now leaves that
  refund out, and passes the cancellation's amount to a person when the two
  sit side by side. Such a request also never got its own credit note, because
  the booking had no invoice to credit when it was paid back. Once the invoice
  exists, and only where the payment has no cancellation credit note of any
  kind, the repair tool now offers that note, for the amount paid back, but
  never raises it by itself. Its report starts by asking you to check this
  booking's invoice in Xero for a credit already raised for the request: if
  there is one, nothing more is needed, and the report stays because the app
  cannot record it. Otherwise confirm the action by its key. Where the payment
  may have a cancellation credit note, that note may already include the
  request's refund if it was raised before this release, so the tool offers
  nothing and asks a person to work in two steps: first always compare the
  note's lines in Xero with the cancellation's own refund and edit it in place
  if the request's refund is in it (waiting for a note still queued or failed
  in Xero Operations), then raise the request's credit by hand only if none
  exists yet. It never re-raises a request's note that was voided in Xero: that
  stays the officer's decision.

  A payment that already lost a request's refund this way is not corrected by
  itself: it is recounted only when Xero sends an update about the
  cancellation's credit note, the account-credit note, or a booking change's
  credit note on its invoice (never the request's own credit note), and that
  may not happen again. After deploying, and after any rollback and roll
  forward, run the read-only check in the Xero architecture guide's #4215
  deploy note. It lists the bank-transfer payments that read less refunded than
  their records show. Check each one in Xero, because a cancellation credit
  note voided in Xero is listed too. Then replay one of its stored credit-note
  events from Xero, Inbound events. Stop the previous release's Xero inbound
  worker before this release takes over, because while it runs it can drop the
  request's refund again.

  The same deploy note has a second check for the opposite case. Before this
  release, a cancellation credit note could have been raised for the whole
  refund, including a request's refund that had no note of its own. This
  release then counts that request's refund twice. Such a payment reads more
  refunded than its records show, and the settled-cash audit lists it under
  "folded", which is misleading here. A third check lists every request the
  repair tool sends to a person because its payment has a cancellation credit
  note, whatever the payment shows, so a folded note is found before anything
  is counted twice. To fix one, first always compare the cancellation note's
  lines with the cancellation's own refund - a credit already raised for the
  request does not make this unnecessary. If the request's refund is in it,
  edit the note in place so it carries only the cancellation's own refund (Xero
  needs its allocations and refund payments removed first, and a removed
  reconciled payment's bank line matched again; a lock date blocks the edit
  until the club's adviser lifts it). Then raise the request's credit by hand
  in Xero only if none exists yet. Never void the note: on a bank transfer a
  void puts the refund back on the refund list as owed.
- **A credit note that was already used in Xero now fails with a plain reason,
  instead of a bare "400" from Xero (#4218).** If a treasurer used a member's
  credit note in Xero directly (for example an offset against something the member
  owed) and the app was not told, the app could still try to apply that credit to
  a new booking. Xero refused it, and the failed operation sat under Active
  failures with Xero's raw "400" message, which never said why.

  When Xero refuses a credit-note allocation because the note has less left than
  the allocation needs, the app now reads what the note has left and fails the
  operation with the reason "The credit note this allocation needs has only $X
  left in Xero; it was used outside the app. Retrying will not help until that
  credit is restored in Xero." If the use in Xero was a mistake, reverse it there
  and press **Retry in background**; the retry sends the allocation again and
  should go through. If it was deliberate, nothing in Xero needs changing: the
  invoice already shows what is still owed, but the failed row stays under Active
  failures until the planned fix (#4219) clears it. If Xero cannot be read
  to confirm it, the failure looks exactly as it did before. This change only makes the
  failure clear; it does not change any credit balance or write anything to Xero.
  Bringing the app's credit ledger into line automatically is planned separately
  (#4219).
- **A booking-repair credit note no longer waits for a credit note that will
  never be raised, and a Xero operation that succeeded no longer shows an old
  error (#4049).** When a price reduction cancelled an unpaid card request
  that the booking's Xero invoice had already billed, the booking system
  raises an invoice-correction credit note for that part. That note waits for
  the change's own credit note, if the change raises one. If the repair tool
  had to queue the correction note itself, it guessed whether the change
  raised its own note. It guessed wrongly when the change gave back applied
  credit with nothing paid by card, or when an organiser's card refund raises
  the note. The correction note then waited six hours and appeared as a
  second item for a person to review.

  Each change now records on its history whether it raises its own note, and
  the repair tool reads that record. Changes made before this release have no
  record, and the repair tool uses its old reading for them. At worst that
  holds the note for a person to review, and it never raises the note in the
  wrong order.

  A Xero operation that succeeds, including after an operator's retry, no
  longer keeps an earlier attempt's error code and message, and the Xero
  Operations and record-activity panels never show an error line on a
  succeeded operation. Previously such a row could still show an old message,
  such as "BILLED_OFFSET_AWAITING_OWN_NOTE", in red. Operations that succeeded
  before this release keep the old text in the database, but the panels no
  longer display it.
- **A payment's refund credit note voided in Xero now stays inactive even when
  a retry is recording it at that moment (#4223).** When a cancelled booking's
  bank-transfer payment was refunded, the booking system keeps one refund
  credit note in Xero for the payment. If the treasurer voided that note in
  Xero just as a retry of the refund's note was recording it as already raised,
  the retry
  could mark the voided note live again and point the payment back at it.

  The retry now waits for the incoming Xero sync and then keeps the void: the
  note stays inactive even if its mirror was missing, its voided status is
  kept with the note's stored details, and the payment's pointer is released.
  If another operation holds the payment busy, the inactive note is saved and
  pointer cleanup waits for the nightly link cleanup, allowing both operations
  to finish. The same rule already covered a refund request's own note
  (#4195), and now covers card payments' notes too.

  Deploying: no database change. Stop and drain old refund-note workers and
  web/direct retries before enabling new refund-note writes; the old and new
  canonical writers take row locks in different orders. Rollback requires the
  same drain in reverse (see the Xero architecture guide's deploy note).
- **A bank-transfer refund whose Xero credit note is voided comes back to the
  refund list, with one question (#4162).** Before, voiding the credit note
  for a bank refund left the club's records disagreeing with each other: the
  payment's total said one thing, its refund history another, and nothing told
  the treasurer. Now each night the app takes that refund back out of the
  payment's records and puts it back on **Money to settle** as owed, asking:
  has the money gone to the member? The answers are **Yes, raise a fresh credit
  note** (one new note, dated today), **Yes, I already recorded it in Xero
  myself** (type the note's number; the app checks Xero has it, live, for the
  right amount, and keeps track of it), **Not yet** (leave it on the list) or
  **No, the club keeps it** (with a reason). The member is not emailed and
  nothing is raised in Xero until someone answers. A voided note that was only
  a duplicate changes nothing. A note the app cannot match to one refund is
  listed on **Stuck States** for a person to check instead.

  What you need to do: this ships switched off, reporting only. Before turning
  it on, run `pnpm run xero:bank-refund-void-count` to see how many voided
  bank-transfer refund notes there already are and what will happen to each,
  then set `XERO_ENABLE_BANK_REFUND_VOID_WRITES=true`. The first night after
  that puts each older void on the refund list too.
- **A credit note used in Xero outside the app now fixes the app's credit ledger by
  itself for a booking's applied credit (#4219).** When a treasurer uses a member's
  credit note directly in Xero (for example an offset against something the member
  owed) and the app then tries to apply that same credit to a booking, the failed
  allocation used to sit under Active failures for good, with no button that could
  clear it. Now, when Xero refuses the allocation and the app confirms the credit
  was used, it writes that credit down, stops counting it as applied to the
  booking, closes the failed rows (shown as "Closed: credit used outside the app")
  and carries on with anything else the booking needs. The member's credit balance
  does not change and nothing is sent to Xero. Only credit used on things the app
  has no record of is counted; credit used on another of the club's own invoices is
  left to the existing sync.

  The released amount is now unpaid on the booking's invoice in Xero, and that is
  where to collect it from: the booking page in the app does not show a balance for
  a booking that was already paid. An email asking the member to pay follows in a
  later release. Other credit-note allocations that fail for the same reason are
  unchanged (reverse the use in Xero and retry). Anything the app cannot account
  for is left exactly as it was, and if the use in Xero is later reversed the
  credit does not come back automatically yet.
- **Repairing a card booking's invoice payment in Xero Operations no longer
  records too much card cash when account credit was used (#4010).** If Xero
  refused the card payment when a booking's invoice was raised, an officer can
  repair it from the Xero Operations panel. That repair used to record the
  whole invoice total as card cash. On a booking partly paid with the member's
  account credit, that overstated the card cash, so the Stripe deposit no
  longer matched, and the credit then had nothing left to settle. The repair
  now records the card cash the invoice was meant to receive, the same figure
  used when the invoice was first raised. Repairs of operations made before
  that figure was kept still record the invoice total, as before.
- **Repairing a partly completed invoice in Xero Operations now respects an
  officer's mark, and closes the operation when it succeeds (#4256).** If an
  officer marked an operation resolved in Xero, or not replayable, while a
  retry of it was already starting, the retry could still go ahead and mark it
  repaired, and two retries at once could both send the payment to Xero. A
  retry now takes the operation first, so the officer's mark wins and the
  retry does nothing. A successful payment repair now also marks the operation
  succeeded, so the booking stops showing the payment as not recorded. If the
  invoice email had also failed, the operation stays partly completed for that,
  and its message now says the email is what is left. A repair interrupted
  part-way (the server stopped) comes back as partly completed when an officer
  uses Mark failed or Reset stale running, so Retry repairs it again. Marking
  an operation not replayable while a retry of it is running is refused with
  "try again when it finishes". Rows repaired before this release stay partly
  completed; retry them once and they close. A retry never sends a payment
  Xero already holds for that invoice, and Reset stale running now says how
  many operations it failed and how many interrupted repairs it returned.
- **A card refund's credit note is raised again when the note an officer
  resolved by hand is later voided in Xero (#4250).** When a refund credit note
  only partly went through, an officer can mark it resolved in Xero. If that
  note was later voided in Xero, the app still counted it as covering the
  refund, so the nightly check raised no new note and Xero was left with no
  live note for a real refund. A resolved note that Xero records as voided or
  deleted now covers nothing: the refund shows on the list of refunds missing
  a credit note, and the nightly check queues a fresh one. Notes resolved by
  hand that are still live in Xero count exactly as before.

  So after voiding a card refund's credit note in Xero, don't make a
  replacement note by hand: the app raises one overnight, and a hand-made one
  as well would record the refund twice. The resolve dialog in Xero Operations
  now says so for credit notes.
- **The "refund ledger divergence" alert for a bank-transfer payment now says
  what is usually wrong, where to look, and how to fix it (#4230).** When the
  refunds Xero accounts for on a bank-transfer payment add up to less than the
  refunds the club recorded on it, the booking system keeps its own record and
  alerts the treasurer. The alert used to blame a credit note voided in Xero,
  but it never fires while a voided note is waiting for the nightly follow-up.
  What it usually means is a refund with no credit note of its own: when a
  payment already has its refund credit note, a later refund on it - for
  example a second cancellation refund, or the card-refunded part of an
  approved refund appeal - is counted under that first note and Xero never gets
  a note for it. The alert now names the payment, its booking and the credit
  note whose change raised it, and asks for a note to be raised by hand only
  for a refund whose note was never raised - never for one whose note was
  voided, which is answered on the refund list or Stuck States. The Xero
  guide's troubleshooting table quotes it. Nothing changes in how notes are
  raised; giving each later refund its own note is a separate change (#4287).

  The deploy notes add a read-only query that lists bank-transfer payments
  whose paid-back refunds - hand-backs, a cancelled booking's review refunds
  and card refunds, less bank refunds the void follow-up took back - add up to
  more than their refund credit notes, so officers can raise the missing notes
  by hand. Tests now pin, against a real database, that a group organiser's
  repayment and the recount's handling of a payment's charge records were
  already safe, the current handling of a later refund on a bank-transfer
  payment, and which voided-note states can reach the alert.
- **A booking change made while its Xero invoice is being raised is no longer
  lost from the invoice (#3980).** If a member or officer changed a booking in
  the few seconds the booking's first Xero invoice was being created, the
  invoice could go out with the old guests and price, and nothing in Xero
  carried the difference.

  Now a change saved just as the invoice is linked is refused with "please try
  again in a moment", and nothing is changed; trying again adjusts the invoice
  like any other change. A change that landed a moment earlier is caught when
  the invoice is linked: if the booking is now worth more, the difference is
  billed automatically on a supplementary invoice; if it is worth less, the
  treasurer gets a task in Xero Operations to check the invoice and raise a
  credit note by hand, then choose **Resolve (fixed in Xero)**. The task says
  how the change was settled, so any refund already paid out is accounted for
  too. No credit note is ever raised automatically.

  Not yet covered: when the change asked the member's card for the extra and
  they pay it, that payment is not recorded against the supplementary invoice
  in Xero, which shows it owing until a treasurer matches it. Recording such a
  payment against the right invoice follows in #3953.
- **Replaying a voided refund credit note in Xero Inbound Events now recounts
  the payment again (#4291).** Before, once the app had recorded that a refund
  credit note was voided in Xero, any later event for that note did not
  recount the payment. This included a retry of the void event after it failed
  partway, a repeat delivery from Xero, or a **Replay** from Inbound Events. If
  the first void event stopped before it recalculated the payment's refunded
  total, the total stayed wrong and a replay could not fix it. A later event
  for a voided note now recalculates the payment's refunded total. The voided
  note stays switched off and is never made the payment's refund note again.
- **A second refund handed back on a bank-transfer booking now gets its own
  Xero credit note (#4287).** When a bank-transfer payment already had its
  refund credit note in Xero, a cancellation refund the treasurer handed back
  later was counted under that first note and Xero never got a note for it, so
  Xero showed less credit than the club had paid back. Each such refund now
  gets a credit note of its own, for exactly that refund's amount. The same
  applies to the first refund handed back on a bank-transfer payment that was
  also partly paid by card, where the first note's amount could otherwise come
  out wrong. If Xero later voids such a note and the nightly check takes the
  refund back off the booking, that refund stops counting towards any later
  credit note on the payment. When the treasurer then re-confirms that refund
  with a new credit note, it counts again, once, so a later card refund's credit
  note is no longer raised short (#4315).

  Nothing is raised for refunds handed back before this release: the
  read-only query in the deploy notes still lists those payments so their
  notes can be raised by hand. A refund appeal's card part, a Stripe dashboard
  refund and a late card capture's refund on a bank-transfer payment get their
  own notes too, from #4312. A cancellation never refunds a bank-transfer
  payment to a card (it gives account credit), so no card refund is left
  sharing the first note.

  While the previous version still runs during an upgrade, or after rolling
  back, its Xero worker cannot raise these new credit notes and leaves them
  failed; retry them from the Xero failed-operations panel once this version
  is running alone.
- **A card payment for a booking change is now recorded in Xero even when the
  booking's invoice was raised before the member paid (#3953).** If a booking
  was changed before its Xero invoice existed, and the member paid the extra by
  card only after the invoice had gone out, Xero never heard about that
  payment: the invoice showed as part-unpaid although Stripe held the money,
  and the treasurer had to match it by hand.

  Now, when such a payment arrives, the app reads the booking's invoices in
  Xero and records the payment against the one that still has that money due:
  the supplementary invoice raised for a change that landed while the invoice
  was being created (#3980), or otherwise the booking's own invoice, which
  already bills the change. Example: a $300 invoice, a guest added for $80,
  paid by card - Xero shows $380 billed and $380 paid. Each payment is
  recorded once, however many times Stripe or the member's browser report it.

  Each payment is recorded by one document only: if the booking's own invoice
  payment, a supplementary invoice for the change, or the supplementary invoice
  for a change made while the invoice was being raised already records it, the
  app leaves it there.

  Nothing is guessed. If Xero can't be read, the invoice the payment belongs to
  has nothing left due, or the invoice's own payment hasn't been recorded yet,
  the payment is not recorded and the treasurer is emailed - as it is for an
  older payment the app can't tie to a booking change, where another invoice
  on the booking may already record it; the operation in
  **Xero Operations** says why, and **Retry** runs it again once the cause is
  fixed. Payments on cancelled bookings, and on bookings paid by internet
  banking, are not recorded this way.

  A refund of such a payment from Stripe names the invoice it paid on its
  credit note. The booking-vs-Xero repair tool now reports **card payment not
  recorded in Xero** for bookings affected before this change, and can queue
  the fix.
- **A card refund on a bank-transfer booking now gets its own Xero credit
  note (#4312).** When a bank-transfer payment also took a card payment (an
  edit paid by card) and some of that card money was refunded, the refund
  was counted under the payment's first refund credit note and Xero never
  got a note for it, so Xero showed less credit than the club had paid back.
  These card refunds now get a credit note of their own, each for exactly
  that refund: the card part of an approved refund appeal, including one the
  payment recovery job finishes later; a refund made in the Stripe
  dashboard; and a refund of a card payment captured after the booking was
  cancelled. A card payment taken twice by mistake, and refunded, still gets
  no note: Xero never received it. If Stripe fails one of these refunds days
  later and the app sends it again, the failed refund's note covers the
  refund the app sends in its place, so Xero is not credited twice; if that
  one fails too, the cover passes to the next refund the app sends for it, if
  any. A refund made in the Stripe dashboard always gets a note for its full
  amount. If Xero voids one of these notes, it is
  listed on Stuck States for a person and never mistaken for a bank refund
  to take back.

  Only card refunds made after this release's marker migration runs get a note
  of their own. Older ones are never given one: the read-only query in the
  deploy notes still lists those payments so their notes can be raised by hand.
  While the previous version still runs during an upgrade, or after rolling
  back, it treats these new credit notes as it treated card refunds before.
- **A failed Xero operation now says why, in plain English (#4278).** The Xero
  operations screen, a record's Xero activity, and the warning on a booking whose
  invoice failed used to show Xero's raw error text or a JSON dump. Each now shows
  one headline (what happened), what it means for the club, and "What to do",
  including whether the app tries again by itself. Common causes are covered: the
  daily request limit (with a rounded wait), an invoice already paid, a credit note
  with less credit than expected, a duplicate contact name, a locked period, an
  archived account or contact, a lost job, a timeout and a lost connection to Xero.
  When the reason is hidden for privacy, or is not one the app recognises, it says
  so rather than guessing. Xero's own wording and the error code are still one
  click away under "Show technical details".
- **A refund credit note voided in Xero now always stays voided in the app
  (#4288).** An older reading of the note from Xero - from the inbound Xero
  sync, the card refund-note status recorder, or a treasurer's "I already
  recorded it in Xero myself" answer - could arrive after the void had been
  recorded and make the note look live again. The app then counted a voided
  note as covering the refund. On a bank transfer, the sync could also put the
  voided note's amount back into the payment's refunded total. It could also
  record the note's old allocations and refund payments.

  Every reading now carries Xero's own last-updated time, and an older reading
  never overwrites a newer one. A voided note is never made live again: Xero
  never un-voids a note, so re-crediting always takes a new one. If a
  treasurer's "already recorded it" note is voided while the answer is being
  saved, the answer is refused with a plain message and nothing is recorded.
- **A Xero task that loses a start-up race to a failed twin now tries again
  instead of failing by mistake (#4338).** The app keeps at most one live Xero
  task per document. When two parts of the app started the same task at once,
  the second was told to use the first one's task; if the first had already
  failed in that split second, the second failed with a database error instead.
  It now starts its own attempt, as a retry a moment later would, so it makes
  one more call to Xero, which can fail again and add one failed entry towards
  the repeated-failure alert. If the first task had succeeded, part-succeeded,
  been cancelled or been marked resolved in Xero by an officer, the second
  still stops with the same error as before. The clearest case was
  applying a member's credit to a booking twice at once while the credit note
  had been used in Xero outside the app: the ledger was brought into line
  correctly, but one run showed as failed, and the second run's failed
  allocation could stay on the Active failures list. Both runs now finish, and
  every failed allocation from the pair is closed, and the second close is
  recorded in the audit log, when the ledger is brought into line. No credit balances, invoices or Xero records change.
- **The Xero Operations Failed view now shows only the failures that still need
  attention (#4220).** Choosing Failed under Status also picks "Active only"
  under Failure, so rows that a later run repaired or replaced, or that an officer
  marked resolved in Xero, no longer sit beside the one that really needs you. A line
  above the list says how many are hidden, and "Show them" brings them back;
  they stay as the audit trail and nothing about them has changed. Links saved
  with only the Failed status still show every failed row, as before.
- **Closing a failed card refund as paid another way now records the money back
  in Stripe as well as the bank payment (#4369).** When Stripe had accepted a
  card refund and then failed it, Xero still showed that money leaving the
  Stripe account. Paying the member by bank and closing the row as Paid
  another way, while that old card note covered the amount, queued no bank
  document for the transfer.

  Closing now queues two documents: an invoice for the amount the card note
  covered, recording that money back in the Stripe account, and a
  bank-transfer refund credit note for the full amount paid back. Paying back
  less than the card note still leaves the difference on the Xero
  reconciliation report. A close the card note does not cover is unchanged.
  The invoice is never emailed and is not the booking's bill. If an officer
  voids it in Xero, the app stops counting it and does not raise it again.

  A close already taken by a previous release is unchanged, and there is no
  automatic backfill. After this release has taken a covered close, do not
  roll back to a release that does not know this invoice: that release will
  still send the bank note and leave the invoice waiting, so Xero shows both
  the old card note and the bank note until this release sends the invoice.
- **A card refund Stripe failed later no longer creeps back into a payment's refunded total (#4370).** When Stripe accepts a card refund and then fails it, the refund's credit note stays in Xero. Any later credit note on the same payment, such as a second refund, used to count the failed refund again, so the payment showed more refunded than the member actually got back.

  The recount now takes each failed refund off once. If an officer closed it "Paid another way", the Stripe reversal invoice already takes it off; if that reversal is voided or deleted in Xero, the failed refund counts again. An older failure that was never reversed comes off through the record of the failure, never more than the payment's refund notes cover above the money still standing. Payments with no failed refund are counted exactly as before, and nothing is called in Xero. New double counts are prevented. A bank-transfer payment already overstated is corrected at its next credit-note event; a card payment already overstated keeps its stored figure and is flagged for an officer, because the recount never lowers a card payment's total on its own.
- **A Xero task that two parts of the app run at once no longer shows as failed
  when one of them succeeded (#4356).** The app keeps at most one live Xero
  task per document, so when two parts of the app start the same task at once
  they share it and each sends the same request to Xero. If one succeeded and
  the other was turned away (for example by Xero's rate limit, or because the
  same request was already being handled), whichever answer came back last was
  recorded. A task whose payment, invoice or credit note was in Xero could
  therefore show as failed on the Xero Operations page and count towards the
  repeated-failure alert. A failure is now never recorded over a success or a
  part-success, and a part-success is never recorded over a full success; a
  success still replaces an earlier failure, because it is Xero's answer to the
  same request. A late failure also no longer lands on a part-completed task
  while Retry is repairing it, which could leave the payment unrecorded.
  Nothing changes in Xero, and no money moves.
- **A Xero retry is no longer marked failed by an earlier attempt that
  answers late (#4373).** When a Xero call stalled or failed and the operation
  was retried, the earlier attempt's late answer could still be written onto
  the retry while it was running, so the Xero Operations panel showed the
  retry as failed mid-run and a second retry could start beside it.

  Each attempt now records its outcome only on its own run. A late answer
  from an earlier attempt is left out and logged, and the retry's own result
  is the one shown. Nothing changes for operations that are not retried.
- **Officers are told when Xero records a document after they resolved its
  operation by hand (#4374).** Two attempts at the same Xero call can share one
  operation. If one failed, an officer marked the operation resolved in Xero and
  made the document by hand, and the other attempt's call then succeeded, Xero
  could end up holding the document twice and nobody was told.

  The late success is still recorded, with its Xero links. When it recorded
  a document in Xero, the finance contacts now get one **Xero Sync Error**
  email per operation saying so and naming it. Check Xero: if the same
  document was also made by hand and the app did not find and use it, void
  the duplicate.
- **A kept card payment for a booking change is recorded in Xero even if the
  step after the keep fails (#4382).** When a treasurer keeps a late card
  payment whose change invoice was retired because the payment seemed never to
  come, that invoice is put back in the queue in the same save as the decision.
  The usual Xero sender then records the money. Previously that revival
  happened only after the decision was saved, and a failure there left the
  money in Stripe with nothing in Xero and nobody told.

  A waiting invoice, and a revival the payment does not safely cover, are
  unchanged: those still happen after the decision is saved.
- **A late card payment for a booking change that a treasurer keeps on a
  cancelled booking is now recorded in Xero (#4324).** Before, when the
  booking's Xero invoice existed and no change invoice was waiting on the
  payment, keeping it recorded nothing: Stripe held the money and Xero never
  showed it. The app now records it with the document that matches what Xero
  already bills. Where the booking's invoice already bills the change, or the
  extra invoice the app raised for a change made while that invoice was being
  created does, the payment goes on that invoice, for no more than it still shows due, so the
  invoice is paid off rather than a second invoice counting the same income
  twice. Where nothing in Xero bills the change, the app raises its kept-payment
  invoice, as it does for a kept booking payment; that includes a change whose
  invoice was moved to, and paid by, a later payment, or waits on one. Where a change invoice already
  answers the payment, that invoice records it, as before. Where the payment
  names no booking change, nothing is recorded automatically, even where an
  unpaid invoice names the payment, and the booking-vs-Xero repair tool lists
  it for the treasurer. Each payment is
  recorded once: a repeated Stripe notification, a re-keep after a reopen, or
  the repair tool running beside a keep never records it twice, and refunding a
  reopened payment withdraws a recording that has not been sent. The repair
  tool's dry run now lists payments kept before this fix, with the document
  that will record each, and its apply records them; a payment the treasurer
  already entered by hand in Xero would be recorded again, so check the dry run
  first (see the maintenance guide). And where that extra invoice cannot be
  raised because a kept-payment invoice already bills its change, a Xero
  Operations task (`PRIMARY_INVOICE_UNDERBILLED`) now asks the treasurer to bill
  what is still due, rather than the shortfall going only to the server log.
- **A card change's Xero invoice is no longer lost when a later change replaces
  its unpaid payment request (#3403).** When a member did not pay for a change
  by card and a later change asked for that money again together with its own,
  the earlier change's waiting Xero invoice was never sent: it was cancelled a
  day later while the later request still collected the money, leaving card
  money in Stripe that no Xero invoice named until someone ran the
  booking-versus-Xero repair report.

  Now, as the owner decided ("follow the money"), the earlier invoice moves to
  wait on the request that carries its balance. When the member pays that
  request, both invoices go to Xero, each for its own amount and each marked
  paid; the earlier amount is never added to the later invoice. If the member
  never pays, nothing is invoiced, as for any unpaid card change. If the later
  request was already paid when the move happens, the earlier invoice is sent
  straight away. A declined card on the earlier request is covered too, and
  if that declined request is later paid from an old browser tab after all,
  its invoice goes back to it and records that payment instead. If the
  member ends up paying both the old request and the one that took it over,
  the change's invoice still records only one of them; the old request's
  payment, arriving second, is recorded by its own receipt, and where the
  newer request is paid second an officer is told once so the extra can be
  refunded or credited.

  Separately, when several invoices wait on one card payment, Xero now records
  them as paid only while together they add up to no more than the payment;
  one that would not fit is held back and an officer is told, as a single
  invoice larger than its payment already was.

  Nothing changes for bookings paid by internet banking, where each change's
  invoice is already sent unpaid when it is priced. Invoices the system had
  already cancelled this way before this release are left to the repair
  report, which still lists them as a missing supplementary invoice.
- **The Xero connection has its own table, with no secret in it (#3806).**
  Whether Xero is connected, to which organisation, and the lock that stops two
  servers refreshing the same Xero sign-in at once now live in a small table of
  their own. The Xero sign-in tokens stay in the encrypted credential store,
  which is now the only copy the app reads. The old token table is kept up to
  date for the previous release during an upgrade and is removed in a later
  release.

  A club already running a build that moved the Xero tokens into the credential
  store (#3454) notices nothing. A club upgrading from v0.13.2, the newest
  tagged release, or anything older reconnects Xero once from Admin → Xero
  after this upgrade; until then Xero shows "reconnect required" and Xero work
  waits. The upgrade notes say how to check, and how to avoid the reconnect.
- **A repaired booking invoice no longer says the club received a card payment
  that was never taken (#4413).** Repairing a price increase used to send the
  extra invoice to Xero as already paid by card, even when the member had not
  paid or was paying by bank transfer. Xero then showed money in the Stripe
  account that Stripe had never taken.

  The repair now follows the same rule as the booking edit itself. An unpaid
  card request waits until the card payment succeeds. A payment already taken
  is recorded. A bank transfer, or an edit with no card payment to point at,
  is raised as unpaid so the treasurer can record the money when it arrives.
  A request a later card payment already carries waits on that later payment.
  An invoice instruction that does not say whether to record a card payment
  is sent unpaid.
- **A refund's Xero credit-note check now counts only that refund's own live
  note (#4265, #4258, #4321).** The app checks, for each bank-transfer refund,
  whether Xero holds a live credit note covering it. Three things could make
  that check read "covered" when the refund was not.
  - A refund request's own note, resolved by hand in Xero, was counted towards
    the payment's other refunds, and kept counting even after it was voided.
    For example, a $300 request note made a voided $200 cancellation note look
    spare, so the nightly check left a $200 refund with no credit in Xero.
  - A refund closed as "covered by another refund's note" was credited with
    that other refund's whole note.
  - A credit note the app had raised for one refund, whose Xero operation was
    resolved by hand or not yet finished, could also be accepted as the
    hand-made note for another.

  Now a refund counts only its own live note, never a refund request's. A
  voided note that the nightly check judges after this release is undone and
  put back on the refund list as owed, as the check intends. A void the check
  already marked spare before this release stays marked and is not looked at
  again; this release changes no existing record. Answering "already recorded
  it in Xero myself" with a note that such an operation records is refused with
  a plain message, and nothing is recorded. The app still cannot recognise a
  note made by hand in Xero for a failed operation that was then marked
  resolved, because it never learns that note's number.
- **"Resolve (fixed in Xero)" on a failed refund credit note now asks which Xero
  note you made, and checks it (#4421).** When the app couldn't raise a refund's
  credit note in Xero, an officer could make the note by hand and mark the job
  resolved, but the app never learned which note it was. The same note could
  then also be given as the answer for a different refund, so one $200 note
  covered $400 of refunds and Xero understated the club's refunds.

  Now the dialog asks for the credit note's number and shows the refund's
  amount. The app checks the note in Xero: it must be approved or paid, a sales
  credit note for the booking's Xero contact (the member's, or the
  organisation's) and that exact amount, and not allocated to another invoice.
  It records the note against that refund and watches it, so if the note is
  later voided in Xero the refund goes back on the list to be dealt with. A note
  already recorded against another refund is refused with a plain message, and
  nothing is recorded. The dialog stays open while it checks Xero and shows any
  refusal next to the number. A job whose refund amount can't be read can't be
  resolved this way: the screen says to use **Mark non-replayable** and ask the
  treasurer, rather than making a note by hand. Jobs resolved before this
  release keep no note number.
- **Approving a manual credit grant now raises its Xero credit note (#4431).**
  The admin who requests the credit chooses the account: the member's own
  money (an overpayment or a double charge) or goodwill. The admin who
  approves sees that choice and cannot change it. Approval queues one Xero
  credit note for that credit. Spending the credit uses that note.

  A deduction is refused while the member still has credit that already has
  a Xero note, because the note would stay at its full amount. Older credit
  that was granted before this change, and never had a note, is unchanged:
  it still gets its note when the member spends it. A grant requested before
  an account was chosen has to be rejected and requested again.
- **A card payment that is larger than one Xero invoice is recorded across the invoices that bill it (#4434).**
  When a later request carries an earlier change, the earlier invoice can move onto the later payment while that payment's receipt is still waiting. The receipt used to record only what the first invoice had left due, and an officer had to enter the rest by hand. It now records the rest on the next invoice that bills the same payment, up to what each invoice has due, and still tells an officer only about money no invoice can take. A credit release already on an invoice is not treated as this receipt's own payment. Nothing is recorded twice, and nothing is posted as a Xero overpayment.
- **A retried extra card payment is recorded in Xero even when a credit release already paid the same invoice (#4435).**
  After a crash, the receipt used to treat any live payment with the same Stripe reference as its own. A credit release on the booking's main invoice uses that same reference, so the retry could adopt the release's payment and record nothing. It now accepts a payment only when the reference matches, the amount equals the receipt, and that payment is not already the credit release's. Otherwise it records its own payment. The money was already collected; both payments now show in Xero.
- **Removing a credit note's allocation in Xero now lowers what a payment looks to have refunded (#4447).**
  Deleting an allocation in Xero, while leaving the credit note itself, used to leave that amount counted as already refunded. The next update from Xero drops it, and an older update that arrives later does not put it back, so a later cancellation is not told there is less left to refund than there is.

  No money moves on its own.
- **A card refund of credit already recorded in Xero now gets a credit note (#4493).**
  When a member paid by card for credit that had been used in Xero, and that
  payment was recorded on the booking's invoice, a later refund of the card
  left Xero still showing the money as received. That refund now raises one
  credit note for the amount refunded, against the same invoice, and sending
  the refund again does not raise a second note.

  Refunds that were already missed are not repaired. A card payment taken after
  a booking was cancelled is unchanged.
- **Xero refund-note repairs report when a reset prevents completion (#4440).** If an operation is reset while its repair runs, the officer now sees the same retry message as an invoice repair instead of a success message. Retry once to close the operation.
- **A treasurer can now pull a change made in Xero into the club system straight
  away, instead of waiting for the next scheduled run (#4432).** A member's page,
  a booking's page and the Xero Sync page each have a "Sync from Xero now"
  button for officers with finance edit access; view-only officers see it
  disabled. The member and booking buttons re-read just that member's or
  booking's invoices and credit notes and repair them the same way the scheduled
  run would; the Xero Sync page's button runs the whole scheduled reconcile on
  demand. Each reports what it changed, or "Already in step". The buttons are
  rate-limited, and each sync is recorded in the audit log under the existing
  `xero` category, so the same Support and Finance readers see it and nobody's
  readership changes.

  The scheduled inbound sync and the whole-club button now share one run claim
  held by the database, so the two can never run at once: whichever starts
  second reports "A sync is already running". If the server running a sync
  stops, the database frees the claim straight away.
- **The Xero Sync page now shows when the last Xero webhook arrived, and warns
  when none has arrived for too long (#4432).** While Xero is connected and
  nothing has arrived for longer than the club's threshold (24 hours unless the
  club changes it on that page), a warning appears there and in Needs Attention
  and Stuck States. Changing the threshold is recorded in the audit log.
- **A payment deleted in Xero no longer stays as a live payment in the app
  (#4531).** When the treasurer deleted a payment in Xero, often to re-enter it
  by hand during bank reconciliation, the app kept its own record of that
  payment active for good, so the booking looked paid twice and the "recorded
  in Xero" totals were overstated.

  Now, when the app next reads the invoice or credit note, it asks Xero about
  any payment that has disappeared from it. Only a payment Xero confirms as
  deleted is retired; the hand-entered replacement stays as it is. If Xero
  cannot be asked at that moment (for example, the day's Xero allowance is
  nearly used up), the app tries again on its own every few hours until Xero
  answers.

  Payments deleted before this release are not retired by themselves, and
  neither is a booking change's card payment. Run
  `pnpm run xero:deleted-payment-link-backfill` to see them (it changes
  nothing), then run it again with `--apply` to retire the ones Xero confirms
  deleted. `docs/MAINTENANCE.md` has the steps.
- Fix: one rule now decides whether a Xero payment still counts (#4576). The fee-gap, change-capture receipt, refund-note settlement and credit-note spend readers all treat a `DELETED` or `VOIDED` payment as dead, in any letter case, instead of four hand-rolled copies that missed `VOIDED` and two that were case-sensitive. A census test fails on any new hand-rolled payment-status comparison.
- **A card payment for released credit is no longer recorded twice in Xero
  (#4494).** Where a booking's extra invoice for the balance its first invoice
  missed was raised after the member paid by card for credit used in Xero, the
  extra invoice could record that same card payment as its own, beside the
  payment the credit-release sweep records on the booking's invoice, overstating
  the money received. The extra invoice now never pays itself from that money,
  and is raised unpaid when nothing else could pay it. An extra invoice queued
  before this release records no payment when it is sent, retried or repaired
  if what it would take, together with the credit-release money, is more than
  the card took. The sweep waits for such an invoice that has not been sent and
  still can be, and holds, telling an officer, where it may already have
  recorded part of the card payment, cannot be sent any more, or is still
  unsent after a week, saying whether to retry the invoice or record the
  payment by hand. Members see no change.
- **A refund credit-note job that stalls in Xero no longer overwrites the note
  an officer recorded by hand (#4426).** A refund credit-note job can stall in
  Xero, be marked failed with **Reset stale running** or **Mark failed**, and
  then be resolved by hand with the number of the credit note the officer
  made. If the stalled job then came back with a note of its own, it replaced
  the officer's note on the job, linked its own note to the payment and
  recorded a refund payment against it in Xero, so Xero could hold two credit
  notes for one refund and the app lost track of the hand-made one.

  The officer's note now stays recorded. The late note is not recorded,
  linked, or paid against in Xero; the audit log gets one Xero entry naming it,
  and the finance contacts get one **Xero Sync Error** email naming it, its
  amount, the booking and the note the job keeps: check the late note in Xero,
  and that it is not recorded on the payment, before voiding it. If the late
  note is the very one the officer recorded (its answer was lost and the
  officer found it), nothing is sent. A job only marked failed, or resolved
  without a note number, still records the late note as before.
- **Two updates to one Xero link at the same moment no longer lose a detail
  (#4445).** When the app adds details to a stored Xero link, such as a refund
  credit note's status or an invoice's payment count, it used to read the
  stored details and write them back with the new ones. Two updates landing
  together could each read the old details, and the later one then wiped out
  the earlier one's addition. A later repair or recount could then judge that
  link wrongly.

  The new details are now added to the stored ones in a single database step,
  so both updates keep what they wrote. Nothing changes in what is shown, and
  there is nothing to do. One detail stored outside this path, a treasurer's
  note on a voided bank-refund credit note, is no longer masked when a later
  update merges into the same link.
- **A failed Xero credit that the app could not close now says so (#4220).** In
  the Xero Operations list, a failure that is still active because a credit note
  was used in Xero outside the app shows a "Credit used outside the app" chip. It
  says the app could not close the row itself and that any amount still owed is
  chased from Xero. Nothing about the row's status or retry behaviour changes.
- **A changed booking's Xero invoice is no longer thrown away while Stripe is slow to cancel the old payment request (#4665).** When a member's booking change was replaced by a newer payment request, and Stripe had not yet confirmed the cancel of the old request (an outage, or a retry waiting its turn), the nightly tidy-up of old waiting invoices could cancel the old change's Xero invoice instead of moving it to the new request. When the member then paid, no invoice named that change, the booking's main invoice could be overpaid, and the booking-vs-Xero check reported a missing invoice. The tidy-up now leaves that invoice waiting until the cancel finishes, and the cancel's last step moves it to the new request, so the member's payment is invoiced for both changes, each for its own amount. A cancel that has given up for good is handled as before.
- **Checking erased-member Xero contacts no longer risks losing link details.**
  Recording what Xero said about a contact left behind by an erasure now merges
