  browser's, which is what selects the retroactive pricing path; a life member's
  date no longer reads a day early; a family member's date of birth on a
  membership application no longer shares a formatter with the application's
  submission and review timestamps; partner-invitation expiry and family-group
  creation times on the family groups screen now follow the club; the
  promo-code redemption list's on-screen "Redeemed" time now matches the day
  already used for its export filename; on the family-group request review
  screen, a declared date of birth is now shown as the day it was declared while
  the "Requested" stamp beside it is converted into club time, so approving a
  request can no longer record a birthday a day out - which matters because the
  day decides an age tier, and the age tier decides a price band; a member's
  "last stay" now reads the same day in the summary strip at the top of their
  page and in the history line below it, instead of differing by a day; the
  payments screen's default "last updated" range now covers the whole of the
  club's day, where it previously cut off partway through it and dropped the most
  recent payments from the officer's view with nothing on screen to say so; and
  the dashboard's hut-leader coverage card now counts the same nights as the
  roster and bed-allocation cards beside it on a day boundary.

  Clubs whose recorded timezone matches the timezone their server was already
  running in will see no change at all.
- **The events calendar now shows club time to everyone, wherever they are
  reading it from (#2870).** The month calendar at `/calendar` and
  `/admin/calendar` worked out what day it was, and which day each event
  belonged to, from the **reader's own computer**. For a club whose members are
  all in one country that was invisible; for anyone looking at the calendar from
  overseas it was wrong. The times of day were a separate problem with the same
  cause: they were correct for the club, but they came from a timezone fixed
  when the software was built rather than from the one recorded in the admin
  Club Time settings, so changing that setting could not move them.

  What a member or an officer will notice:

  - the month heading over the grid is the club's current month. It could
    previously be the **previous month** for any club west of Greenwich,
    because of how the heading was worked out;
  - the highlighted "today" ring is on the club's today, and the "Today"
    button jumps to the club's current month;
  - an evening event stays on the evening it happens at the lodge, instead of
    sliding onto the neighbouring day's square for a reader in another
    timezone;
  - the times on the coloured event chips, in the day list and in an event's own
    detail panel follow the club timezone recorded in the admin settings. They
    were already the club's times rather than the reader's, so most clubs will
    see no change here - what changes is that an operator who moves the setting
    is now followed without the server being reconfigured;
  - when an officer opens an existing event to edit it, the date and time boxes
    are filled in with the club's date and time. Saving a 7pm event from
    overseas used to store 7pm in the **officer's** timezone, quietly moving
    the event for everybody else. It now stores 7pm at the club;
  - a new event opens on the club's today rather than the reader's;
  - the "Repeat" wording ("Weekly on Tuesday", "Monthly on the 3rd Tuesday")
    describes the day that was actually picked. An officer working from overseas
    could previously be offered "Weekly on Monday" for a date they had selected
    as a Tuesday.

  For repeating events, the whole series is now generated on the club's
  calendar and keeps the club's wall-clock time. That matters twice a year: a
  7pm series stays a 7pm series across a daylight-saving change instead of
  becoming 6pm or 8pm, and a rule anchored on "the third Tuesday" stays on the
  third Tuesday of the club's month. Which timezone the club is in is the one
  recorded in the admin Club Time settings, so an operator who changes it no
  longer has to have the server reconfigured for the calendar to follow.

  Nothing already stored is changed or moved, and there is nothing for an
  operator to do. One class of NEW event is written differently, and it is worth
  knowing about even though it is rare: on the spring morning when the clocks go
  forward there is an hour that does not happen, and an event created for a time
  inside it is now stored at the moment the clocks jumped to - 3:00 am where it
  would previously have been recorded as 3:30 am. That is the intended answer
  for a time that never existed, and it affects one hour of one day a year.
- **The last screens and services that worked out a date for themselves now ask
  the club's own calendar instead (#2870).** For a club in New Zealand nothing
  visible changes - every label, heading and filter is the same as before. For a
  club west of Greenwich, three of these were showing the wrong day, and the rest
  were one edit away from doing so.

  This is the sweep that finishes the club-time migration. Most of it is
  bookkeeping: forty-odd places had each written out their own copy of "which
  calendar day is this", "what is today at the club", or "how do we print this
  date", and they now share one answer. Where a screen was already printing the
  right day, it still prints exactly the same characters - the change is that
  there is now one place to correct rather than forty.

  Three were genuinely wrong rather than merely duplicated, all in finance and
  calendar surfaces that read a date through the server's timezone instead of
  the club's: a finance chart's month labels, a finance date-range picker, and
  the events calendar's own month heading. A club whose server sits behind
  Greenwich would have seen those name the previous day, and at the turn of a
  month, the previous month.
- **A rule in the developer documentation would have broken every scheduled job
  if somebody had followed it (#2870).** It said a module that nothing
  command-line-reachable touches should use the request-cached way of reading the
  club's timezone. Measured across the nine places that read it, only one is
  reachable that way - the other seven are the nightly jobs and the configuration
  transfer, and the check that decides "reachable" cannot see them by design,
  because the scheduler loads each job lazily at run time rather than importing
  it up front. Following the rule would have put a server-only guard on seven
  cron modules and broken each of them at its first tick. The rule now says so.
- **The admin sidebar's "Unpaid Finished Stays" link now uses the club's own day,
  and keeps using the right one when the tab is left open (#3123).**

  That link in the Needs Attention list opens the bookings list filtered to stays
  that have already ended and are still unpaid, and the number in the badge
  beside it counts exactly the same thing. The filter's cut-off date was being
  worked out from the timezone of the machine the site runs on, while the count
  was worked out from the timezone the club has saved on its own settings page.
  For a club whose two do not match, the link and the number beside it were
  describing different days - so the list could open a booking short, or one long,
  of what the badge had promised. The same link is offered in the Ctrl-K search
  palette, which had the same cut-off and therefore the same discrepancy.

  Separately, and in every timezone, that cut-off was worked out **once** when the
  page was first loaded and never again. An administrator who left the admin panel
  open overnight came back to yesterday's filter sitting next to a count that had
  been refreshed for today. Both the link and the palette now work the date out
  each time they are drawn, from one shared place, so the two can no longer
  disagree with each other and neither goes stale.

  Nothing needs configuring. A club whose saved timezone matches its server's -
  which is every club today - sees only the second fix: the link keeps up with the
  date, instead of being frozen at whenever the page was opened.
- **The bed board's default seven-night window now starts on the club's own day
  (#3123).**

  Opening **Admin → Bed Allocation** without picking dates shows the next seven
  nights starting today. "Today" was read from the server's timezone rather than
  the club's, and the same default was used by the board's **Auto-allocate** and
  **Approve** actions when they are run without an explicit date range - so for a
  club whose saved timezone is behind its server's, those two could allocate and
  approve over a window starting a day early. All three now start from the club's
  own day, worked out once per request.

  For a club whose saved timezone matches its server's the window is unchanged.
  For any other, the board opens on the club's date and the two write actions act
  on the same nights the board is showing.
- **An exported report's cover date and its filename can no longer disagree
  (#3123).** The PDF an officer downloads from the Reports screen stamps
  "Generated: 16 April 2026" on its first page and puts the same day in the saved
  file's name. Those were two separate readings of the clock, taken a few seconds
  apart with the page capture in between - so an export running across the club's
  midnight produced a file named for one day whose cover said another, in a
  document somebody keeps and later files by date. Both now come from a single
  reading.
- **A booking page decides once what day it is (#3123).** The "take myself off
  this stay" card and the guest-consent card beside it each worked out the club's
  current day for themselves, rather than using the one the page had already
  resolved for its other checks. Across the club's midnight that could offer a
  member a self-removal button that the very next check refused, or hide one they
  were still entitled to. Both cards now read the page's single answer.
- **Public fee and policy pages no longer print their season dates through a
  hard-coded New Zealand timezone (#3123).** The date ranges beside each season,
  booking period and cancellation period were formatted through
  `Pacific/Auckland` written into the code, rather than through the club's own
  settings - and the values being formatted are plain calendar dates that need no
  timezone at all. The published wording is unchanged for New Zealand clubs; a
  club elsewhere no longer has this one club's timezone baked into its public
  pages.
- **Mountain Conditions shows trails again after Whakapapa's website update
  (contributed from the triyder fork, triyder#45).** Whakapapa moved its
  trail lists behind collapsible panels
  whose content is no longer part of the page itself, which left the Trails
  section of the scraped report empty. The scraper now reads the same data
  feed the panels draw from whenever the page carries no trails, so every
  area's trails - name, open/closed status, groomed flag and difficulty -
  come through as before. Nothing changes for the other sections, and no
  admin action is needed.
- **Someone whose only admin job is the money can now get into the admin area to
  do it - and still cannot get at anything else (#2984, #2975).** A club that
  gave somebody the "Finance Viewer" or "Treasurer" role, and nothing else, had
  handed them a job they could not fully reach. The system had two different
  ideas about whether such a person counted as an administrator: parts of it
  said no and hid the Admin link, other parts said yes and pointed them at the
  Payments screen. The visible symptom was small and confusing - pages that
  needed the list of lodge names to say *which* lodge a payment was for came up
  empty for them, with no way for an administrator to fix it from the Access
  Roles screen.

  Holding any one of the seven admin areas - Overview, Bookings, Membership,
  Finance, Lodge Operations, Content, or Support - now counts as being an
  administrator, and the Admin link appears. That is the whole of the change:
  being let in the front door grants nothing on its own. Every screen, every
  action and every underlying request still asks for the specific area it
  belongs to, exactly as before. A finance-only administrator reaches the admin
  area and the Finance screens and nothing else - they cannot open Members,
  Bookings, Site Content, Access Roles or Settings, and they cannot change
  anything in Finance either if their role is view-only.

  A Full Admin is unaffected in every respect.

  Three smaller tightenings ship with it. The built-in help assistant used to
  decide which help text to give an administrator by asking only "are you an
  administrator", which meant any administrator could ask it for the help page
  of any admin screen, including ones they cannot open. It now asks whether they
  could open that screen. Nobody loses anything by this - asking about the page
  you are looking at always works. The roster on the Notification Recipients
  screen now lists finance-only administrators alongside everyone else; who
  actually receives which alert is unchanged, because every alert is still
  matched to the recipient's own areas. And AI Diagnostics - the "why is this
  booking stuck" assistant - now opens for any administrator, which is what it
  was always meant to do: it used to be offered to everyone in the admin area but
  answered "forbidden" to anyone without the Overview permission, which after
  this change is exactly the finance-only administrator the release exists for.
  It still shows nobody anything their own permissions would not show them.

  Underneath, this release also adds a permanent check that the admin area's
  permissions really are enforced. It walks every admin screen and every admin
  request the software has and tries each one as sixteen different kinds of
  administrator, using the real permission check each request performs rather
  than an assumption about it, so a future change that let the wrong role
  through - or shut the right one out - fails the build instead of reaching a
  club. Where a request asks for something different from what its address
  suggests, every one of those is now written down with the reason, and a new one
  appearing without a reason fails too.
- **Pressing Edit on a fee now brings the form into view (#3255).** On the
  admin Fees page, the Edit buttons for hut-fee seasons and for individual
  joining and annual fees sit in lists below the form they open, which renders
  at the top of its panel - so pressing Edit appeared to do nothing and the
  filled-in form opened off the top of the screen. The page now scrolls the
  panel into view when the form opens. Nothing about how fees are calculated
  or stored changed.
- **The Modules reference now lists every module, and cannot quietly fall
  behind again (#2996).** Three modules that were already on the Admin →
  Modules page - the AI help assistant, Maintenance reports and the Alpine
  Central Server connection - had no row in the operator guide's settings
  reference, so an administrator reading the guide could not find what they
  did or how they ship. All three are documented now, with their defaults.

  Behind the scenes, the guide's table is checked against the application's own
  module list every time the test suite runs, in both directions: a module with
  no row, a row for a module that no longer exists, a wrong label or a wrong
  default all fail the build. The second, unchecked copy of that table in
  `CONFIGURATION.md` - which had already drifted - is gone, replaced by a
  pointer to the guide. The setup-readiness check also reads the module
  list from that one place instead of keeping its own copy, so a new module
  reaches the readiness page the moment it is added. No module behaviour or
  default changed.
- **Signed money amounts are formatted by one shared helper (#3264).** The
  "+$25.00" / "-$120.00" style used for promo adjustments, booking-history
  deltas and finance report changes was written out seven times, and the
  copies had started to differ: three showed a zero adjustment as "-$0.00",
  and the promo-code box on the booking form dropped the thousands separator
  ("-$1234.56") and ignored the club's configured currency. All seven screens
  now share the club's standard money formatter, so a zero shows as "$0.00" and
  larger amounts read "-$1,234.56" everywhere.

  The same tidy-up reaches every amount on two screens, which is worth saying
  plainly: the member's booking review step and the admin booking page each
  carried their own copy of the plain money formatter as well, so their totals,
  per-guest prices, applied credit, remaining-to-pay and account-credit balance
  now read "$1,234.56" in the club's configured currency where they previously
  read "$1234.56" with a hard-coded dollar sign. The amounts themselves are
  unchanged. The finance-manager access check
  is likewise imported from its single defining module, and the finance
  dashboard's chart value types and badge tones are typed from the components
  that render them, so a new option cannot be added on one side and silently
  missed on the other.
- **Integer-cent money has one formatter (#3302).** `formatCents` (an integer
  cent amount to a dollar string) had been copied at many call sites - the
  admin payments and refund-requests pages, the member account-credit
  section and its equivalent admin screen, the audit log description
  builder, the booking-cancellation dialog, several booking-cancellation and
  refund-appeal messages, and others a follow-up review found - all quietly
  repeating the pre-#3264 bug pattern: a hard-coded `$`, no thousands
  grouping, the club's configured currency ignored. Every one of those now
  reads the shared helper. Larger amounts (over $999) gain grouping, and a
  **negative amount's sign now sits before the `$`** (`-$25.00`, not the old
  `$-25.00`) - matching `formatSignedCents` (#3264) and the locale
  convention. That sign change reaches a few places a member or admin can
  see it directly: an audit log's price-difference line, the account-credit
  history on both the member's and the admin's screen, and an admin refund
  email whose remaining-balance line can be negative. See the pull request
  description for the exact list and reasoning.

  Two genuinely different renderings stay distinct rather than becoming more
  copies, both now a separate named function, `formatCentsPlain`, rather
  than an option on `formatCents` (so calling the wrong one is a different
  import, not a different argument): the AI assistant and AI Diagnostics
  monthly spend-cap editors, which show a bare two-decimal number for an
  editable input, and the Xero refund-note repair report, which renders a
  bare decimal delta (and "unknown" for an amount not yet known) rather than
  a currency string. Both are pinned by existing test fixtures and are
  byte-identical to before.

  One report-only formatter composes from the shared helper for its dollar
  arithmetic but keeps its own local decoration, because it is a genuine
  rendering difference no fixture pinned away: the Xero invoice rounding
  audit's compound `"$1.50 (+150c)"` line (the dollar half now groups
  thousands like every other screen; only the parenthesised raw-cents
  suffix is local). A club's configured currency now formats consistently
  everywhere this issue reached.

  **The instrument the issue asked for:** a new lint rule bans hand-rolling
  `(cents / 100).toFixed(n)` anywhere in `src/`, so a future twelfth copy of
  this formatter fails the build instead of quietly regrowing - the pattern
  three separate merges in this same epic have already shown regrows without
  one. A short, reasoned exemption list covers the genuinely different cases
  (an editable input's plain value and a raw numeric export cell).
- **AI spend caps are now counted in the club's own currency (#3354).** The
  AI help assistant and AI Diagnostics price their usage in New Zealand dollars.
  For a club configured for another currency, the monthly caps read as the
  club's money but were compared against a New Zealand-dollar figure, so they
  were off by the exchange rate, and the module descriptions said "NZ$10" and
  "NZ$0" whatever the club's currency.

  Both AI settings pages gain a **Currency for AI spend** card: an administrator
  with support-edit access enters how many units of the club's currency one New
  Zealand dollar buys, and the card shows the rate and when it was last set, so a
  stale rate is visible rather than silent. Every estimate is converted through
  that one shared rate (rounded up, so the caps still trip early rather than
  late) before it counts against a cap, and the caps and spend figures render in
  the configured currency. Until a rate is set, spend is counted as if one New
  Zealand dollar were one unit of the club's currency, which is exactly how it
  was counted before, so nothing changes for a club that does not act. A New
  Zealand club sees a one-sentence note that no conversion applies and nothing
  to set. Past usage is not re-priced. One new settings table; the rate, like
  the caps, does not travel in a config-transfer bundle. A change to the rate is
  recorded in the audit log under the `admin` category, exactly as changes to
  the two AI spend caps already are, so it is readable with the same
  support-view access.
- **Lowering a lodge's capacity now warns how many partner spots it removes.**
  On the lodge configuration screen, typing a capacity lower than the saved one
  shows how many partner-shared double-bed spots the change takes away, before
  you save, including when the lodge has no saved capacity yet and any figure
  you type would remove spots. Nothing is shown when raising, when unchanged, or when the lodge has
  no shareable double beds; the save is never blocked. See the
  [capacity model](docs/CAPACITY_MODEL.md).
- **A failed save on an admin screen now always says why (#3445).** About two
  dozen admin screens each carried their own copy of the code that turns a
  refused request into the sentence an officer sees, and the copies had drifted:
  on most of them a refusal with a blank message showed an empty red alert, and
  on nine a refusal whose message was not text showed the words
  "[object Object]".

  Those twenty-one copies, and eight further one-line readings in the same
  screens, now read the refusal one way. A blank message falls back to the
  screen's own fixed sentence, such as "Failed to save membership type", and a
  message that is not text does the same. A real message still shows exactly as
  the server wrote it. Screens whose messages carry extra detail - the email
  template editor's list of what to fix, the finance mapping panel's details,
  and the Xero actions' recovery hints - keep that detail on top of the same
  rule. One converged screen is member-facing: the two-factor sign-in panel,
  where a blank refusal now reads a sentence instead of an empty alert.

  Not every screen is covered yet. A check now fails the build if anyone writes
  a new private copy of the rule as a function, but the same reading written
  inline into a handler survives on many screens beyond these, and converging
  those is a filed follow-up. No server response changed.
- **Stay dates are now read the same way on every screen.** A booking or season
  date that arrives in an unusual form, an offset-less timestamp such as
  `2026-07-04T13:45:00`, used to show a dash on some admin screens and the raw
  text on the public token pages. It now shows the day it names, "4 Jul 2026",
  everywhere. Every value a route actually emits, and every fallback for a value
  that is not a date at all, renders exactly as before. Behind it, one decoder (`formatStayDate` and
  `formatStayDateOrNull`) now replaces about forty copies, and a check fails the
  build if a new one appears.
- **The money census now shows what the stored night prices are made of, and
  which edits went to a person, month by month (#3531, stage 3 of 3).**
  `npm run booking-money:census` - read-only, one snapshot - adds night rows by
  provenance and guest strands by the edit gate's own verdict (`EXACT`, or the
  cause an edit would park with) per booking-creation month, and every edit
  financial review by cause per month, beside the reconciliation verdicts it
  already reported. The two share one cause vocabulary: what the gate would
  park against what it did park. Run it before and after a deploy and the
  effect of the earlier two stages reads off as one line against another.
- **Every amount a person reads now says `$84.50`, not `8450 cents` (#3533).**
  The audit trail's own sentences, operator report lines, cron summaries and
  error messages render money through the shared `formatCents` - 30 sites, seven
  of them in the cancellation path alone - and the admin audit-log's metadata
  panel annotates every `…Cents` key with the amount beside the stored number
  (`"refundAmountCents": 2275,  // $22.75`). Nothing stored changed: money is
  still whole cents, existing audit rows are untouched, and a new lint arm now
  fails the build on the next `${someCents} cents` sentence.
- **The club's currency and its number and date format are now settings a Full
  Administrator can change, instead of values only somebody with access to the
  server could set (#3563).** They live at **Admin → Setup & Configuration →
  Club Currency & Locale**, and the operator guide is
  `docs/guides/club-format.md`.

  Nothing changes for an existing club on upgrade. On the first start after
  upgrading, the values the installation was already using are copied into the
  new setting, so a club running in New Zealand dollars stays in New Zealand
  dollars and nobody has to do anything. From then on the recorded setting is
  the authority for the setting: changing `CURRENCY` or `LOCALE` on the server
  no longer changes what the page shows. **Keep those server settings in
  place, and keep them matching this page.** Every **amount** the site writes
  is still worked out from them, and removing them would leave the site
  writing New Zealand dollars while the page shows your club's real choice.

  **This entry is the setting; #3564's entry below is the screens.** On its
  own this change only records the club's choice - which is why it is worth
  reading #3564's entry in this release before you decide what to expect,
  because that is where the screens are moved onto it and where the ones that
  have not moved are named. No amount already recorded is rewritten or
  re-converted by either - an amount of 8450 cents is still 8450 cents, and
  this setting only ever decides how one is written.

  Changing either value needs an explicit confirmation and is written to the
  audit log with who did it and what it was before. Only a Full Administrator
  can see or change the page; an administrator holding every other permission
  at edit cannot. An invalid currency code or language tag is refused with a
  message saying what a valid one looks like.
- **Card payment code no longer guesses the currency (#3563).** The two places
  that create a card charge used to fall back to the server's currency setting
  when a caller did not say which currency to use. Every caller now states it,
  so the answer is visible where the charge is made rather than hidden in a
  default. No charge is taken in a different currency than before, and nothing
  about how any amount is calculated changed.
- **The currency and number format you set in the admin panel now reach the
  screens (#3564).** The entry above made the club's currency and its number
  and date format a recorded setting a Full Administrator can change, at
  **Admin → Setup & Configuration → Club Currency & Locale**. On its own that
  changed no screen. Ten screens now follow it.

  A club outside New Zealand sees its own currency code beside a hut fee, a
  nightly rate, a membership or joining fee, a promo-code amount, a monthly AI
  spend cap and a booking-request total. The audit log writes its dates and
  times the club's way, and so does every row of the health dashboard, a
  promo-code export notice groups its counts the club's way, and the lobby
  display writes its date the club's way. None of this needed a rebuild or a
  change on the server, which is the point: those values were previously
  frozen into the software when it was built, so a club could set them and be
  ignored.

  **Two clocks on those screens deliberately did not move, and will look odd
  until the next change.** The "Last refresh" line at the top of the health
  dashboard, and the live clock on the lobby display, are written by the
  shared date machinery rather than by their own screen, so they still follow
  the server's `LOCALE` while the rows and the date beneath them follow your
  setting. Nothing is wrong if you notice it; the next change moves that
  machinery and the mismatch goes away.

  **Keep the server's `CURRENCY` and `LOCALE` in place, and keep them matching
  the page.** Every **amount** the site writes - a price, an invoice figure, a
  statement line, an email total - is still written from them, along with
  every date outside the screens listed above and the two clocks just named,
  and those move across in the next two changes. If the two disagree you will
  now see your chosen currency code sitting beside amounts written the old
  way, on the same screen. That is the mismatch to avoid; the admin page, the
  operator guide, `CONFIGURATION.md` and `.env.example` all say so, and each
  will stop saying it as its part becomes true.

  Nothing already recorded is rewritten or re-converted: an amount of 8450 cents
  is still 8450 cents, and this setting only ever decides how one is written.

  **One installation will see a change it did not ask for, and it is the
  intended one.** If you build your own image and the currency baked into that
  build differs from the one set in the running container's environment, the
  screens above were showing the build's value while the recorded setting held
  the container's. They now show the recorded setting. That is the defect this
  work exists to fix, but it is worth knowing before you notice it.
- **The currency and locale you set in the admin panel now reach every amount
  the product writes (#3565).** Since the previous release a club has been able
  to record its currency and the way it formats numbers under Admin, but nothing
  read that setting: every amount on every screen, in every email and in every
  description sent to Xero was still rendered from the value frozen into the
  server image when it was built. That is the defect this programme exists to
  fix, and this release fixes it for money in one move.

  Every screen that shows an amount - the booking flow, the member dashboard and
  booking pages, the admin bookings, payments, refunds, promo codes, members,
  fees, subscriptions, reports, health and AI pages, the finance dashboard, the
  lobby display and the public booking-request and payment pages - every email
  that names an amount, and every line of text this product writes into Xero,
  now renders in the currency and number format your club recorded. There is no
  longer a way to write out an amount without saying which club's format it is
  in, so no future screen can quietly fall back to the server's own value.

  **What a club on the shipped New Zealand defaults will notice: nothing.** Every
  amount is rendered byte-for-byte as before, in screens, emails and Xero text
  alike, which is checked by test against the formatter that was retired.

  **What a club that has changed its currency will notice:** every amount, on
  every surface, now shows the currency you recorded. This release is money
  only: dates and times still follow the server's `LOCALE` setting and move
  in a later release (#3566), so keep
  that one matching the format you recorded until then. Nothing about how money
  is calculated, charged or refunded changes - this is entirely about how an
  amount is written out.
- **Every admin can now see the club's currency and locale; only a Full Admin
  can change them (#3596).** Until now the **Club Currency & Locale** page was
  for Full Admins only, so a treasurer or a bookings officer trying to work out
  why an amount or a date was written a certain way could not check the setting
  that decides it.

  Any admin can now open the page from **Admin → Setup & Configuration → Club
  Currency & Locale** and read both values, where each came from, and who last
  changed them. Admins who are not Full Admins see them read-only, under a note
  saying changing them needs Full Admin, and the **Change currency and format**
  button is greyed out for them. The server still refuses a change from anyone
  but a Full Admin. Nothing else changes: saving still needs the same
  confirmation and is still recorded in the audit log, and the Club Time Zone
  and Environment Safety pages stay Full Admin only to open as well as to change.
- **Dates and times now follow the locale you set in the admin panel, and AI
  spend is counted in your club's own currency (#3566).** Since the previous
  release every amount has followed the currency and format recorded under
  Admin → Club Currency & Locale, but dates and times were still written the way
  the server's `LOCALE` setting said - and in the published image that meant New
  Zealand English for every club. This release finishes the job: every date and
  time on screen, in the club's time zone, is now written the way the club
  recorded, including the lobby display's clock, the health dashboard's "Last
  refresh" line, the audit log, the stuck-states page and the induction record.
  Emails follow too, as soon as the setting is saved, and the daily chore-roster
  email - which always wrote its date the New Zealand way - now does as well.
  Alphabetical order on the lockers list and in photo galleries follows the same
  setting.

  **What a club on the shipped New Zealand defaults will notice: nothing.** Every
  date, time and amount is written byte-for-byte as before, on screen and in
  email, which is checked by test against the formatters that were retired.

  **What a club on another format will notice:** dates in its own style - for
  `de-CH`, for example, a 24-hour clock and German month names, which can make
  the lobby display's date line a little wider. The date labels along the bottom
  of the report charts (such as "Apr 16") are still written in English; that is
  a known limitation, noted in the operator guide.

  **AI spend now uses the club's recorded currency.** The monthly AI caps were
  already labelled in it, but spend was still converted using the server's
  `CURRENCY` setting, so a club that had switched currency in the panel could not
  set a conversion rate at all and had its spend counted as if one New Zealand
  cent were one cent of its own money. Now the cap and the spend are in the same
  currency. **Changing the club's currency now clears the AI spend conversion
  rate** - it was set for the old currency - and the audit log records that as
  `AI_SPEND_CURRENCY_RATE_CLEARED`; re-enter the rate for the new currency on the
  AI settings page. That new audit record is readable by anyone with support
  view access, like the rate record beside it; it carries two currency codes, a
  rate and the administrator's id, and no member data.

  The server's `CURRENCY` and `LOCALE` settings now do nothing an existing club
  can see; they only seed a brand-new installation. The one thing still taken
  from `CURRENCY` is the currency card payments are charged in, which the next
  stage (#3567) decides.
- **Finance figures drop soft-deleted bookings (#3745).** Guest nights,
  occupancy, booked revenue, the payment status counts, outstanding and
  collected additional payments, and the booking hut fees the P&L view compares
  with Xero no longer count a booking an admin has deleted. Net Collected
  already left deleted bookings out (#3637), so every Finance figure now counts
  the same bookings, the same as Reports' default view. The admin delete
  action only deletes bookings that are already cancelled (INV-ADDPAY-030),
  which Finance already left out, so most clubs will see no change: a figure
  moves only where a direct database edit left a deleted booking with a stay
  status.
- **The legacy dashboard booking export leaves deleted bookings out too
  (#3745).** Its past-stay and forward-pipeline lists no longer include a
  booking an admin has deleted, so they match the Finance dashboard. Deleted
  bookings are always cancelled, which the export already left out, so most
  clubs will see no change here either.
- **Money fields now offer whole-dollar controls (#3414).** Administrators can
  use accessible up and down controls or arrow keys to adjust a dollar amount by
  one whole dollar, while direct entry accepts up to two decimal places.
- **The admin dashboard no longer shows a Bed Allocation card when the club has
  bed allocation switched off (#3841).** Before this, a club that doesn't use
  bed allocation still saw the card, and it counted every guest due in the next
  seven days as "awaiting a bed", a number that could never be cleared. Its link
  also led to a page that is closed while the module is off. The card now
  appears only when bed allocation is on, as the bookings list and the
  stuck-state checks already behave. Nothing changes for clubs that use bed
  allocation.
- **The Public fee and policy blocks panel can no longer lock itself up over a
  hidden Book Now page, and deleting a page handles its rare edge cases
  (#3852).** If the **Book Now** button was hidden while it still pointed at a
  page that was later hidden, every **Save visibility** failed with a generic
  message and the controls that could fix it were not on screen. The target
  choices now stay visible whenever a page target is saved, and a failed save
  shows the server's own reason, which names the setting to change.

  Deleting a page is also safer in the uncommon cases. The audit log copy of a
  deleted page is now the page as it was at the moment it was removed, so an
  edit made just before the delete is not lost; the message after the delete
  says when that copy is not complete because part of the page was redacted or
  too large to keep. Two officers deleting the same page at once now get one
  delete and one "page not found", not an error. A **Book Now** setting left
  pointing at a deleted page is set back to the booking flow and the message
  says so. A settings save whose chosen page is deleted at the same moment is
  refused with the usual "not published" message rather than an error. The
  delete confirmation now says when its footer or **Book Now** check could not
  run, and that links written as relative addresses are not detected; the
  "could not clear the stored copy" message no longer promises it clears in a
  few minutes, and says that saving any page clears it.
- **A hut-leader label saved as a plural no longer reads "Hut Leaderss" (#3976).**
  The admin sidebar and a few other screens built the plural by adding an "s"
  to the club's hut-leader label, so a club that had typed "Hut Leaders" saw
  "Hut Leaderss". A label that already ends in "s" is now left as typed.

  The Hut-leader label field (Admin → Appearance → Identity) now says to enter
  the singular, for example "Hut Leader". A club whose label is plural should
  change it to the singular, because the singular wording elsewhere ("held for
  a hut leader") still uses the label exactly as saved.
- **Club identity now opens read-only, with Edit, Save and Cancel (#3976).**
  Under Admin → Appearance → Identity, the club name, short name, hut-leader
  label and Facebook URL fields are read-only until you click **Edit**.
  **Save club identity** only becomes available once something has changed,
  and **Cancel** restores the last saved values. Save and load messages now
  appear at the top of the section instead of as pop-up notifications.
- **Finance diagnostics now say what each queued card refund or cancel is (#4076).**
  A refund queued to the group organiser's card (for a joiner's booking edit, a
  group cancellation or an approved refund appeal), a retry of an older whole-group
  refund, an officer-confirmed edit refund or charge, a booking edit's own refund,
  the refund of a payment made on an already-replaced payment request, and an
  approved late-capture refund were each reported as another scenario or as an
  unrecognised recovery. Each now carries its own scenario code and a plain-English
  label, and the labels moved into the tool descriptions so they no longer take
  room from the rows. A test fails when an export of `payment-recovery-keys.ts` is
  neither mapped to a scenario nor declared not a recovery key. Read-only
  diagnostics; the recovery key builders moved into `payment-recovery-keys.ts`
  with their output unchanged, and nothing about payments behaves differently.
- **Keyboard focus now returns to the Edit button after Save or Cancel in
  admin settings sections (#4087).** Saving or cancelling a settings section
  used to drop keyboard and screen-reader users to the top of the page,
  because the button they had just pressed disappeared. Focus now goes back
  to the section's Edit button (or the Add or row Edit button for booking
  periods and minimum-stay policies), or to the section itself when Edit is
  not available. Pages that move to the top after a successful save, such as
  Member fields, still do. A save that fails keeps the section open and puts
  focus back on Save if the browser had dropped it. Mouse users in Chrome and
  Edge also see the Edit button scroll back into view, because those browsers
  focus a button when it is clicked. Nothing needs configuring.
- **Keyboard focus now stays in the list after a minimum-stay policy or
  date-specific period is activated, deactivated or deleted (#4116).** These
  buttons reload the list, which used to drop keyboard and screen-reader users
  to the top of the page. Activate and Deactivate now keep focus on the same
  row's button. Delete moves focus to an Edit button, never to a button that
  would change something on a stray key press: the same policy's Edit for a
  minimum-stay policy (which stays listed as inactive), and the next period's
  Edit for a date-specific period (the previous one's for the last period). If
  that row is gone, or the list could not be reloaded, focus goes to the card.
  A delete that fails returns focus to the row it was pressed on. Each row's
  buttons now also announce which policy or period they belong to. Nothing
  needs configuring.
- **Pressing Edit in an admin settings section now moves keyboard focus into
  the section (#4115).** In most settings sections, pressing Edit used to drop
  keyboard and screen-reader users to the top of the page, because the Edit
  button they had just pressed disappeared. Focus now lands in the section:
  on the first field that Edit made editable, or on the section itself when
  there is no such field. Add and a row's Edit for booking periods and
  minimum-stay policies now put focus in the form they open. Allocation
  preferences and club identity keep their current behaviour. Nothing needs
  configuring.
- **Key-prefix lookups and prefix searches now match their prefix literally
  (#4146).** Prisma's `startsWith` runs as SQL `LIKE`, where `_` matches any
  character and `%` any run, so a lookup whose prefix carried an id could read a
  row belonging to a different booking or group settlement whose id differed
  only at that position. The duplicate-capture refund check (now also scoped to
  its booking) and a group settlement's organiser hand-back tasks now escape the
  prefix through one helper (`exactPrefix`). So do the prefixes people type: the
  admin Xero force-sync's member and booking id lookup, the admin member and
  booking searches, and the member guest search, where typing `%%` previously
  matched every name instead of acting as a prefix. The retirement of a
  payment's pending refund credit note is escaped too, for consistency only: it
  was not reachable, because that query is already scoped to the payment's
  `localId`. A real-PostgreSQL test pins both the wildcard and the fix, and a
  source census (`INV-SSOT-006`) keeps new lookups on the helper.
- **Admin searches match the characters you type (#4190).** Underscores,
  percent signs and backslashes are now literal in admin text searches, while
  matching still ignores letter case. Image and page reference checks also
  match the actual URL or path, so a similar address no longer appears as a
  reference merely because it differs at an underscore or percent sign.
- **The audit log's category filters now match action names exactly (#4165).**
  For older activity entries recorded without a category, the Admin Audit Log
  and a member's own activity timeline decide the category from the action's
  name. Those name checks treated `_` as "any character" (in the starts-with
  checks and in the one contains check that has one, `DATA_EXPORT`), so the Xero
  filter's `xero_` check also picked up every `xero.` entry, such as a Xero operation
  marked failed or a contact synced to a member. The checks now match the name
  exactly, and the `xero.` entries are named on the Xero filter on purpose, so
  nothing moves: every action the platform writes, and every action in the
  recorded history of uncategorised entries, stays under the same category and
  on the same member timelines as before. A real-PostgreSQL test pins that.
- **A club's Join page can now show what it costs to join as one figure per kind
  of member (#4295).** Until now the page could only show the joining fee and
  the annual subscription in two separate blocks, and the visitor had to add
  them up. A new `{{first-year-costs}}` block shows the total directly: the
  joining fee plus the first year's subscription, for each publicly listed
  membership type and age group, for example "Adult $390, Youth $155, Family
  $500".

  The totals are worked out from the same fee schedules and exemptions the
  invoicing uses, so a new schedule is reflected from the day it takes effect,
  with nothing to edit. A page served from the site's short cache can lag a
  schedule that starts today by a few minutes. A family is shown as its joining
  fee plus its flat per-family subscription, so the family rule is whatever the
  club has set in the Fees screen; a per-member family fee is not multiplied by
  the number of members, so a club should price its family with a per-family
  fee. A group that needs a subscription but has no annual fee set is left out
  rather than shown at its joining fee alone, which would look like the whole
  cost, and a group exempt from the subscription (for example young children)
  shows its joining fee only. A subscription that is reduced for people joining
  part-way through the season is shown as "up to".

  The block only appears when both the Joining fees and Annual membership fees
  visibility switches in Page Content are on. Nothing changes for a club that
  does not use the block, and nothing about invoicing or fees changes.
- **Cron health no longer turns a Xero job amber over one routinely skipped
  row (#4375).** A Xero outbox or replay run that worked its batch, but passed
  over a row another caller had already claimed or finished, was recorded as
  SKIPPED and shown as a warning. It now records SUCCESS. SKIPPED is kept for a
  run that did no work: Xero off or not connected, a credit-sync check that
  already ran this interval, or a sweep with nothing to read. An outbox or
  replay run still shows a warning when rows failed, or when Xero refused rows
  before any call (an outage cooldown, the daily limit or the environment
  check), naming how many and where to look.
- **Setup wizards save the step you are on in order (#4014).** The Xero,
  Stripe, Google and Lobby Display setup wizards remember which step you were
  on, so a return from a provider's sign-in page picks up where you were. Two
  quick step changes could rarely save those positions out of order, so the Xero
  wizard could come back from connecting one step behind; this was seen in the
  automated browser tests. The wizard now sends its position saves one at a
  time and keeps the last one alive when you leave for the provider's page.
  Nothing about what each step checks has changed.
- **The database backup setup wizard now remembers which step you were on
  (#4409).** Like the Xero, Stripe, Google and display setup wizards, leaving
  it and coming back opens where you left off, instead of at step 1. Admins
  with access to Backups can see and save that position; nothing else about
  who can change backup settings has changed.
- **Setup wizards wait for a save to finish before letting you move on
  (#4410).** While a step in the Xero, Stripe, Google, backup or display setup
  wizard is still saving, Continue, Back and the other steps are briefly
  disabled. Before, replacing the Xero credentials and pressing Connect straight
  away could let the save finish during the connection and undo it, leaving
  Xero showing Not Connected.
- **Error messages are readable in dark mode, payment-option and calendar
  text is no longer faded, and doubled buttons are gone (#4553).** In dark mode, red error text and the red error
  boxes used a dark red that was very hard to read on the dark background. They
  now use the lighter red the status labels already use. Light mode and printed
  pages look the same as before.

  The short descriptions under the Card and Internet Banking payment choices
  (group bookings, joining a group, and admin booking for a member) and the
  times in the calendar's event lists were faded below a readable contrast.
  They now use their normal text colour.

  Fourteen buttons that go to another page, such as "New Booking", "Back
  to sign in" and "View in Xero", were a button inside a link, so keyboard and
  screen-reader users met two controls for one action. Each is now one link
  that looks the same as before. A lint rule now stops a link and a button
  from being nested again.
- **A failing page no longer throws you out of the area you were in (#4467).** Every area - admin, the member pages, finance, the lodge kiosk, sign-in and the public website - now has its own error screen, shown inside that area's navigation instead of the site-wide one. **Try again** reloads just the failed page from the server, a link takes you back to the area's home page, and only an error ID is shown, never the technical message. No new loading placeholders were added, but every existing one now tells screen-reader users that the page is loading.
- **The committee role form now points at what needs fixing (#4467).** When a
  role cannot be saved because a field is wrong, such as a missing role name
  or a role email that is not an address, the form says so next to that
  field, and a list at the top of the form names every problem and links to
  each field. The list takes the keyboard and screen-reader focus, so it is
  read out straight away. Before, the browser's own pop-up caught some of
  these, and the rest came back as a bare "Invalid input" at the top of the
  page.

  Saving a correct role works exactly as before. This form is the first on a
  shared form layer that other forms will move to.
- **Payment choices, inactive rows and error messages are clearer to read and
  hear (#4563).** On admin Book, the organiser's group settlement and the group
  join page, the chosen payment option (Card or Internet Banking) was shown by
  colour alone. It now shows a check mark and the word "Selected", and a screen
  reader announces which option is chosen, as the member booking screen already
  did.

  Inactive chores, committee roles and assignments, booking policies and
  periods, family members and fully covered hut-leader candidates are no longer
  greyed out to the point of being hard to read. They keep their normal text
  and say "Inactive" or "Archived"; inactive cards also have a dashed border.

  In light mode, error messages use a slightly darker red, so they stay
  readable when they appear on a grey panel. On the committee page, the row
  edit and remove buttons now tell a screen reader which role or member they
  act on.
- **More greyed-out text is now readable, and says what state it shows
  (#4594).** Several screens faded text to show a state, which made it hard to
  read. They now keep their normal text and say the state in words:

  - On the admin booking calendar, past days keep their bed counts and "+N
    more" buttons at full strength; past days stay grey, and a screen reader
    hears "past".
  - On the lodge kiosk, a guest who has left shows a "Departed" tag and a
    dashed outline instead of fading.
  - When editing a booking, a guest you have taken off stays crossed out and
    gains a "Removed" tag.
  - On Notification Recipients, an alert an admin cannot receive now reads
    "Locked:" followed by the reason, and a screen reader reads that reason
    with the checkbox.
  - A member already added as a guest, and the page editor's fixed slug and
    menu order, are no longer faded.
- Fixed three admin permission mismatches (#4581): the lodge hub hides the Lockers card from admins who cannot open `/admin/lockers` (membership area); `/admin/subscription-lockout` now needs the membership area, matching its API; and the Booking Rules hub (`/admin/setup/booking-rules`) opens for Booking Officers. No one gains access their API did not already allow.
- Fix: the lodge page offers the Seasons & Rates card only to admins who can open the fee console (bookings or finance), and reads the season count only for those the seasons API answers (bookings), so a lodge-only admin no longer sees a card that refuses them, and an unread count no longer says "No seasons yet" (#4643).
- Mount the booking-history money-reconciliation status after hydration so retained hidden server markup cannot contain a second verdict; share the existing payment-panel hydration boundary.
- **Bookings admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4807).**
  Bookings, Booking Requests, Booking Approvals, Booking Change Requests,
  Book on Behalf, Bed Allocation and the Waitlist now live under Bookings.
  The menu, bookmarks and other links still use today's addresses, and
  opening the new Bookings address for one of those pages brings you back
  to the address it has now.
- **Officers can pick which role's menu the sidebar shows, once admin hubs
  are switched on (#4811).** An officer who holds more than one admin role
  gets a "Show menu for" choice at the top of the sidebar: one entry per role,
  plus "All my roles". The menu then lists Home and the hubs that role can
  change, or the hubs it can view when it can change nothing. A Full Admin
  still sees every hub and is not offered the choice. Nothing about who can
  open a page changes, and the search box still finds every page the officer
  may open.

  The choice is saved in a browser cookie named `admin-menu-role`. It is sent
  only to admin pages, the page script cannot read it, and it has no expiry of
  its own: the browser keeps it until it is cleared or the officer picks "All
  my roles". While admin hubs are off, the choice is hidden and saving it
  answers as if the address were not there. Signing out does not clear it.
- **Five admin pages are merged into the pages they belonged with (#4796).**
  Family Suggestions is now the **Suggestions** tab of **Family Groups**. The
  cancellation settings (the old Membership Cancellation page) are now the
  **Settings** tab of **Cancellation Requests**, which replaces the Setup
  Wizard's Cancellation page as well. The Setup Wizard's **Booking Rules** page
  is part of **Bookings Setup**, and its **Operational Integrations** page is
  the **Integration readiness** section of **System Health**. Each old address
  redirects to the tab or section that holds its content, keeping
  any query string, so bookmarks and links keep working. No one can open
  anything they could not open before: each tab and section needs the same
  permission its old page did, and the Setup Wizard's cancellation content now
  needs the membership area, as every link on that page already did. Bookings
  Setup now shows each card only to an admin who can open its page.
- **The admin search box now finds every admin page you can open (#4797).**
  Pressing Ctrl + K (or ⌘ + K), or clicking **Search…** at the top of the admin
  sidebar, used to find only the pages the sidebar links. It now finds forty
  more, among them Chores, Lockers, Seasons, Rooms & Beds, Email Messages,
  Notification Rules, Membership Types, Site Style, the booking policy pages
  and the Stripe, Google, Xero and backup setup wizards. Results are grouped by
  area (Bookings, Finance, Lodge and so on), and the old sidebar section names
  such as "Lodge Operations" still find their pages. A page that was merged
  into another, such as Family Suggestions, is listed under its old name and
  opens the tab that now holds it.

  It still lists only pages you are allowed to open, and hides a page whose
  module is turned off. A lodge page opened from it starts on the club's first
  lodge; choose another lodge on the page.
- **Website admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4801).**
  Site Appearance & Content, Club Identity, Site Style, Site Content, Page
  Content, Site Banners, Image Manager and Mountain Conditions now live under
  Website. The menu, bookmarks and other links still use today's addresses,
  and opening the new Website address for one of those pages brings you back
  to the address it has now.
- **Admin page addresses open only when typed exactly as linked (#4801).**
  Another spelling of an admin page's address now shows Page not found.
- **The Internet Banking settings back link now says Xero Setup (#4863).**
  That link already opened Xero Setup. The words now say Xero Setup instead
  of Finance Setup. Nothing to decide or reconfigure.
- **Finance admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4802).**
  Payments, Internet Banking, Refunds & Credits, Subscriptions, Reports, Xero
  Sync, Xero Member Grouping, a Xero record and Xero Setup now live under
  Finance. The menu, bookmarks, emails and other links still use today's
  addresses, and opening the new Finance address for one of those pages brings
  you back to the address it has now. A member's page opened from Refunds &
  Credits or a Xero page now names that page in its back link as the menu
  does, such as "Xero Sync" or "Xero Setup" rather than "Xero".
- **Fees & booking rules admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4803).**
  Fees, Fee Configuration, Seasons, Age Groups, Promo Codes, Booking Policies
  and each of its policy pages, and Bookings Setup now live under Fees & booking
  rules. The menu, bookmarks and other links still use today's addresses, and
  opening the new Fees & booking rules address for one of those pages brings you
  back to the address it has now.
- **Help & system admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4804).**
  System Health, Issue Reports, Stuck States, Background Jobs, Email
  Deliverability, Audit Log, AI Diagnostics, the AI help assistant, Database
  Backups and Backup Setup now live under Help & system. The menu, bookmarks,
  alert emails and other links still use today's addresses, and opening the new
  Help & system address for one of those pages brings you back to the address it
  has now.
- **Messages & email admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4805).**
  Notifications & Email, Communications, Member Notices, the Message Board,
  Email Messages, Booking Messages, Delivery Rules and Recipients now live
  under Messages & email. The menu, bookmarks and other
  links still use today's addresses, and opening the new Messages & email
  address for one of those pages brings you back to the address it has now.
- **The menu and search use the same names as the Member notices, Delivery
  Rules and Recipients pages (#4878).** Member notices in the Members menu now
  matches the page heading, including the lower-case n. Search lists Delivery
  Rules and Recipients, the names already on those pages and on the
  Notifications & Email cards. Searching for Notification Rules or Notification
  Recipients still finds them. The help title on Member notices matches the
  page. Those cards and the back links read the same names, so renaming one
  updates the rest.
- **Running Reports over several years no longer freezes the booking site
  (#4937).** **Admin → Finance → Reports** worked out each night's occupancy by
  re-reading every booking once per night, on the same server thread that
  serves members, so a five-year range could stall everyone's pages for a few
  seconds. It now reads the bookings once for the whole range, and the figures
  are unchanged.

  Reports now cover at most 732 days (about two years). A longer From/To range
  shows a message naming that limit in place of the figures; run one report
  per year or two and combine the exports.
- **Admin controls now work from the keyboard (#4970).** Audit entries have
  named expand buttons, calendar booking bars are links, and Image Manager
  folders can be selected with Enter or Space. Folder actions appear on keyboard
  focus and stay visible on touch screens, with larger tap targets. Page content
  editors now announce their name, multiline textbox role and read-only state.
- **Setup explains view-only access before an officer tries to make a change (#4971).** Officers without support edit access now see a view-only banner and disabled checklist, provider-test and completion buttons. Refresh and permitted setup links remain available.
- **One admin menu per role.** The admin sidebar's switcher now offers **Admin**, **Bookings**, **Membership**, **Content**, **Finance** and **Treasurer** menus, one for each role a person holds, worked out from that role's permission areas so club-made roles follow the same rule. A Full Admin sees **Admin** only, plus any other role they hold; other roles get no full-menu option. **Treasurer** is the **Finance** menu plus Subscriptions, Integrations and the refund and unpaid-stay queues. The sidebar no longer repeats the Member Dashboard and Admin Dashboard links from the top bar, and staff pages (`/admin` and `/finance`) leave Book and My Bookings out of the top bar. **Who's at the lodge** has left the top bar for everyone and is now a button under **Open Kiosk** on the dashboard's Lodge Kiosk card, and an Admin account that is not also a club member no longer sees **My Bookings**. The menus are display only - page access is unchanged.
- **Members admin pages still open at their current addresses (#4806).**
  Committee, Deletion Requests, Family Groups, Induction, Applications,
  Member Fields, Members, Cancellation Requests, Membership & Members,
  Membership Types and Subscription Lockout now live under Members. The menu,
  bookmarks and other links still use today's addresses, and opening the new
  Members address for one of those pages brings you back to the address it
  has now.
- **Screen readers can now tell the teacher and parent-helper fields apart on
  the school booking form (#4957).** Each adult row's First name, Last name and
  Email labels are now linked to their boxes, so a screen reader reads out
  which field it is on and clicking a label puts the cursor in its box. Each
  row is announced as "Adult 1", "Adult 2" and so on, and its Remove button as
  "Remove adult 2" rather than just "Remove". Nothing about what the form looks
  like or what it sends has changed.
- **Screen readers now announce what happened after a member or guest acts (#4949).** A declined or failed card, a wrong sign-in code, a refused password reset, and a failed request on the profile, booking, contact, booking-request reply, membership-cancellation, nomination and partner-invite screens now appear in an alert that is read aloud and takes focus, instead of a coloured box that some screen readers skipped. Confirmations such as a sent payment link, a recorded response or a sent message are read aloud too. The cancel booking flow keeps focus on each step's heading instead of dropping it to the top of the page, a confirmation or reply that replaces the button you pressed (a booking-request reply, a membership-cancellation or nomination confirmation, a card payment) takes keyboard focus instead of leaving it behind, a refusal that needs a hosting override moves focus to the override reason, and the reset-password fields say which one failed and why. Amounts and payment wording are unchanged; the only new text is screen-reader-only status lines.
- **Dialog buttons stay reachable on small screens and at high zoom (#4967).**
  Tall pop-up dialogs now scroll within the screen, so warnings and Confirm or
  Save buttons can be reached without changing device or zoom. The admin
  command palette keeps its search box on screen and scrolls its own list.
- **Admin lists now say when they could not load, instead of showing an empty
  list or $0.00 (#4961).** When the Payments, Subscriptions, Hut Leaders or
  Communications send-history list failed to load, the page showed its normal
  empty state - "No payments found", zero totals, "No hut leader assignments
  yet" - or kept the previous search's rows under the new filters. Both looked
  like a real answer.

  Each page now shows a clear error with the reason and a **Try again**
  button, clears the old rows and totals, and hides the summary figures until
  the list loads. On Payments, a filter the server refuses is also pointed out
  above the table, so it is visible without opening **More filters**. On Hut
  Leaders, a failed check of unassigned nights is said, rather than the
  warning simply not appearing, and while the assignments could not be loaded
  the confirm step says its overlap check is unavailable instead of showing no
  clash. Try again keeps keyboard focus on its button and announces that it is
  trying again.
- **Every admin "email the member?" dialog now has a Go back button.** The last
  step before cancelling a booking, approving or rejecting a request, reviewing
  an application, refunding an appeal and the other admin email choices offered
  only the two ways to go ahead; a **Go back** button now sits first in each
  footer and closes the dialog without acting. While a request is in flight every
  button is disabled and the dialog cannot be dismissed. Booking cancellation's
  choices now read **Cancel booking, no email** and **Cancel booking and email
  member**, and the refund-appeal approve dialog repeats the amount being
  refunded. All twelve dialogs share one component (#4966).
- **Website photo galleries no longer make visitors download every full-size
  photo (#4935).** A gallery used to send each visitor's browser the original
  of every photo in the folder, often several megabytes each, even for a small
  thumbnail.

  Image Manager now also saves smaller copies of each JPG, PNG or WebP photo
  you upload, and a folder gallery shows the copy that suits the visitor's
  screen. The full-screen viewer opens the largest copy. Your originals are
  kept, their links are unchanged, and the copies never appear in Image
  Manager: they are replaced, deleted and moved with their photo. GIF and AVIF
  files are shown as before. Uploaded images are also cached more efficiently,
  so a returning visitor's browser re-checks a photo instead of downloading it
  again.

  **Operators:** photos uploaded before this release have no copies until you
  run `pnpm run images:backfill-sizes --root <images folder> --apply` once. It
  is safe to repeat; see "Website-sized copies" in the
  [Image Manager guide](docs/guides/image-manager.md#website-sized-copies).
- **Every date typed into a form or filter must now be a real day.** About 45 date fields, across the lodge kiosk, admin reports, hut leaders, Xero activity filters, the audit log, membership changes, bed allocation, the bookings and payments lists, admin member records, family requests and the member profile, used to check only the `YYYY-MM-DD` shape, so a day that does not exist, such as 30 February, got through and later caused a server error or a search that silently matched nothing. These fields now refuse it straight away with a clear message; a date of birth says "Date of birth must be a real date as YYYY-MM-DD". (ALP-574)
- **Action results are easier to find on Member Applications, Setup and Member merge (#4975).** Failed actions now bring the error into view and move keyboard focus to it, including after an application confirmation dialog closes. Screen readers announce errors and success messages; background refreshes leave focus in place.
- **Module changes update the admin menus after saving (#4974).** The sidebar,
  top menu and Search now reflect the saved modules without a browser reload.
  The Modules page's Refresh button reloads both the saved settings and menus.
- **A refused admin delete or remove now says why (#4976).** Deleting a family
  group, removing someone from a committee role, and deleting or switching a
  season on or off (on the Seasons page and in Hut Fees) now show the server's
  explanation, or a plain fallback, when the request is refused or the
  connection fails. Before, a refused family-group delete showed nothing, a
  committee remove spoke up only when the officer lacked permission, and a
  season refusal from the web server in front of the app showed a JSON parse
  error such as Unexpected token < instead of a reason. The family-group
  message appears above the list, where the officer is looking.
- **Officer queues now show every request, oldest waiting first (#4960).** Member applications, refund appeals, booking approvals, change requests, public requests, policy exceptions and the membership cancellation and archive queues each showed only the newest 25 rows, usually with no total and no way to reach the rest, so the requests that had waited longest were the ones out of sight. Each list now shows a total line such as "Showing 1–25 of 40", with previous and next arrows and page numbers when there is more than one page. The waiting filter of each queue lists the oldest request first; decided and **All** filters still list the newest first. Changing the filter returns to page 1, the page is kept in the address (except on the policy exceptions tab, whose filter is not in the address either) so a reload or a shared link opens the same page, and a link to one booking or request (from an email or **Needs Attention**) shows that record pinned above the list when it is on another page. What approving or rejecting does, and who can see each queue, is unchanged.
- **Member screens now have their own tab title and a real main heading, so
  screen-reader users can tell tabs apart and jump to the page's heading
  (#4951).** The payment link, reset and change password, verify email, confirm
  email change, email sign-in link, family invite, membership cancellation,
  lodge maintenance report, nomination, notice, school attendee confirmation,
  guest consent and booking-request screens now expose one level-1 heading in
  every state (loading, invalid link, success, error). Those screens, plus
  login, dashboard, my bookings and a single booking, get a fixed tab title
  such as `Reset your password | <Club>`, never a name, amount or token. The
  cards on the dashboard and on a single booking sit under that heading as
  level-2 headings. A census test stops a card title under the member-facing
  pages, or in the member cards it lists, from leaving its heading level
  unclassified, and holds the other titles (admin, finance and the member
  components shared across page types) at a falling baseline (`INV-PUB-006`).
  Nothing looks different, except that an H1 an admin puts inside a notice now
  renders as a level-2 heading, so a notice keeps one main heading.
- **Setup shortcuts open the right Xero and lodge settings (#4972).** Xero
  Mappings now opens the account mapping step in Xero Setup, guiding clubs
  through any unfinished prerequisites first. The bed board's no-active-lodge
  warning now links to Lodges, where lodges can be added or reactivated.
- **Clubs can choose their conditions report and booking timings (#4932).**
  The generic ski-field widget and Whakapapa (Mt Ruapehu) report now have separate
  module switches. New installs start with the Whakapapa report off; existing
  commissioned installs retain their choice. Data and finance downloads use the
  club’s short name. Booking Policies → Cancellation lets officers set the
  arrival reminder lead, first extra-payment reminder delay and exception hold
  length from 1–30 days, keeping defaults of 3, 3 and 7. Existing exception
  requests keep their original deadlines.
- **The Booking Requests tabs no longer spill out of their grey strip on a
  phone (#5124).** At phone width the four tabs wrap onto two rows. The second
  row (Policy Exceptions, Public Requests) used to hang out of the bottom of the
  grey tab strip and run into the filter buttons below it. The strip now grows
  to hold both rows. Display only; nothing about the queues changes.
- **Admin hub cards now use the page names that admin search shows (#5128).**
  On the Lobby Display hub the cards read **Display Devices**, **Display
  Builder**, **Display Layouts**, **Display Templates** and **Display
  Reference** (they were Devices, Visual builder, Layouts (Advanced), Templates
  and Reference); on Integrations, **Google Sign-in Setup**, **Backup Setup**,
  **Video Meetings Setup** and **Alpine Central Server Setup**; on Bookings
  Setup, **Seasons** (was Hut Fees & Seasons), whose card now says that nightly
  rates are set under Fees. Each title is read from the admin page registry,
  where the command palette also gets its page names, and a test fails any hub
  card that opens a whole page under another name. Addresses and permissions
  are unchanged.
- **More admin screens say why a save or delete was refused (#4976).** Saving a
  season on **Seasons** or **Fees → Hut Fees**, creating a family group, and
  deleting a work party event used to show "Unexpected token < in JSON", or
  nothing at all, when the server or the web server in front of it answered
  with an error page. They now show the server's own reason when it gave one,
  and a plain "Failed to save" style message when it did not or the
  connection dropped. On **Work Parties** and **Family Groups** the message is
  also announced to a screen reader.
- **Setup wizards announce a failed action every time it happens (#4975).** In the **Stripe**, **Google** and **Xero** setup wizards, **Site style**, the lodge setup wizard, the lodge download that follows saving the Alpine server API key, and the Disconnect button on the **Xero Sync** page, a failed save, verify, upload, disconnect or download now moves keyboard focus to its error and is read out by screen readers. It does so again when the same failure repeats word for word, where before a repeat could pass silently. Errors found when a page loads, such as a failed connection-status read, still show without moving focus.

  Two things are unchanged. On the Alpine server page, the Save, Save key, Enable or Disable, Upload and Download buttons still show a failure without moving focus. In the lodge setup wizard, a season or chore copy where only some rows are refused still lists those rows in its summary.
- **A failed Xero action now moves you to its explanation, every time (#4975).** On **Admin → Finance → Xero** and **Xero member grouping**, any button you press that fails now shows its message where you can see it and moves the screen and keyboard focus to it: a retry, replay, resolve, sync, contact creation, link repair, family-group creation, mode or rule change, dry run, duplicate scan, disconnect, **Refresh**, or **Refresh from Xero**. Pressing the same button again and getting the same failure brings you back to the message. The message sits just above its card, so it shows even while the card is collapsed, and collapsing and re-opening the card does not pull you back to an old failure. A successful **Refresh** clears the last failure. A list or status that the screen loads by itself, on opening or when you change a filter or page, still shows a quiet notice and leaves focus where it was.
- **Admin lists share one range line, and pending deletion requests list the oldest first (#4960 follow-up).** The payments, subscriptions, waitlist, audit log and its timeline, Xero inbound events and operations, and promo redemption lists now word the rows shown the same way, such as "Showing 1–25 of 40" (the audit log and timeline read "1-25 of 40" before, and the others used a hyphen). The bookings list now reads the same way where it said "Page 2 of 5 · 101 bookings", and so does the members list where it said "Page 2 of 5". A link to a page past the last row reads "Showing 0 of 40" instead of a range that names a row the page does not hold. The audit timeline is also the member's own Account Activity on the profile page, so members see the same wording there. The payments, subscriptions and bookings toolbars now show just the count ("40 payments", "101 bookings found"), so a page has one "Showing" line. Both deletion-request queues now page with the same Previous page and Next page chevron buttons as the other officer queues, with the same line even when a queue is empty ("Showing 0 of 0"). Their **Pending** filter lists the request that has waited longest first; the other filters still list the newest first. The same rows are listed, in the order stated above.
- **Chores, Lockers and Lodges: a failed action now takes you to its explanation.** When saving, deleting, deactivating or bulk-creating on these admin pages failed, the message used to appear in a plain box elsewhere on the page and nothing moved, so a keyboard or screen-reader user stayed on the button with no sign it had failed. The failure now appears in an announced alert that takes focus, and takes it again if the same failure repeats. A failed list load still shows quietly, without taking focus, and a failed deactivation no longer hides the lodge list. Saving a chore or a lodge edit, which closes the form, now brings you back to the top of the page.
- **The admin booking calendar now colours each booking status the same way as My Bookings, the dashboards and the booking editor.**
  The calendar kept its own status colours, which disagreed with those pages: Pending, Payment Pending and Bumped bookings all shared one amber, and Completed and Waitlisted bookings looked identical. The calendar's filter pills, booking bars and legend now take the same colour for each status as those pages do, so every status on the calendar has its own colour. The status chips in the bookings list are unchanged, and so are all labels.
- **The Whakapapa conditions panel on the weather page now matches the rest of
  the site.** The live Mt Ruapehu report gains an at-a-glance summary row - road
  status, lifts open, snow base, and the last 24 hours of snowfall - above the
  detail, a "Mt Ruapehu" eyebrow and a "Live" indicator in the header, and clear
  section grouping. Every element carries a stable `wcx-*` class so the exact
  look (card lift, accent keyline, heading treatment, table polish) is applied
